Build guide · US 325i Touring, manual · home garage with welding

E46 M3 Touring Conversion

A build plan for turning a US-market BMW E46 325i Touring (rear-wheel drive, manual) into the E46 M3 Touring that BMW built once, in 2000, and never sold. It follows the recipe most serious conversions use: one whole M3 donor supplies the S54 engine, six-speed gearbox, axle parts, steering, brakes and front panels, and you weld M3 rear-arch steel into the wagon body.

It is written for a home garage with a welder, and it links its sources inline: build threads, finished cars, vendor instructions, BMW documents and videos. It grew in four rounds of research. The first draft came from search-engine extracts. In October 2026 a verification pass re-read the linked pages and checked part numbers against BMW's parts catalog (ETK). A third round then filled in the wiring, fuel-pump control, torque values, Touring subframe work, arch steel and coding, and two skeptic reviews checked that every fact fits these two cars and that each phase can be followed and checked. A fourth round, later in October 2026, covered coding, body and chassis: body-module and powertrain coding, the rear arches, the trunk floor and exhaust, suspension for the Touring's weight, the front axle and brakes, the fuel system, and cooling and A/C. Two more studies worked out what changes if your Touring turns out to be a 325xi, and a gap-filling pass went back to BMW's repair manual (TIS), BMW's coding data, the parts catalog, dealer listings and build threads for what that round had left open. A few sites blocked these checks; claims that rest only on them, or only on a search engine's summary, are marked "(unverified)". Confirm every part number, pinout and torque value for your VIN on RealOEM and in BMW's repair and wiring documentation before you order, cut, re-pin or tighten anything.

Pin tables, continuity checks and button-by-button coding sessions are in the companion Wiring and coding manual. The Calculators page works out gearing, tire-size changes, wheel fitment and tire loads.

Your car
2001–05 US 325iT, 5-speed manual, rear-wheel drive (this build's is a 2003)
Target
S54 engine, Getrag 420G six-speed, M3 axles, steering and brakes, M3 front end, welded M3 rear arches and trunk floor
Donor
One whole E46 M3 with a manual gearbox, same model year as your car or newer
Budget
About $26k–$73k on top of your car, doing the labor yourself, including tools and a 10–15% contingency. New BMW arch steel instead of the donor's adds about $4,460
Time
18–30 months of evenings and weekends
Registered in
Massachusetts: safety inspection only for a 2001–05 car, but anti-tampering and title rules still apply (Massachusetts)
Hardest jobs
Rear arches, immobilizer and coding, and welding the M3 trunk floor in where the spare-wheel well was

Overview

What you are building

BMW M built one working E46 M3 Touring in 2000 as an in-house feasibility study: S54 engine, six-speed manual, rear-wheel drive, Chrome Shadow metallic paint. It came down the normal Touring assembly line and then needed "only minimal manual follow-up work" to fit its M parts (BimmerFile). BMW kept it secret until the M3's 30th-anniversary "M3 Week" in September 2016. BMW's own account gives no reason it wasn't built; it says only that, unlike the E36-based M3 Compact prototype shown to journalists, "the M3 Touring served entirely in-house purposes" (BMWBlog). Later press accounts say M3 customers weren't keen (evo).

Jakob Polschak, then head of prototype building at BMW M, named the hard part: "One important thing we needed to demonstrate was that the rear doors of the standard production model could be reworked to adapt them to the rear wheel arches without the need for new and expensive tools" (BimmerFile). BMW kept the flare off the door skins: it "decided against melding the rear wheel-arch sculpting into the door", and Petroyle's cars keep standard rear doors for that reason (Autocar). Where the arch meets the rear door is still the trickiest junction on any conversion.

One finished conversion was bid to $59,250 on Bring a Trailer without meeting its reserve (Bring a Trailer, Aug 2024); another sold for $65,000 (Built for Backroads, Sept 2025; an all-wheel-drive car with more than $70,000 in it). A UK firm, Petroyle, plans 50 cars from £130,000 (PistonHeads).

The recipe

Documented builds follow the same pattern.

  1. Buy one whole M3 donor. Engine, gearbox, axle parts, brakes, modules and body panels arrive together and match, usually for less than buying them separately. A cheap convertible serves as well as a coupe; see Choose the donor.
  2. Move the running gear as assemblies: the S54 with its 420G gearbox, the M3 front suspension and steering, and the rear axle with the M differential. The M3 rear axle bolts to the same four body points; one shop found "the bolts are the same" (Tenza Motorsports – Supplying the S54 wagon with an M3 rear end (2021), 15:00). One UK builder dropped the donor's front subframe with the engine still on it (PistonHeads).
  3. Keep your Touring's body, interior, body wiring, EWS and keys. An experienced builder told a first-timer: "You're better off keeping the Touring loom and modifying it… The difference in the two looms is just too big" (PistonHeads). The one build we found that fitted the M3's body loom had to move the Touring-only circuits (rear doors, opening rear glass, rear wiper and washer) into it (PistonHeads).
  4. Fit the M3 fuel system. The S54 runs at 5 bar through the M3 filter-regulator, the M3 lines and the short M3 pipe set that joins them to the pump. Move the donor's whole in-tank set into your tank: pump, baffle, jet pump and left sender, BMW's own combination, which owners have fitted to non-M tanks, the same part as yours (e46fanatics). Or fit the donor's whole tank, as several Touring builds did (ThaChileanDude – Building an e46 m3 Wagon in 10 days (2024), 17:00, Calvin's Car Diary – What happened to my £200K E46 M3 Touring project (2025), 30:20, PistonHeads). Keeping your own pump is the fallback, and it needs an adapter nobody has documented. The pump's wiring stays as it is. See Fuel system and Fuel-pump control.
  5. Make the electronics agree. The M3 engine harness and engine computer (DME) go in, with a few body-side wires moved. A vendor flashes the DME so it no longer needs the immobilizer handshake and writes your VIN into it. The M3 cluster gets a fresh memory chip carrying your VIN and then reads your true mileage from the light module. Keeping your Touring's own stability-control (DSC) unit is the documented route, and the steering-angle sensor is calibrated after the alignment. See Electronics and coding.
  6. Do the metalwork. Reinforce the rear subframe mounts and add the V-brace mounts a non-M body lacks, weld in an M3 trunk floor so the M3 muffler fits (new from BMW, or the donor's), weld M3 arch steel into the rear quarters (the donor's, or new BMW panels), and graft on the M3 front end. Reshaping the rear doors is optional.

Why your car is a good start

  • Rear-wheel drive. BMW's catalog lists one front subframe (front axle support 31111096902) for every rear-drive E46, M3 included; only the xi has its own (ETK). Keeping all-wheel drive behind an S54 has needed the xi's own oil pan (the "330xi pan" is the same part, 11137519432) reworked around a single-stage M50-family pump, plus the 330xi six-speed and X3 differentials (ETK, BimmerLife). On FCP Euro's S54 xi Touring the pump chain ground into that pan and wrecked the bottom end: "spun bearings, cracked rods, and a damaged crankshaft" (FCP Euro, part 1). Even converting an xi to rear drive adds the M3 front axle, an adapted gearbox crossmember and a complete MK60 (325xi: rear drive or all-wheel drive). You skip all of that.
  • Already a manual. The pedal box, clutch master cylinder and clutch switch are in place, including the US (and Japan) wire that stops the car cranking unless the clutch is down (clutch switch wiring). BMW lists the same clutch master cylinder, slave cylinder and flex hose for your car and the M3. An automatic Touring would also need the manual pedals, a clutch line, the brake reservoir's sealed clutch outlet opened up and the gearbox section of the harness re-pinned; that last job caused one build's no-start (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to drive my E46 M3 Touring for the first time (2026), 1:16:20, Tenza Motorsports – 5 things they don't tell you about S54 swaps (2021), 07:20).
  • Same platform. The S54 swap into non-M E46s is well documented. After fitting a 2004 S54 to a 2000 323i, an MS42 car, one owner wrote: "I only had to re-pin the X60004 connector on few places, everything else is just plug and play" (e46fanatics); an MS43 Touring also moves wires out of the E-box plug X6011, and an MS45.1 Touring adds wires to the cluster (Harness and re-pinning). Owners have bolted complete M3 rear subframes into non-M cars (e46zone). Small differences still catch people out: sensors that move to the other side of the engine bay, wheel-speed sensor plugs, the Sport button. The Parts list flags each one.
  • Same floor and inner arches. BMW lists the same rear axle carrier panel (41117000246) and trunk floor for the US 325i Touring and sedan, so sedan-pattern reinforcement plates should fit (ETK: panel, ETK: Touring floor, ETK: sedan floor). The inner half of the rear wheelhouse (41148231757/758) is the same part on your Touring and the M3 (ETK).
  • A sound shell saves the most time. On the UK builds, rust repair rather than the swap set the pace: Redish Motorsport called cutting out rust "the lengthiest process of this build" (Autoalex Cars – How to build an E46 M3 Touring, part 3 (2023), 20:00).

If your car is a 325xi

The owner once called this car a "325x", so decode the VIN before anything else (how to tell an xi). A 325xi is all-wheel drive, and that changes the front half of the plan. BMW gave it its own front frame rails, strut towers and widened tunnel, its own front subframe and steering joint, a transfer case, an oil pan with a tube through it for the right front shaft, and a Bosch DSC 5.7 in place of the Teves MK60 this guide keeps (BMW ST040, ETK). Behind the front seats it's a 325i Touring, so the floor, arches, rear-axle mounts and fuel system follow the guide.

You have two routes:

  • Convert it to rear drive: our recommendation. Hard but feasible. Fit the donor's whole front axle, the M3 lower steering joint with its flexible coupling, the M3 gearbox crossmember on an adapter and the complete MK60 system, for about $0–$1,500 more in parts with a donor built from 09/2002 ($1,000–$3,000 with an earlier one) and 4–8 more weekends (our estimate).
  • Keep all-wheel drive only if all-wheel drive is the point. Very hard: it needs an oil system BMW never made, the 330xi six-speed and a matched pair of differentials, and one of the two US cars that did it wrecked its S54's bottom end through the oil system.

Both routes, with parts, checks, coding and the documented xi builds, are in 325xi: rear drive or all-wheel drive.

How hard each job is

Job Difficulty Why
Engine and gearbox swap Moderate Same platform; heavy but bolt-in. One shop rated its S54 Touring swap about 7.5 out of 10, mostly for the labor (Tenza Motorsports – Building an E46 M3 wagon is far more complicated (2021), 01:40)
Front and rear axle transplant Moderate Mostly bolt-on M3 parts
S54 refresh (rod bearings, VANOS, valves) Moderate to hard Precise work, special tools, a clean bench. Plan 3–7 days for a first rod-bearing job (Paul Vo – Rod bearing installation and torque procedure (2017), description)
DSC and brakes Moderate Keeping your Touring's DSC unit is the documented route. One S54 Touring has run an M3 MK60 with M Track since 2022, but its owner hasn't published how it was coded (NAM3, NAM3 – Black & Tan 332iT #185)
Fuel system Moderate Moving the donor's in-tank set into your tank and fitting the M3 pipe set, lines and filter-regulator, then pressure and delivery tests with the pump on a bypass (Test the fuel system)
Cooling and A/C Moderate; the A/C service is a shop job The M3 radiator, fans and oil cooler bolt to your radiator supports, but the expansion tank needs the M3's brackets welded on or copied with rivnuts, the fan plug X82 has to reach the M3's pusher fan, and the bleed needs the ignition on. A certified shop recovers and recharges the A/C (Cooling and oil cooler, Air conditioning)
Rear subframe mount reinforcement Hard Welding plate to a thin floor, much of it overhead. BimmerWorld recommends an experienced, professional shop (BimmerWorld); one builder who did it himself concluded "take it to a shop" (Tracks and Trails – Fixing the weakest part of my E46 Touring (2025), 13:20)
Electronics and coding Hard Re-pinning connectors, the immobilizer (usually bought as a service), cluster EEPROM work, DSC coding
Floor and exhaust Hard Drilling out the spare-wheel well and plug-welding the M3 trunk floor in at every factory spot weld, plus the V-brace mounts and two M3 muffler brackets; the stock M3 exhaust then bolts up
Front fenders Hard to graft; moderate with carbon Touring fenders Carbon fenders took a few hours of fiddling per side on one build and two days of front-end alignment on another (Tracks and Trails – What it really takes to build an E46 M3 Touring (2026), 04:00, M3projekts – Ep4, front-end alignment (2023), 01:00)
Rear arches Very hard Panel grafting, inner arches, filler work; the inner wheelhouse joint and the door junction took the most time on camera (M346 Projects – Pt 14, M3 body work (2024), 27:20)
Paint Shop job for most A full respray is normal after this much metalwork; one paint shop kept the car four months (M346 Projects – Pt 25, paint reveal (2025), 00:00)

Decide these before you spend money

Decision Options This guide's default Details
Donor Coupe or convertible; manual or SMG; build date; Competition package A running manual car, same model year as your Touring or newer; built from 09/2002 if you want the option of using its DSC Choose the donor
A 325xi's drive Convert it to rear drive with the donor's front axle, the M3 lower steering joint, the M3 gearbox crossmember on an adapter and a complete MK60 system; or keep all-wheel drive with the 330xi six-speed, a matched pair of diffs and your xi oil pan reworked around another pump Convert to rear drive, with a donor built from 09/2002 of your xi's model year or newer 325xi: rear drive or all-wheel drive
DSC and brakes Keep your Touring's MK60 DSC unit, booster and master cylinder; or fit the donor's MK60 with its master cylinder Keep your Touring's. One S54 Touring cleared its DSC light only by refitting its own 325i unit, though its M3 unit got only a blank coding file and a PA-Soft reset (e46fanatics); another has run an M3 MK60 since 2022, with its coding unpublished (NAM3). An M3 MK60 codes only from a session vehicle order with an M3 type key and a date of 09/2002 or later, then needs INPA's initialisation (manual) DSC, brakes and steering angle
Immobilizer EWS-delete flash of the donor DME with your VIN written in; a DME a vendor has virginized, synced to your EWS, since a used DME keeps its first car's code table for good (BMW ST051); or the donor's EWS and keys Delete plus VIN, bought as a service, unless your state checks DME software: California's Smog Check fails modified software (BAR) Immobilizer (EWS), Registration and legal
Cluster M3 cluster on a new EEPROM chip carrying your VIN, done yourself or by a cluster service Either; the cluster then reads your true mileage from the light module. It keeps the donor's vehicle order for good, because BMW's coding data accepts an M3 cluster only with an M3 order; your light module holds your car's (BMW coding data) Instrument cluster and mileage
Fuel The donor's in-tank set in your tank, the donor's whole tank, or your own pump if it passes the 5-bar delivery test with margin; pump wiring unchanged or the M3 pump module The donor's in-tank set (pump, baffle, jet pump and left sender) in your tank, with the M3 pipe set, lines and filter-regulator; pump wiring unchanged Fuel system, Fuel-pump control
Front fenders Graft genuine M3 fenders onto the rear strips of your 4-door fenders, or buy carbon Touring fenders Your choice Front end on a 4-door body
Rear-arch steel The donor's quarters, coupe or convertible; or new BMW M3 convertible quarters (41357894541/542) with their inner lateral trim panels (41217894553/554), about $2,230 per side at one US dealer (October 2026), so no donor steel goes into your body Ask the RMV Title Division first. If grafting donor steel would bring a "reconstructed" title, or the donor's arches are rotten, buy new; otherwise use the donor's. Check one new inner panel against an M3 skin before you rely on its flange Rear arches and doors, Massachusetts
Rear doors Leave them standard and blend the flare in before the shut line, as BMW did; flare the door's trailing edge; or carry the flare across and re-cut the gap. At the shut line the M3 surface stands about 11–20 mm proud of the stock door (our estimate) Standard doors: BMW's way, with no door metalwork and the factory gaps kept Rear doors
Floor and exhaust Fit a new BMW M3 trunk floor; graft the donor's M3 floor; weld in a flat panel, or bond in a carbon M3-shape floor as one S54 Touring did (NAM3 – Black & Tan 332iT #724 (2026)); or keep the spare-wheel well and fit a muffler in the Touring's position, such as a US E36 M3 muffler, giving up the M3's rear-muffler layout (e46fanatics, NAM3 – Kaiv's first S54 Touring #14) A new BMW M3 floor (41127895619) with its front reinforcement (51717894229), $763.61 and $88.22 at BMWPartsDeal (October 2026): new steel that mates with the same rails, and no donor body steel for Massachusetts' "reconstructed" title question. The donor's floor is the fallback Exhaust and the spare-wheel well
Springs, dampers and wheels M3 struts and dampers with a stiffer rear spring, or M3-fitment coilovers; 18-inch Style 67 or 19-inch wheels M3 coupe struts and springs in front; at the rear, M3 dampers with springs about 7–9% stiffer than an M3 coupe's (our estimate), or M3 coilovers with a stiffer rear spring. Choose before the arch mock-up: moved-over M3 coupe springs sat one Touring low enough to rub (Tenza Motorsports – ECS coilover install (2022), 00:40) Suspension for Touring weight, Wheels, track and offsets
Cooling and A/C Your plain heater valve with the CSL's hose, or the M3's pump valve wired and coded; the M3's viscous and pusher fans, or a single electric fan; your A/C lines with the donor's pressure hose Your plain valve with hose 64212282548, no wiring. The M3 radiator, viscous fan and pusher fan, as BMW fitted them, with your fan plug X82 reaching the pusher; the pusher needs the M3 bumper's ducting. Keep your condenser and lines, fit the donor's pressure hose 64536902681, and keep the M54's old compressor until the A/C is charged: BMW sets the new oil by what it held Cooling and oil cooler, Air conditioning
Shop or DIY Reinforcement welding, paint, A/C, alignment, DME flash, cluster, exhaust Decide now: shop lead times set your calendar Shop briefs

Documented builds compared

This table lists the E46 Tourings we found that were converted to M3 specification and documented well enough to compare, with BMW's own 2000 prototype first as the reference. Rows are grouped by how far each build went (full M3 body, body only, or an S54 swap that kept the Touring body) and run oldest first; problems are noted in the column where they happened, and "not stated" means the sources don't say. DME is the engine computer, EWS the immobilizer and DSC the stability control; the Exhaust column also covers the trunk floor and rear bumper.

Other E46 S54 swaps worth learning from

These are sedans and coupes, not Tourings, but each one taught a wiring, coding, gearbox or fuel lesson that applies to your car.

Build Car Lesson Sources
ShopLifeTV, US, 2015–22 2001 330i sedan, automatic converted to six-speed, with a matched donor DME, EWS, key and cluster The EWS's clutch/park-neutral input stopped the first start. He coded the input off instead of wiring the clutch switch to the EWS, which removes a start interlock. His advice to "realign the LCM" to a donor cluster would change the car's recorded mileage. Check-engine and traction lights came back years later. First start (2015), 01:08, Parts (2016), 03:14, The end (2022), 05:19
Import Modify, US, 2018 328Ci race car (MS42) with an MSS54 bought with an EWS delete Two small E-box plugs differed (3-pin against 4-pin), so compare every plug before first start. The EWS-delete DME still needed the car's own EWS to accept the key. The same vendor flash removed emissions functions: decline those options. Ep.36 (2018), 01:05, Ep.41 (2018), 01:49, 12:23
DBO, US, 2019–21 2001 330Ci, manual, fitted with a complete M3 body harness The DM-TL plug had three wires on the 330Ci and four on the M3. The M3 brake booster's holes had to be slotted to fit the firewall. The crew guessed the fuel pressure at 4 bar; BMW sets the S54 at 5 bar (BMW ST041). Part 1 (2019), 08:44, 16:40, Part 2 (2020), 03:41
UNRIVALED, 2021 E46 sedan with an S54 from an SMG car, converted to manual A shop's coding left the SMG donor's DME in limp mode ("still thinks it's an SMG"): the DME software has to change, not just the coding. The M3 heater valve's auxiliary water pump needs its own wiring, or the cooling system is hard to bleed. UNRIVALED (2021), 02:02, 02:32
e46fanatics "S54 swap wiring information", 2013– A 2000 323i with a 2004 S54, and a 1998 323i with an MS43-type body harness A few re-pins in the DME's body connector were enough on these cars, an MS42 car and one rewired for an M54's MS43; an MS43 Touring also moves wires out of the E-box plug X6011, and an MS45.1 Touring adds wires to the cluster. The four-wire map posted there from memory came from an M54 swap (MS42 to MS43); on an MS43 Touring the same wires move the other way. Use the Wiring and coding manual. e46fanatics
Kalim (e46fanatics), 2011–18 Two sedans (MS43 and MS45.1), one a 2003 325i The M3 pump, baffle, left sender and lines went into the non-M tank, which BMW lists as the same part for the US 325i Touring. Swappers who left the pump on its stock relay found it ran, but a US DME stored a fuel-pump fault without lighting the check-engine lamp. p.1, p.38, ETK
nextelbuddy (NAM3), 2020 2003 330i ZHP sedan (MS45.1 body harness) with an S54 The oil-pressure lamp went out at ignition on, because the M3 routes the oil-pressure switch through the DME. One added wire from the DME connector to the cluster plus a cluster coding change fixed it; pins are in the Wiring and coding manual. NAM3

What the builds teach

  1. The arch-to-door junction is where builds differ most. BMW's prototype and Petroyle's cars stop the flare at the shut line and keep standard rear doors (Autocar), and JMCCRNA did the same "to follow the BMW prototype" (e46fanatics). Most others carried the flare onto the door: yavz's body shop bent the doors to shape (PistonHeads), SOS Customz hammered the edges out (SOS Customz – Building a BMW E46 M3 Touring Wagon (2023), 02:00), Calvin's body man welded a section in (Calvin's Car Diary – PT9 (2020), 02:20) and Tracks and Trails laid the flare over the door and re-cut the gap (Tracks and Trails – What It REALLY Takes to Build an E46 M3 Touring (2026), 15:40). Flaring the door after the quarter is on opens the shut gap by 3–4 mm, which M346 rebuilt with panel bond (M346 Projects – Pt 22 Rear door flare finishing (2025), 01:00), and the San Diego car's first quarters stopped short of the door and were redone (Bimmer INVASION – E46 M3 Wagon in San Diego (2023), 11:20). Either way, the front of the coupe flare sits wider than a four-door body and has to be dressed in (M346 Projects – Pt 14 M3 Body Work (2024), 28:20). See Rear arches and doors.
  2. No M3 front fender fits a four-door body. Everything else in the M3 front end fits, give or take a few brackets (M3projekts – Ep3 (2023), 08:00, 09:30), but the fender is longer and sits further out (Tracks and Trails – What It REALLY Takes to Build an E46 M3 Touring (2026), 02:20); one shop called the wings "the big headache" (PistonHeads). Builders grafted steel (SOS Customz – Building a BMW E46 M3 Touring Wagon (2023), 05:00, Calvin's Car Diary – PT9 (2020), 07:00) or bought M3Projekts' carbon Touring fenders, which still took two days to align on one car (M3projekts – Ep4 Frontend alignment (2023), 01:00) and hours of trim fitting on another (M346 Projects – Pt 18 M3 front end installed (2024), 08:00). A graft that stops the arch line short is shown on Calvin's second Touring (Calvin's Car Diary – PT5 (2020), 07:20). See Front end on a 4-door body.
  3. The rear underside gets rebuilt, not just cut. The M3 silencer won't clear the spare-wheel well, so every full-body build that shows its floor replaced it: with a new BMW M3 floor (Redish Motorsport – BMW M3 Touring build: Part 1 (2022), 04:40), the donor's floor (M346 Projects – Pt 14 M3 Body Work (2024), 00:40), part of an M3 panel (Tracks and Trails – I spent $10,000… rear end (2025), 01:20) or a carbon panel (Autocar). The Touring floor also lacks the M3 silencer's extra hangers (Redish Motorsport – BMW M3 Touring build: Part 1 (2022), 06:00, Tracks and Trails – rear end (2025), 03:20) and the V-brace mounting boxes (Tracks and Trails – rear end (2025), 06:00, Autoalex v2 – Building an E46 M3 Touring: Massive update (2024), 04:00). Three builds welded subframe plates, with the tank out (Autoalex Cars – Part 3 (2023), 15:20, Tracks and Trails – Fixing the weakest part… (2025), 09:00, PistonHeads); M346 bonded his, and nobody has compared the two (M346 Projects – Pt 14 M3 Body Work (2024), 23:00). Parts of one kit wouldn't fit Calvin's Touring, which has no rear-seat bulkhead (Calvin's Car Diary – PT15 (2025), 30:00). The builds that kept the well ran a non-M, ZHP or US E36 M3 muffler instead (Tenza Motorsports – Mixed exhaust (2021), 00:40, Project BMW – This S54 swap wagon pulls hard (2021), 04:00, NAM3 – Kaiv's first S54 Touring #14, NAM3 – Black & Tan 332iT #25), and one of them later bonded in a carbon M3-shape floor (NAM3 – Black & Tan 332iT #724 (2026)). See Exhaust and the spare-wheel well and Rear subframe mount reinforcement.
  4. The builds that bought an EWS delete started; the ones that tried to sync struggled. Tracks and Trails sent his DME file away for a delete (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to Drive my BMW E46 M3 Touring for the First Time (2026), 1:12:40), and Tenza bought a Kassel DME with the delete, the wagon's VIN and a matching cluster for about $1,000 (Tenza Motorsports – M3 touring build finally runs! (2021), 02:00, Tenza Motorsports – 5 things they don't tell you, part 2 (2021), 06:07). After a delete, the car's own EWS still checks the key and releases the starter (BMW ST051, Import Modify – Ep.41 S54 Swap, First Start! (2018), 12:23). Two S54 Tourings that tried to sync a used or virginized DME to their own EWS couldn't: one moved to the donor's EWS and key and still didn't start (e46fanatics); the other had been running on two keys, the M3's at the antenna and its own in the lock, and its thread ends unresolved (e46fanatics). Keep the clutch switch wired to the EWS, as Tracks and Trails and ThaChileanDude did (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to Drive… (2026), 08:40, ThaChileanDude – Building an e46 m3 Wagon in 10 days (2024), 19:56). See Immobilizer (EWS).
  5. The M3 tank or pump went in without reported trouble; the regulator and lines are what caught builders out. M3 tanks went into five of the Tourings above (PistonHeads, Tenza Motorsports – Total build cost (2022), 05:00, ThaChileanDude – Building an e46 m3 Wagon in 10 days (2024), 17:00, Calvin's Car Diary – PT15 (2025), 30:20, NAM3), and Tracks and Trails put the M3 pump into his Touring's tank (Tracks and Trails – rear end (2025), 27:20). His car then wouldn't start until he fitted the M3 filter-regulator (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to Drive… (2026), 1:14:00); M346's regulator leaked at first start (M346 Projects – Pt 13 Engine Start! (2024), 05:40); Project BMW found the 325's fuel and purge lines didn't suit the S54 (Project BMW – S54 Engine Swap Wagon RUNS (2021), 00:20). A US SULEV (M56) Touring has a sealed tank of its own, which Tenza replaced (Tenza Motorsports – No more SULEV! (2021), 00:20), so check your engine code before you plan, and check that changing a SULEV car's fuel system is legal where you live. See Fuel system.
  6. Wheel-speed sensors and the DSC unit can leave the ABS light on. M3s built before 09/2002 have an MK20 DSC with inductive sensors and gray plugs; your Touring and later M3s have the MK60's active sensors with blue plugs (BMW ST056). That likely explains why Tenza found the M3 and non-M wheel-speed sensor plugs wouldn't mate on its 2004 Touring with a 2002 donor; it fitted non-M sensors in the M3 hubs and saw an ABS light at the first start, standing and before the brakes were bled (Tenza Motorsports – 5 things they don't tell you, part 2 (2021), 03:20, Tenza Motorsports – M3 touring build finally runs! (2021), 07:20). Three months later, after less than half a mile of driving, the builder reported no problems (Tenza Motorsports – 5 things they don't tell you, part 2 (2021), 04:00). On a 2003 xi Touring the M3 sensors "plugged right in", but the xi's own Bosch sensors use the same blue housings, so that shows only that the plugs mate (e46fanatics, BMW ST056). Check your plugs before you order. One S54 wagon never cleared its DSC light with an M3 MK60 and went back to the 325i unit (e46fanatics). Bry5on's ran on both and has used the M3 unit, with M Track, since 2022 (NAM3, NAM3 – Black & Tan 332iT #185); three other builds above used the M3 unit (M3projekts – Ep5 S54 install (2023), 20:00, NAM3, e46fanatics), and Kaiv's first S54 Touring got one later (NAM3 #25). None of them has published its coding steps. ThaChileanDude's ABS light was still on after the swap (ThaChileanDude – Building an e46 m3 Wagon in 10 days (2024), 34:48). See DSC, brakes and steering angle.
  7. Small wiring differences caused the no-starts and the lights left on. Tracks and Trails' no-fuel no-start came from automatic-gearbox plugs that look the same but are wired differently (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to Drive… (2026), 1:16:20). A 2001 325iT lost its oil and battery lamps because the M3 harness routes them through the DME (e46fanatics); Tenza's driver's mirror and cruise control never worked (Tenza Motorsports – Total build cost (2022), 07:20); ThaChileanDude's tamper dot and check-engine light stayed on (ThaChileanDude – Building an e46 m3 Wagon in 10 days (2024), 35:19). The coolant-level and washer plugs move sides and had to be extended on several cars (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to Drive… (2026), 22:40, M3projekts – Ep5 S54 install (2023), 04:00, Tenza Motorsports – 5 things they don't tell you (2021), 00:40). For a US inspection, M346's "converted" DMEs never set their readiness monitors (M346 Projects – Pt 26 Final Wagon Reveal (2025), 43:20), while a swap builder who keeps stock US software apart from the EWS delete reports every monitor ready (e46fanatics). Three builds above run catless headers, which a US road car may not do. See Troubleshooting and Registration and legal (US).
  8. Rust and life, not the swap, set the schedule and the bill. Autoalex's donor lost its inner arches as soon as it was stripped, cutting out rust was "the lengthiest process", and the car took about three years, two engines and £70,000 (Autoalex Cars – Part 1 (2023), 07:40, Autoalex Cars – Part 3 (2023), 20:00, Autoalex Cars – It Took 3 Years And £70,000… (2025), 18:40). Calvin's car is still not running after seven years and more than £100,000 (Calvin's Car Diary – I have big news… (2026), 18:40), and Petroyle's donors often come with rotten boot floors (Hagerty – "New" BMW E46 M3 Touring (2026), 06:40). yavz's build stalled for years and E91M3's was sold off after three months (PistonHeads, PistonHeads). For scale, M346 started from a rust-free wagon and finished in 27 months of mostly DIY work (M346 Projects – Pt 1 (2023), 02:00, M346 Projects – Pt 26 Final Wagon Reveal (2025)), and SOS Customz did the metal and body in about 30 days with two full-time people (SOS Customz – Building a BMW E46 M3 Touring Wagon (2023), 26:00). See Plan and budget.

Plan and budget

Check your own Touring first

Before you buy a donor, make sure your Touring is the car this guide assumes. Most checks cost nothing; Phase 0 of the build records the results.

Check How What the answer means
Model and build date Decode the VIN: 325i or 325xi, build date, option codes An xi changes the plan (If your car is a 325xi). The build date sets the facelift front (from 09/2001), how modules are coded (ZCS before 09/2001, the vehicle order after) and which DME you have
Engine and tank Engine code on the block or in the VIN decode; look at the tank You want an M54B25 with a plastic tank. An M56 SULEV car has a CAN-controlled pump module, a sealed metal tank and no return line (ETK), so the fuel plan doesn't apply as written; one M56 Touring took the M3 tank, which changes a certified evaporative system, so ask your state first (Tenza Motorsports – No more SULEV (2021), 00:20, Registration and legal). BMW's 2002 bulletin introduced the M56 with automatics (BMW B11 75 02). Read one way, BMW's catalog lists a five-speed for the US 325i M56 Touring (ETK); read another, that gearbox sits in groups shared with other engines, and the only M56 gearbox-module harness it lists is for automatics (ETK), so a manual M56 is probably a conversion. Either way a manual isn't proof of an M54: check the engine code and the tank
DME Read the label in the E-box MS43 on cars built to 02/2003, MS45.1 from 03/2003 (ETK); forums and Kassel's chart call the second "MS45". No label? The MS45.1 has the leak-test heater wire in X60004 pin 2 and wires in pins 5 and 15; the MS43 has the heater wire in the E-box plug X6011. On a car built in 02 or 03/2003, check rather than assume; a 325xi should have an MS43 in every year, but read its label too (manual). It sets your re-pin list
DSC, not ASC only Label on the hydraulic unit, or the option list BMW also lists ASC-only units for US Tourings, and an ASC-only car has no steering-angle sensor (ETK); BMW's 2003 US spec sheet for the 325i Sport Wagon lists DSC (BMW USA). Cars built before 09/2001 also have an early MK60 with analog yaw sensors (e46fanatics)
Rear axle carrier panel (RACP) Clean and inspect all four subframe mounts top and bottom, the ends of the V-shaped beam and the rail-to-floor spot welds, using CMP's criteria (CMP, part 1, part 2) Cracks are repaired before plating. A torn panel is a body-shop job: BMW's 21 kg replacement (41117000246) is marked "This part is discontinued" at BMWPartsDeal (last price $1,304.68, October 2026), so ask a dealer whether a successor exists (BMWPartsDeal)
Rust Rear arch inner lips, sills and jacking points, around the tank and brake-pipe brackets, battery box, floor On one Touring Redish found the jacking points delaminating, corrosion behind the tank brackets and holes in the battery box (Autoalex Cars – Part 3 (2023), 03:00, 12:40)
Options Climate control (automatic IHKA or manual IHKR), DSC button or console switch center, xenon lights, front fogs and a rain/light sensor (together they set your light module's part number), steering-wheel buttons, mirror harness on facelift doors, cruise A/C is confirmed working with IHKA; nobody has confirmed IHKR (e46fanatics). Without front fogs, the M3 bumper's fog lights need a fog-variant light module, the fog button and relay K47; no coding turns them on (manual, BMW coding data). Facelift Touring doors have ribbon-cable mirror harnesses that M3 mirrors don't plug into (M346 Projects – Pt 21, M3 mirror retrofit (2024), 00:20)
Coding kit Build it and prove it on the unmodified car: INPA reads the cluster, light module and DSC, and NCS Expert reads the vehicle order (FA) or key code (ZCS) Fix the cable, port or software before taking any backup; Phase 0 then saves every module's coding and the cluster and light-module EEPROMs. See Factory documentation and coding kit

Choose the donor

Buy one complete, running E46 M3 with a manual gearbox. A running car lets you test the engine, gearbox and electronics before they come apart. The builder of two Hungarian conversions puts it simply: "Coupe or Cabrio/Vert doesn't really matter… better if she is mechanically fine" (M3projekts – Cheapest UK M3 donor, Ep7 (2023), description).

  • Model year: the same as your Touring or newer. EPA policy and state engine-change rules generally want the engine to be the same model year as the chassis or newer (see Registration and legal). A 2003 Touring can take an engine from a 2003–06 M3; a 2005 needs a 2005 or 2006. Choose a donor whose underhood emissions (VECI) label shows a US 50-state certification; in Massachusetts the emissions category matters too (see Massachusetts).
  • If your Touring is a 325xi, choose its route first. Converting it to rear drive takes the donor's whole MK60 system with its sensors, pipes and harness branch, so buy a donor built from 09/2002. Keeping all-wheel drive leaves the donor's 420G, front axle, MK60 and diff unused (325xi: rear drive or all-wheel drive).
  • Build date. Several parts change with production date:
Part Earlier cars Later cars What it means for you
Engine computer MSS54, to about 09/2003 MSS54HP, from about 09/2003 (NAM3) Either works. Keep the DME with its own engine harness, which also changes at 09/2003 (ETK)
DSC unit Teves MK20, to 09/2002: 43-pin plug and a separate pre-charge pump (ETK) MK60, from 09/2002 (Competition unit from 12/2004): the same 47-pin plug as your Touring's (ETK) Matters only if you'd use the donor's DSC. An MK20 won't plug into your harness. An M3 MK60 codes only from a session vehicle order with an M3 type key and a date of 09/2002 or later, then needs INPA's initialisation (manual, Session 5)
Master cylinder and booster 34312282343 and 34332282193, to 09/2002 34317838638 and 34332282622, from 09/2002 (ETK) Only for the donor-DSC route
Rod bolts M11 twelve-point, reused, on engines built up to 12/12–13/2002 M10 E-Torx, new every time, tightened in three cycles (BMW SI B11 04 04) Vendors and ETK give 02/2003 for the change; go by the bolt heads, not the date. Late engines need 12 new bolts
Instrument cluster Coding index 20–22 Redesign clusters, coding index 23–24, roughly 2003 on (e46fanatics) Prefer a redesign cluster: it properly supports the M Track light and brake-force display. For a Touring built from 09/2002, use a cluster from 09/2002 or later: ECUswap calls it compulsory ("zwangsweise") (ECUswap); a 2003–06 donor gives index 23 or 24. The cluster keeps the donor's vehicle order, since BMW's coding data accepts an index-23 or -24 cluster only with an M3 order (BMW coding data). The backlight wire also changed at 09/2002, so an older cluster in a later Touring needs a wire added, and a newer cluster in an older Touring a light-module update (e46fanatics)
Rear wheel-speed sensors Early type, to 09/2002 Later type, from 09/2002; your Touring changed at 09/2001 (ETK) You keep your own sensors: they suit the M3 hubs, and from 09/2002 the M3 uses the same parts (Brakes and DSC). A donor built before 09/2002 has the MK20's inductive sensors with gray plugs, which don't fit your harness; that likely explains why a 2004 Touring's plugs didn't mate with its 2002 donor's (Tenza Motorsports – 5 things they don't tell you, part 2 (2021), 03:20), while on a 2003 xi Touring, whose Bosch sensors use the same blue housings, the M3 sensors' plugs mated (e46fanatics)
Competition package (ZCP) — From 12/2004: a quicker rack (shared with the CSL), 345 × 28 mm front rotors and 19-inch Style 163 wheels (ETK: rack, ETK: rotor) Nice to have, not needed
  • Manual, not SMG. SMG cars cost less (one estimate says 20–30%, unverified), but you'd add the manual shift parts and clutch hydraulics an SMG car lacks, a manual gearbox-harness section (Redline) and manual DME software. The MSS54's hardware is the same for both gearboxes, but BMW released separate manual and SMG software, so an SMG donor's DME needs a reflash or a vendor's conversion, not just coding (NAM3, ECUWorx). One SMG-donor DME that a local shop "coded" stayed in limp mode (UNRIVALED – Watch this before you S54 swap your BMW (2021), 02:02). The PistonHeads Touring's builder converted an SMG donor.
  • Coupe or convertible. Convertibles usually cost less (see the price table below), and for this conversion they give up almost nothing:
    • BMW lists separate M3 convertible quarter panels (41357894541/542), but the arch is almost certainly the same pressing as the coupe's. Both cars have the same rear track, wheels and body width, and the same filler flap, bumper brackets and side skirts meet the flare (ETK: quarter, ETK: flap, BMW USA). BMW's own dimension drawings of the two M3s show the same arch opening within 2–9 mm and the same flare within 3–7 mm (our measurement from the drawings, an estimate) (M3 coupe drawing, M3 convertible drawing). Confirm it with section templates at seven stations before you cut (Datum, stations and templates).
    • A convertible quarter covers the whole outer skin from the door shut line to the tail light, the part a Touring needs; it lacks only the coupe's C-pillar. Its arch flange sits on the convertible's heavy inner side frame, so expect more spot welds to drill (ETK). It brings the same M3 trunk floor, front fenders, hood and bumper as a coupe.
    • One owner-built Touring used both quarter sections and the trunk floor from a 2003 M3 convertible (M346 Projects – Pt 1, M3 part out (2023), 06:40).
    • M3 convertible front seats don't fit a Touring (e46fanatics), and the convertible's front struts (31312282265/266) and springs are sized for a heavier nose, a front axle load of about 856 kg against the coupe's 779 kg: plan on coupe front springs or coilovers with a convertible donor. Its rear dampers (33522282267) were built for a rear load close to your Touring's (our inference), though aftermarket makers sell one damper for both M3s (ETK, Suspension for Touring weight).
  • Damage and rust you can accept. A bent shell is fine if the parts you need are intact: drivetrain, axle parts, front panels (hood, fenders, headlights, bumper), both rear arch areas and the trunk floor around the muffler. Rust is the bigger risk. E46 rear-arch rust starts at the inner arch, hidden under seam sealer (Redish), and Redish says M3 inner arches "are always rotten out" (Autoalex Cars – Part 3 (2023), 04:20), and Autoalex's cheap coupe donor lost its inner arch as soon as it was stripped (Autoalex Cars – Part 1 (2023), 07:40). That car revved cleanly, but its frame and subframes turned out to be "in seriously bad condition" (BMWBlog).
  • Paperwork. Get the title or salvage paperwork and a bill of sale, and photograph the VIN plates and engine number; your state may ask for proof of the engine's year.

Test it while it still runs. Some tests need the seller's agreement; do the rest before teardown.

Test How Record or look for
Drive it Fully warm; every gear; listen at warm idle A knock at idle; clean shifts into all six gears and reverse; diff clunk or whine. One 190,000-mile donor's gearbox later refused a gear on track (Autoalex Cars – It took 3 years and £70,000 (2025), 13:40)
Fault codes Scan every module with INPA and save the lists Stored faults in the DME, DSC, cluster, airbag and EWS
Module IDs Record each module's part number and software; read the DME's ID and its stored VIN slots (AIF) with Tool32 (ECUWorx); back up the cluster EEPROM with PA-Soft Unit types (MK20 or MK60, MSS54 or HP) and the cluster's coding index. Send the DME data with the DME if a vendor flashes it
Compression and leak-down Warm engine, all plugs out Compression of about 11–12 bar (160–174 psi) minimum, about the same on every cylinder: a figure from a forum compilation, so confirm it in TIS (Flow compilation, p.47). No leak-down figure turned up; judge how even the six cylinders are
VANOS Tool32 or INPA VANOS tests; listen for rattle; if allowed, take the valve cover off and look at the exhaust-hub tabs and the oil-pump disc (Beisan) VANOS faults, and the test readings to compare after the refresh (Phase 12); a cracked hub tab means a new hub
Fuel pressure Gauge on the threaded test fitting at the regulator, beside the filter under the left front floor (filter cover off); pump run through a bypass at its module's socket, terminals 30 and 87b (pins 6 and 2 of plug X10157, through a switch with a 15 A inline fuse), BMW's method (BMW ST041) 5.0 ± 0.2 bar; 20 minutes later no more than 0.5 bar (7 psi) lost and still 4.5 bar or more (Bentley, quoted on e46fanatics). It proves the pump, regulator and check valve you'll move
A/C Run it on max Cold air and a compressor that engages. Then have a shop recover the refrigerant before you open anything; venting it is prohibited (EPA)
DSC and ABS Warning lights at start; a careful hard stop on a quiet road Lights out, ABS working
Options fitted Look for headlight-washer nozzle covers in the bumper and a second pump on the washer bottle Headlight washers were an option on US M3s (BMW code 502), not standard (ETK)
Measurements On level ground, on BMW 18- or 19-inch wheels, in BMW's normal position: a full tank, two people of about 68 kg (150 lb) in the front seats and 14 kg (31 lb) in the middle of the trunk (TIS 32 00). At each corner: BMW's ride height (rim flange at the bottom middle to the arch's lower edge), the heights of the hub center, the arch lip and a body point both cars share, and how far the lip sits outboard of the tire (Measure and mock up before you cut). Photograph the spring paint marks, the label on each front strut, the B-pillar tire placard and the underhood A/C and emissions labels BMW's 605 mm front and 587 mm rear on 18-inch wheels (619 and 600 mm on 19s), ±10 mm with left and right within 10 mm, shows a stock stance (TIS 31 00, TIS 33 00). Your hub-to-body and hub-to-lip targets for the Phase 6 mock-up, and the A/C charge
Donor option Price seen Source
Running E46 M3 2005 coupes $37,275–$45,150 and 2005 convertibles $12,750–$31,500, in sales from Dec 2024 to Jan 2026 (from search extracts) Hagerty
Rough donors used for conversions $6,500 for a curbed 2002 M3 that needed a clutch (2021); £7,000 for an insurance-write-off convertible (UK, 2023); £9,250 for a rusty 190,000-mile coupe (UK, 2023). In Canada in 2025, manual M3s with over 400,000 km were asking more than CAD 20,000 Tenza Motorsports – S54 swap costs (2021), 01:00, M3projekts – Ep7 (2023), 01:00, Autoalex Cars – I bought a cheap E46 M3 (2023), 00:40, Tracks and Trails – Can I do it? (2025), 07:40
Salvage or wrecked M3 A salvage-title convertible already missing its rear end, about $4,500 (bought around 2018); a clean-title 2003 six-speed with salvage history, $7,100 (April 2019) autoevolution, e46fanatics
Used S54 with DME and harness, about 200k miles About $3,500 asking locally, $6,000 and up on eBay and Copart (June 2025). The same thread suggests a whole '03.5-on convertible donor for under $9–10k NAM3
Complete used M3 rear axle €1,650 (Germany, 2023) M539 Restorations – Project Cologne PT13 (2023), 00:40
Tip

An engine on its own is cheaper, but you would still need the M3 axle parts, steering, brakes, cluster, harness, fuel parts and body panels. Bought piece by piece, those usually cost more than a rough whole car.

Budget

These ranges assume you do the labor. Rows marked "estimate" are planning figures, not quotes. Vendor prices were checked in October 2026 unless a date is given; £ and € prices are as listed, before shipping and import costs.

Item Range (USD) Basis
Donor M3 $8,000–$20,000 Estimate; recent prices under Choose the donor. Add travel or transport: one build spent about $1,000 collecting its cars (Tenza Motorsports – Total build cost (2022), 01:40)
Rod-bearing parts $750–$1,100 BimmerWorld's OEM kits are $753.99 for engines built to 2/03 and $844.99 from 4/03, with new M10 bolts (BimmerWorld); upgraded bolts or coated bearings cost more (estimate). Shops charge $1,625 (EAS); Mr Vanos in the UK charges £1,995, including a new oil pump, ARP bolts and two engine mounts (Mr Vanos)
VANOS refresh $155–$1,135 Beisan's seal and rattle kit is $155 (Beisan); BimmerWorld's kit with a new exhaust hub is $979.99 without seals (BimmerWorld)
Other engine seals, gaskets, chain guide, shims $500–$1,500 Estimate
Clutch, dual-mass flywheel, pilot bearing, bolts $600–$1,800 Estimate
420G seals and gear-identification switch $100–$300 The switch is about $78 (NAM3); seals estimate
Axle refresh: subframe and diff mounts, RTABs, arms, end links $800–$2,000 Estimate
Brakes: pads, rotors, pad-wear sensors, M3 front hoses, booster grommet, DOT 4 brake fluid; parking-brake shoes if worn $600–$1,500 Estimate
Rear springs about 7–9% stiffer than an M3 coupe's, or M3 coilovers $1,200–$3,500 Estimate. The donor brings its struts and dampers; budget for new rear springs about 7–9% stiffer than an M3 coupe's (our estimate). BMW's M3 rear springs are about $75–$101 each at FCP Euro (October 2026), and no maker sells a kit for an M3-axle Touring (FCP Euro, Suspension for Touring weight)
Rear subframe reinforcement and V-brace mounts $250–$700 in parts The MSW kit is about $155–$160 (Morehead); Redish's plates were £180, plus £125 for six tank and brake-pipe brackets, in 2023 (Autoalex Cars – Part 3 (2023), 16:00); aftermarket V-brace boxes were "like a hundred bucks" in 2025 (Tracks and Trails – I spent $10,000 on my E46 Touring's rear end (2025), 07:40). Shop labor: $800–$1,200 quoted in 2019, about $2,200–$2,400 with bushings and an alignment (e46fanatics); one 2025 Canadian quote was CAD 2,500, against CAD 2,300 to do it yourself including a new welder (Tracks and Trails – Fixing the weakest part of my E46 Touring (2025), 13:20)
Trunk floor, muffler brackets and heat shield $0–$1,400 Recommended new parts at BMWPartsDeal, October 2026: floor 41127895619 $763.61, reinforcement 51717894229 $88.22, brackets 41122494844 $27.19 and 41112493931 $71.40, rear heat shield 51482494848 $259.12, together $1,209.54 plus shipping (floor); add $92.19 for a new M3 canister holder 16132229735 if the canister has to move and you didn't keep the donor's. $0 if you graft the donor's floor and brackets. The M3 exhaust comes with the donor; a new rear muffler 18107831783 is $5,093.16 at BMWPartsDeal (October 2026). One builder found a used CSL muffler for $400 in 2024 (M346 Projects – Pt 9, CSL muffler (2024), 02:40), but a CSL rear section was never US-certified
Fuel: a new M3 filter, seals and clamps; the donor's in-tank set, pipe set, lines, regulator housing and regulator (a new regulator only if the donor's fails its Phase 1 test) $250–$900 Estimate. If the donor's are missing or damaged, a new delivery unit is $559.16 and a new pipe set $159.88 at BMWPartsDeal, and a new baffle $123.62 at BimmerWorld (October 2026) (BMWPartsDeal, BimmerWorld)
Cooling: new expansion tank and holder, thermostat, vent screw, hoses and BMW antifreeze; the M3 radiator, oil cooler and both fans come with the donor $400–$900 Estimate (Cooling and oil cooler)
A/C: recovery on both cars, a new receiver-drier and O-rings, PAG oil, evacuation and charge; the donor's pressure hose $300–$700 Estimate (Air conditioning)
DME: EWS delete with your VIN written in (manual software if SMG) $100–$349, plus shipping Kassel charges $109 for the delete plus $20 for the VIN, or $349 for its engine-swap coding with every swap option (Kassel). DUDMD charges $215–$225 (DUDMD). RPM charges $300 (October 2026) (RPM). Severn charges $100–$200 depending on shipping, and its page says "off-road use only" (Severn). For the sync route, RPM's used-DME EWS programming is $300 (RPM)
Coding kit: laptop, K+DCAN cable, PA-Soft interface, 10 A charger; Standard Tools 2.12 with NCS Expert 4.0.1 $300–$800 Estimate; less if you own a suitable laptop. BMW doesn't sell the software to owners (Factory documentation and coding kit)
Cluster: new EEPROM done yourself, or a service $50–$400 Estimate. Huggins Racing lists a used-cluster VIN and mileage correction, which sets a used cluster to your car's true mileage, at $125 and its rear-door LED mod at $100 (October 2026) (Huggins, Huggins). One Touring build paid Kassel about $1,000 including shipping for the DME tune, EWS delete and cluster mileage together (2021, Tenza Motorsports – 5 things they don't tell you, part 2 (2021), 05:40)
Wiring: terminals, repair leads, depinning keys $100–$300 Estimate. Redline's plug-in E46 S54 swap harness is $265 and needs an EWS-deleted DME (Redline)
Body materials $500–$2,000 Estimate, using the donor's arch steel. New BMW arch steel adds about $4,460 for both sides (tip below)
Front fenders $0–$2,000 Grafting the donor's costs only materials; carbon Touring fenders are €1,400 before VAT (M3Projekts)
Paint (full respray) $6,000–$15,000 Estimate; varies widely by region and shop
Tires, alignment, fluids, hardware $1,500–$2,500 Estimate
Tools you don't own yet $1,000–$3,000 Estimate: welder, respirator and extraction, spot-weld cutters, test gauges and the fuel test kit, torque wrenches, engine stand (Tools and test equipment). One builder's MIG welder was about CAD 1,200 (Tracks and Trails – Fixing the weakest part of my E46 Touring (2025), 13:00)
Contingency 10–15% Estimate; every documented build met work it hadn't planned
Total About $26k–$73k Including contingency; before selling leftovers. New BMW arch steel adds about $4,460
Tip

If the donor's arch steel is rotten, or you'd rather keep donor steel out of your body, here is what new BMW steel costs (October 2026). At one US dealer the M3 convertible's rear side panels 41357894541/542 were $2,105.60 each (list $2,561.00) and its inner lateral trim panels 41217894553/554, which include the outer half of the wheelhouse, $127.54 and $118.80; the M3 coupe's side panels 41217890689/690 were $6,932.63 each and its interior side frames 41217890677/678 $1,311.70 each (BMWPartsDeal: 41357894541, 41217894553, 41217890689, 41217890677). That makes about $2,230 a side for new convertible steel and $8,240 a side for coupe steel, before freight and tax (our arithmetic). Each page said "Ships in 1-3 Business Days", but stock isn't confirmed until you order. That the convertible's inner panel carries the M3-width arch flange is our reading of BMW's diagram, so check one against an M3 skin first. New convertible steel for both arches plus the new trunk floor and its reinforcement comes to about $5,310 (our arithmetic), with no donor steel in your body (Massachusetts).

In Europe, eStore-Central lists the convertible quarter at €1,979.88 each and the inner panels at €141.50 and €131.82, about €4,280 for both sides plus an M3 filler flap (51172695524, €45.06), and the coupe quarter at €6,518.67 each (eStore-Central). R44, a UK shop that prices in pounds, lists the coupe quarters at £4,420 each (R44: left, right). BMW's inner arch panels have been £990 each since 2025 (Redish); we infer that is the M3 coupe's interior side frame 41217890677/678. LBL Panels' M3 arch sections are £225 standard or £375 for a full arch, in 1.2 mm steel (2026, unverified), but no current listing turned up in October 2026 (m3cutters). Redish has also used a fabricator's repair panels at "like 10%" of the price of a BMW side panel, which it put at "2,300 and something pounds" (Autoalex Cars – Part 3 (2023), 06:00).

Selling what you don't use (the M54, the 5-speed, the MS43 or MS45.1 DME, replaced 325i axle parts, donor interior and panels) can recover $2k–$5k (estimate). Hold back the fallback parts listed under Space, storage and logistics, and keep the M54's A/C compressor until the A/C is charged (Air conditioning).

If your car is a 325xi, converting it to rear drive adds about $0–$1,500 in parts with a donor built from 09/2002, or $1,000–$3,000 with an earlier one, net of selling the xi's drivetrain and DSC (our estimate). No source costs keeping all-wheel drive. Both routes are in 325xi: rear drive or all-wheel drive.

For comparison, Autoalex's UK build with specialist help cost about £70,000, including two engines (Autoalex Cars – It took 3 years and £70,000 (2025), 18:40), and the all-wheel-drive Touring that sold for $65,000 had more than $70,000 in it (Built for Backroads). A US S54 swap that kept the non-M body and spare-wheel well came to $21,665 all in, including both cars and a budget paint job (Tenza Motorsports – Total build cost (2022), 01:20). With one finished car bid to $59,250 without selling and another sold for $65,000, build this because you want the car, not as an investment.

Time

Rough durations for one person working evenings and weekends. These are planning estimates; the last column shows what builders reported.

Phase Weekends Evidence
Buy, test and strip the donor 4–8 One builder stripped a convertible donor in about a week (M346 Projects – Pt 1, M3 part out (2023), 02:00)
Strip your Touring 2–4
Subframe mounts and floor 4–8 Cutting one V-brace mounting box off a donor "took all day" (Tracks and Trails – I spent $10,000 on my E46 Touring's rear end (2025), 06:20)
Rear arches (and doors, if you reshape them) 8–16 A professional shop took about four weeks, two people at 40–50 hours a week, for the whole body from first cut to paint (SOS Customz – Building a BMW E46 M3 Touring wagon (2023), 26:00)
S54 and axle refresh (in parallel with the bodywork) 6–10 Plan 3–7 days for a first rod-bearing job (Paul Vo – Rod bearing installation and torque procedure (2017), description); Beisan quotes 7 or more hours for a DIY VANOS job (Beisan)
Reassembly: axles, engine, fuel, cooling, exhaust 8–12
Wiring, coding, first start, shakedown 4–8 Allow a week or two for the DME and cluster to visit a vendor; RPM quotes 1–2 business days after arrival, with overnight shipping both ways (RPM)
Front end, paint and trim 4–8, plus shop time One paint shop kept the car four months (M346 Projects – Pt 25, paint reveal (2025), 00:00)

If your car is a 325xi, converting it to rear drive adds 4–8 weekends (our estimate): the front-end trial fit and transplant, with any anti-roll-bar brackets, 1–2; a gearbox-crossmember adapter 1–2; the DSC hardware and pipes 1–2; the DSC loom and coding 1–2 (325xi: rear drive or all-wheel drive).
