Factory documentation and coding kit

BMW's documentation is the reference for every standard procedure, torque and wiring diagram this guide doesn't print. Load the right VIN: one Touring swapper found the diagrams changed once he entered his wagon's VIN, and a Bentley page that didn't match his car misled him (e46fanatics).

Source Use it for Where
BMW TIS (newTIS) Repair instructions, tightening torques, technical data and capacities, body dimensions (group 41 00), alignment values; wiring diagrams (WDS) by VIN newTIS (it runs a browser check, so open it in a normal browser). Read body-side diagrams with your Touring's VIN and engine-side ones with the donor's. One builder found it lacked the right MSS54 DME diagram (e46fanatics). BMW's repair text (TIS issue 12/2007) is also free to read, page by page, on workshop-manuals.com for the 325i Touring and the M3 coupe; the M3 convertible has its own (example page)
BMW WDS (Wiring Diagram System), public mirror Wiring diagrams, DME pin tables, connector views and component locations; the manual's pin tables name the drawing behind every wire wds.psjr.org. It has no VIN filter: pick each drawing by the models and build dates in its title. ISTA shows the diagrams for your exact VIN; BMW's official portal sold a one-day subscription for $32 in October 2026 (BMW AOS)
ETK parts catalog Part numbers, which models use a part, changes by build date RealOEM or bmwfans.info; search by VIN
Bentley E46 service manual A printed manual for the 325i; a seller listing says it also covers the 2000–05 M3 (unverified) Bentley Publishers
BMW service bulletins SI B11 04 04: S54 rod bearings, bolts, torques, oil and break-in. SI B12 09 13: inspections fail when the DME holds the wrong VIN SI B11 04 04, via NAM3, SI B12 09 13, via NHTSA
BMW training manuals How the systems work: E46 M3 (ST041), MS S54 engine management (ST055), EWS (ST051) ST041, ST055, ST051
SGBD job documentation The jobs, status bits and fault numbers Tool32 uses, for the S54's DME (MSS54DS0.PRG), the MK60 DSC (DSC_MK60.PRG) and the other modules SGBD documentation and its MK60 page, a community transcription of BMW's job files
"Flow" E46 M3 torque compilation A forum PDF of the M3's fasteners built on RealOEM printouts, with a TIS alignment page. Cross-check only; confirm in TIS Google Drive, via NAM3

Coding kit. Buy it early and prove it on your unmodified Touring before you need it. Setup steps are in the Wiring and coding manual.

  • Laptop: a dedicated Windows 10 or 11 laptop, 32- or 64-bit, running Windows natively (not in a virtual machine or Boot Camp), with its charger plugged in. BMW Standard Tools 2.12 installs on Windows 7–11, so older advice that it needs Windows XP is out of date (e46fanatics).
  • Cable: a K+DCAN USB cable with an FTDI chip and a switch that bridges OBD pins 7 and 8. On an E46 only the DME talks on pin 7; the cluster, light module and DSC are on pin 8, so an unbridged cable can't read them (e46fanatics, NAM3). Set it to COM1 with a 1 ms latency timer (NAM3).
  • PA-Soft interface: PA-Soft (BMW Scanner 1.4) needs its own interface for cluster and light-module EEPROM work. Its driver is the step most likely to fail on Windows 10 and 11, so install it first (e46fanatics, NAM3).
  • Software: BMW Standard Tools 2.12 (INPA, Tool32, NCS Expert, WinKFP) with E46 data files, plus NCS Dummy and an NCS profile that allows editing, such as Revtor's or FISTER (ECUWorx). Use the NCS Expert 4.0.1 that comes with Standard Tools 2.12, with a manipulation profile such as Revtor's NCSDUMMY4.PFL or terra's "Expert Mode w/ Manipulation": version 3.x doesn't run on 64-bit Windows (NAM3, NAM3). Two owners' INPA builds, labelled 5.00 and 5.0.2, had no MK60 steering-angle page, while builds 3.0.1 and 4.4.7 are reported to have it; Tool32 runs the job, LENKWINKEL_DSC_ABGLEICHEN, either way (e46fanatics, e46fanatics, SGBD documentation). BMW's dealer software, ISTA, is optional.
  • Power: a battery charger or power supply of at least 10 A on the car whenever you code or flash (ECUWorx).
  • For the cluster, if you do it yourself: an EEPROM programmer (R270 type), a hot-air rework station and a blank M35080 chip (e46fanatics). A cluster service replaces all three.
  • Not enough on their own: BimmerGeeks' ProTool reads E46 faults but can't code an E46 (BimmerGeeks); Carly lists only comfort and lighting coding (Carly); the Foxwell NT530 does resets, not module coding (BimmerWorld).
Note

BMW doesn't sell Standard Tools, PA-Soft, NCS profiles or data files to owners; they circulate through forums and vendors (e46fanatics). Scan what you download, and keep the laptop for the car.

Tools and test equipment

  • Lifting and moving: a two-post lift makes this far easier. Without one you need tall jack stands, an engine hoist with a load leveler, a transmission jack, an engine support bar, an engine stand, a low table or dollies for dropping subframes, and wheel dollies to move the stripped shell. Read Safety before anything heavy comes out.
  • Measuring and testing: two torque wrenches (one covering about 5–60 Nm, one reaching 300 Nm for the hub nuts), a torque-angle gauge, a compression tester and a leak-down tester, a fuel-pressure gauge with an adapter for BMW's threaded test fitting (BMW names adapter 13 5 220 for the S54 regulator's fitting and for later non-M rails; BMW ST041 Part 2, BMW ST055), a relay-bypass switch with a 15 A inline fuse, a graduated container of 2 L or more and a quick-connect cap rated for 5 bar for the fuel tests (Test the fuel system), a mechanical oil-pressure gauge with an M12×1.5 adapter for the oil-pressure-switch port (Flow), a cooling-system pressure tester, a multimeter, a vernier caliper for panel thickness, a profile gauge for arch shapes, and a tape measure and plumb bob for ride height and body diagonals. Toe plates and a camber gauge are optional.
  • Engine bench: Plastigauge in the green PG-1 grade FCP Euro uses (FCP Euro – S54 rod bearing replacement DIY (2022), 01:20), feeler gauges and valve shims, E-Torx sockets E10, E12 and E14, and a 12-point 12 mm socket for M11 rod bolts. From Beisan's VANOS procedure: BMW's crank-turning socket 83300491056 (or a 36 mm 12-point socket on early engines, which have four Torx bolts at the crank hub; later engines take a 27 mm hex adapter), and a 32 mm fan wrench with water-pump pulley holder 83300491046 for the left-hand-thread fan clutch (Beisan). If the VANOS unit comes off, add the S54 timing set (cam bridge, locking pins, crank pin) and a transfer-gear holder (ECS Tuning – S54 valve adjustment and VANOS rebuild (2025), 01:30).
  • Driveline and chassis: a clutch alignment tool, a flywheel lock, an O2-sensor socket, a spring compressor for the front struts, bushing press kits (trailing-arm bushings, subframe and diff mounts), a ball-joint separator, an inner tie-rod tool, a pressure bleeder with an airtight cap (BMW's limit is 2 bar, 29 psi: BMW TIS 34 00 050) or a slave-cylinder bleed tool, a brake-pedal depressor and caps for the brake pipes you open in Phase 4, and a brake-line bender: BMW supplies straight pre-flared lines (Calvin's Car Diary – What happened to my £200K E46 M3 Touring project (2025), 37:20).
  • Body: a MIG welder set up for thin sheet (wire, gas and settings: Welding settings and safety), 8 mm (5/16 in) spot-weld cutters, with spares, and a spot-weld chisel, cut-off and flap discs, a hole punch for plug-weld holes (6 mm for the arch lips, 8 mm elsewhere), butt-weld clamps, clecos and panel clamps, a panel flanger if you joggle the arch seams, a cross-line laser, a tram gauge and 3 mm hardboard for the arch offsets and templates, a straightedge for door flush, copper or aluminum backing paddles, hammers and dollies, long sanding boards, and a plastic welder if you graft the rear bumpers.
  • Electrical: depinning keys and a crimper for BMW's terminal families, a multimeter, labels and heat-shrink. Turner sells 12- and 23-piece depin sets (Turner, unverified). Coding hardware is under Factory documentation and coding kit.
  • Safety equipment: a respirator rated for metal fume plus local extraction, two fire extinguishers and a fire blanket, welding blankets, and eye, face and hand protection.

Space, storage and logistics

For 18–30 months you'll store two cars' worth of parts: a stripped Touring shell, an engine on a stand, the donor's axle assemblies and your own, panels, glass and boxes of small parts. Plan the space before you buy the donor.

  • Room to work: one bay for the Touring shell on wheel dollies, with room to open its doors and weld around it; a bench and the engine stand; shelving or wall racks for panels, axle assemblies and labelled bins; and dry storage for parts waiting to be sold. The donor needs a second bay or a driveway spot only until it's stripped.
  • Strip the donor fast. Test it, take everything on the Parts list, cut out the steel you need, then let the shell go. One builder stripped his donor in about a week (M346 Projects – Pt 1, M3 part out (2023), 02:00). Protect what you store: one builder's power-steering line kinked in storage and had to be replaced (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to drive my E46 M3 Touring for the first time (2026), 1:05:20).
  • The donor shell and its title. Sell or scrap the shell through a licensed dismantler or scrapyard; Autoalex's went to a new owner (Autoalex Cars – Part 2 (2023), 13:40). Ask your DMV what happens to the donor's title when the car is dismantled, and keep copies of the title, bill of sale and the VIN-plate and engine-number photos for the engine-change paperwork (Registration and legal).
  • Fluids and refrigerant. Have a shop recover the A/C refrigerant from both cars before either system is opened; venting it is prohibited (EPA). Drain oil, coolant, brake fluid and fuel into labelled containers and take them to a recycling center; your Touring keeps its brake fluid in (Phase 4).
  • Your Touring off the road. Ask your insurer about a storage policy and your DMV whether to keep the car registered during the build.

What to sell, and when. The right-hand column is the guide's one list of fallback parts: your way back if the DSC, cluster, cruise or fuel route doesn't work out. The phases point here.

Safe to sell early Hold until the car has passed inspection
The M54, 5-speed gearbox and clutch, once the M54's A/C compressor is off: keep that until the A/C is charged (Air conditioning) Your Touring's DSC unit, booster and master cylinder, and the donor's
The MS43 or MS45.1 DME and engine harness, once you've tagged its X60004 wires Your Touring's original cluster, with its EEPROM backup
325i axle parts you've replaced: rack, control arms, struts, rear subframe, trailing arms, brakes The donor DME's original file, and the donor's EWS and keys
Touring front panels you've replaced: hood, fenders, bumper, headlights The donor's clutch-switch module, if you fitted a new M3 one (your Touring's doesn't work with the MSS54)
Donor interior, glass, doors and trunk lid; a convertible's top The donor's body harness and connector pigtails, a source of terminals and missing wires
The fuel pump and tank you didn't fit, and the donor's fuel-pump module
The donor's wheel-speed sensors, if it's an MK60 car (built from 09/2002); an MK20 donor's don't fit your harness

Shop briefs

Give any shop a written brief. These cover the jobs this guide suggests outsourcing.

Job Ask for Tell them
A/C, before teardown Recover the refrigerant from both cars, and write down how much refrigerant and how much oil came out of each The donor's compressor and pressure hose are coming out; you'll cap every opening. BMW puts the recovered oil back in at the charge (Air conditioning)
A/C, after first start Fit a new receiver-drier, 64538377330. Set the oil by BMW's rules: drain the donor's compressor and refill it with the amount drained from the Touring's old compressor plus 10 g, add back the oil recovered from the Touring, and add about 30 ml (1 oz) for the new drier: about 150 ml (5.1 US fl oz) of PAG in all, ND-8 grade for the Denso compressor (spareto). Evacuate for at least 30 minutes, with no more than 7 kPa (2 inHg) of change in a 5-minute hold. Charge R-134a by weight to the underhood label, then run the compressor in The system has been open for months. Only the compressor-to-condenser hose (64536902681) is an M3 part; the condenser, the other lines and the drier's bracket are the same parts on both cars (ETK: M3, ETK: Touring). Bring your photo of the label, the Touring's old compressor and the recovery figures. BMW's targets: low side 1–2 bar, high side 10–15 bar, centre vent 4–20 °C (40–68 °F) (Air conditioning)
Subframe reinforcement welding Underside plates at all four mounts plus the topside work: the rosette welds over the rear mounts, the floor tied to the rails, and V-brace mounting boxes It's a Touring with no rear-seat bulkhead, so kit parts that brace against one won't fit (Calvin's Car Diary – What happened to my £200K E46 M3 Touring project (2025), 30:00). Keep the kit's spacer plates; no structural foam; the tank, fuel lines and EVAP parts are out. The brake pipes along the floor are still full of fluid: unclip and move them clear of each weld, or shield them (Safety). See Rear subframe mount reinforcement
Paint A full respray (or the panels you list), including door shuts, jambs, under the hood and the tailgate opening; the color code from the body tag What you've prepped and what they must finish. The M3 panels were fitted in primer, so gaps are set. For a color change, ask whether the doors come off and the glass comes out, as on one build (M346 Projects – Pt 23, paint shop prep (2025), 03:00)
Exhaust With the M3 floor, fitting only: the stock M3 front section 18107832909, intermediate pipe 18107832313 and muffler 18107831783 on the center support and BMW's three muffler brackets; flanges 22 ± 2 Nm (16 ± 1.5 ft-lb), muffler clamp 15 Nm (11 ft-lb), hanger nuts 22 Nm (16 ft-lb), hanger bolts 20 Nm (15 ft-lb). With the well kept: a rear section from the M3 mid-pipes to the muffler you choose, such as a US E36 M3 muffler Keep the M3 catalysts, all four O2 sensors, the secondary-air parts and an unaltered muffler: Massachusetts bans by-passes and gutted or louder systems (c. 90 §16). Bring the donor's gap figures. Check clearance to the floor, tank, bumper and tires at full bump; fit heat shields; set the tips to your bumper cut-outs. See Exhaust and the spare-wheel well
Wheel alignment BMW's E46 M3 values, set in BMW's design position after a ride-height check: the M3's normal-position load (a full tank, 68 kg (150 lb) on each front seat and 14 kg (31 lb) in the middle of the trunk), then weights near the struts until each corner is within 2 mm of the M3 ride height. Before and after printouts Tell the shop: M3 axles on a body with major repairs, so BMW allows only the design-position method, not the rig's ride-height-input mode (TIS 32 00 150, 32 00 155). Every geometry part is M3, so the M3 values apply. Front camber moves only about ±0.5° in the strut-tower slots (tool 32 3 140) and caster not at all; rear camber is set at an eccentric bolt and rear toe with tool 32 3 030 (Wheel alignment). If the car sits more than 10 mm below the M3 heights at that load, fix the springs first. You'll calibrate the steering-angle sensor afterwards
DME flash An EWS delete with your Touring's full 17-character VIN written in; manual software if the donor was SMG; otherwise stock US software, since a Euro file can drop US emissions functions. Ask for BMW's latest US software for the donor's hardware: BMW's bulletin SI B12 22 08 (2009) says the original programming of 2001–05 US M3 DMEs could misjudge catalyst efficiency (NHTSA bulletin index, record 10029304) Decline secondary-air, rear O2, catalyst and EVAP deletes: they're illegal on a road car. Ask that every readiness monitor still runs; one builder's modified DMEs never set them (M346 Projects – Pt 26, final reveal (2025), 43:20). Send the fault list, hardware number and AIF you saved. If your state checks software, ask whether their file passes (Registration and legal)
Cluster service Your Touring's VIN in the M3 cluster, with the odometer set so it takes your true mileage from the light module; the M3 coding index and coding kept, not re-coded "from the factory vehicle order"; the donor's vehicle order left in the cluster, since NCS codes an index-23 or -24 cluster only with an M3 order (BMW coding data); rear-door warning lights added if offered Send a photo of your current odometer. Never let anyone change the light module's mileage to match a cluster. Owners name Kassel, Fixels and RPM Motorsport (NAM3) and Huggins Racing (e46fanatics); Kassel added the rear-door warnings for one Touring (Tenza Motorsports – 5 things they don't tell you, part 2 (2021), 05:40)
Machine shop, if you fit ARP rod bolts Resize the rods after the new bolts go in, as ARP's sheet requires (ARP) Mark every rod and cap

Safety

  • Lifts and stands. The car's center of gravity moves when the engine or rear axle comes out. Strap it to a two-post lift or put stands under the end that's getting lighter, and reposition the lift arms; one builder supported the rear once the engine was out (Tracks and Trails – Removing the M54 drivetrain (2025), 06:20). Lower subframes level: studs pass through them (Tenza Motorsports – Supplying the S54 wagon with an M3 rear end (2021), 04:40).
  • Fuel. Drain and remove the tank, filler neck and EVAP parts, including the vapour separator in the right rear wheel well, before you weld or grind anywhere near the rear of the car, and cap every line. Store fuel in approved cans away from the work. When you run the pump for a test, work outdoors or with the doors open, away from flames, sparks, heaters and grinding, with an extinguisher at hand, eye protection and fuel-resistant gloves. Relieve the pressure before you open a joint: BMW warns that "residual fuel pressure may be present" (BMW ST041 Part 2). Never run the pump dry or with the front feed line open, and collect test fuel only in an approved container (Test the fuel system).
  • Refrigerant and coolant. Never open an A/C line before a shop has recovered the refrigerant: nobody may vent it (EPA). The cooling system runs at up to 2.0 bar (29 psi): open the expansion-tank cap only with the coolant cold. BMW checks the level only at 30 °C (86 °F) or below (Cooling and oil cooler).
  • Battery and electronics. Disconnect the battery before welding, unplug the DME and alternator, and clamp the welder's ground close to the weld, never through suspension parts (Garagistic K0536).
  • Fire. BimmerWorld warns that BMW's factory chassis coating "can be extremely flammable" (BimmerWorld). Strip coatings and seam sealer back from the weld, keep two extinguishers and a fire blanket at hand, and stay with the car until everything has cooled.
  • Fumes. Reinforcement plates are often zinc-coated, as CMP's 2.5 mm plates are (CMP), and weld-through primer is zinc-rich. Zinc fume causes metal fume fever, so use local extraction or a respirator rated for metal fume (OSHA). Settings and test coupons: Welding settings and safety.
  • Airbags. Disconnect the battery and follow BMW's procedure before removing the steering wheel or anything else with an airbag.
  • Brakes. The brake fluid stays in the system through the build (Phase 4), so keep weld heat and spatter off the brake pipes along the floor: unclip and move a pipe clear of a weld, or shield it, and keep every opened end capped (our recommendation). Don't drive until the pedal is firm, then prove the ABS with a careful hard stop on a quiet road (DSC, brakes and steering angle).

Parts list

"Source" says where each part comes from: Donor M3, Keep (from your Touring), Buy new, or Fabricate. Take every donor part before the shell goes; anything you miss turns up months later. In the web version you can filter by source and tick parts off as you get them. Part numbers come from BMW's parts catalog (ETK). To see which models use a part, add its number to https://bmwfans.info/parts-catalog/, for example 31111096902. Check every number against your VIN on RealOEM before ordering. Single-use fasteners, seals and fluids are under Consumables and single-use parts. If your car is a 325xi, its extra and different parts are in 325xi: rear drive or all-wheel drive.

Engine and engine bay

Part Source Notes
S54B32 engine, complete with ancillaries Donor M3 Keep the alternator, starter, A/C compressor, power-steering pump, intake, airbox, sensors, and the secondary-air pump and valve with it. The compressor is a Denso 7SBU16C filled with ND-8 PAG oil; Denso lists 5 pulley grooves for 64526910458 and 4 for the later 64526916232, so check the donor's pulley before you buy a belt (spareto: 64526910458, 64526916232)
M3 engine support arms; new engine mounts Donor M3 The arms set the engine's position; check oil-pan clearance to the rack before tightening. Fit new mounts
M3 engine harness with its E-box branch and gearbox-module harness Donor M3 Take the E-box fuse carrier and every E-box plug: X6011, X6021, X6053 and X6054, and the battery feed X64101/X64102 (WDS, manual). Keep the gearbox-module harness with it: its X6053 halves don't mate with a Touring's. The harness changes at 09/2003 (ETK)
M3 DME (MSS54 or MSS54HP) Donor M3 Keep it with its own harness; EWS delete with your VIN, see Immobilizer (EWS)
M3 accelerator pedal Donor M3 Your pedal's wires use the same X60004 pins on all three DMEs, and both cars list the same pedal module, 35426786282 (WDS, ETK); take the M3's as a spare
Radiator 17102228941; fan shroud 17112228943 with air ducts 17112228945 and 17112228946 Donor M3 They bolt to your Touring's radiator supports, which take the same mounting parts on both cars. Leave off the Touring's adjusting screw, drain plug and lower seal; the M3 radiator has no drain plug (ETK: M3, ETK: Touring, Cooling and oil cooler)
Viscous fan 11521712058 and coupling 11527831619 Donor M3 Your manual Touring has none: ETK lists the mechanical fan for automatic Tourings only (ETK: M3, ETK: Touring). The coupling has a left-hand thread
Electric pusher fan 64546988914 with compression shroud 64546905077 Donor M3 It sits in front of the condenser. Your manual Touring's electric fan sits in its radiator shroud (17117561757), with its plug X82 on the shroud. The DME wire stays on the same pin, but X82's lead may need extending or re-routing to reach the pusher (ETK, ETK: Touring shroud, WDS, manual). A manual Touring almost certainly has no pusher of its own, and WDS names X82 the auxiliary-blower connector (WDS): in one M3-Touring swap the M3 pusher "bolted right into the touring's rad support and plugged right in" (NAM3). It needs the M3 bumper's ducting: one Touring couldn't use it behind its stock bumper and fitted it with an M-Tech II bumper (NAM3 – Kaiv's first S54 Touring #20)
Coolant expansion tank 17112283344; thermostat 11531318274 (80 °C) and O-ring 11531318402; vent screw 17111712788; hoses Buy new The plastic tank gets brittle with age (BimmerWorld). It sits on the donor's holder 17112229108, on the other side of the engine bay from the 325i's, so extend or re-route the level-sensor lead (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to drive (2026), 22:40). The holder is M3-only and also carries the secondary-air pump; the 2.0 bar cap and the level switch are the same parts on both cars (ETK, ETK: air pump, Cooling and oil cooler)
Secondary-air pump brackets 41147894115 (front) and 41147894116 (rear), on the right strut tower Donor M3, or buy new A non-M body lacks them. They're the only M3-only body brackets where the M3 holder 17112229108 sits, which carries both the expansion tank and the secondary-air pump, so the holder most likely bolts to them (our inference) (ETK). New, they're about $15–$17 each at BMWPartsDeal (October 2026) (BMWPartsDeal). Measure their positions on the donor, then cut them off and weld them in (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to drive (2026), 23:20, M3projekts – Ep8, trunk floor (2023), 10:00), weld in new ones, or fit copies with rivnuts (M346 Projects – pt 13 (2024), 00:05)
Heater valve Keep (recommended), or Donor M3 Every E46 M3 except the CSL has a valve with an auxiliary water pump (64118369807) whose two wires aren't in your harness; your plain valve (64118369805, the CSL's too) fits the S54 with no wiring (ETK, NAM3). With the M3 valve, wire and code the pump: without it, one car was hard to bleed (UNRIVALED – Watch this before you S54 swap your BMW (2021), 02:32, manual)
Heater hoses: engine to valve 64216902678, heater core to engine 64216902680; valve to heater core 64216902679 with the M3 valve Donor M3 Your Touring's are M54 parts (ETK)
Valve-to-heater-core hose 64212282548, with your plain valve Buy new The CSL's hose, the one ETK pairs with the plain valve and the S54's hoses (ETK). Your Touring's 64218363198 may fit, but nobody has tried it
Washer reservoir, pump and level sensor Donor M3 The M3 reservoir sits low behind the bumper; extend the pump and sensor leads (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to drive (2026), 23:00, M3projekts – Ep5, S54 install (2023), 04:00)
Engine oil cooler 17212228942, holder 17212229744, pipe 17222283209 and brackets Donor M3 All M3-only parts (ETK); fit new O-rings 17222245358 (4). It sits under the radiator and breathes through the M3 bumper's lower opening
Power-steering reservoir, lines and cooler Donor M3 Must match the M3 rack; both hoses differ from the 325i's (e46fanatics)
A/C pressure hose 64536902681, compressor to condenser Donor M3 The only refrigerant line that differs: your Touring's is 64536984883. Have the refrigerant recovered first (ETK: M3, ETK: Touring, Air conditioning)
A/C condenser 64538377614, every other refrigerant line, drier bracket and pressure sensor Keep The same parts on both cars (ETK). The drier itself is new: see Consumables
Exhaust manifolds, catalysts, O2 sensors Donor M3 Keep every emissions part for inspection
E-box housing, DME and injector relays, engine ground strap Keep The same parts on both cars (ETK: E-box, ETK: relay, ETK: ground)

Fuel

Part Source Notes
M3 fuel filter 13327831089 Buy new With the donor's housing and regulator (next row) it replaces the 325i's one-piece filter-regulator 13327512019, on the same bracket (13321435583) and cover (13328230397); take the donor's cover sealing element 13327830949, which the M3 adds (ETK). Fit it all before the first start (Tracks and Trails – Attempting to drive (2026), 1:14:00)

Refit them with a new copper ring 07119963129, O-rings 13531720251 and 13531720252 and lock ring 13531736234 (Consumables); one build's regulator leaked at the first start on bad O-rings (M346 Projects – pt 13 (2024), 05:40). Buy a new regulator only if the donor couldn't be tested, or if test T2 traces a bleed-down to it (Test the fuel system)

Keep the metal sleeve (Fuel system)

Owners have fitted it to non-M tanks, the same part as yours (e46fanatics, e46fanatics). New: delivery unit 16142229684 $559.16, pipe set 16112283288 $159.88, front purge line 16132229652 $89.59 and rear purge line 16132229417 $77.76 at BMWPartsDeal, and the baffle $123.62 at BimmerWorld (October 2026) (BMWPartsDeal, BimmerWorld). Both tanks take the same flange seal and screw cap, so the "sleeve" one owner says the M3 pump needs is most likely the M3 baffle (our inference): fit the two together (e46fanatics). Keeping your own pump is the fallback: it must deliver 1.3 L or more in 30 s at 5 bar (our margin) and needs an undocumented adapter (Choose the pump route)

They clip to your Touring's own points, since ETK lists the same clips and brackets for both cars, plus the two supports; four Touring builds fitted them as they are (ETK, Project BMW – Day 5 (2021), 03:00). Feed and return swapped caused one swap's no-start (NAM3)

Or fit the donor's whole tank (16112229736) with its in-tank set, as several Touring builds did (ThaChileanDude – Building an e46 m3 Wagon in 10 days (2024), 17:00, PistonHeads). An M56 SULEV car's sealed tank is a different case: one was replaced with the M3 tank, but that changes a certified evaporative system, so ask your state first (Tenza Motorsports – No more SULEV (2021), 00:20, Registration and legal). Don't drop a tank with its vent hoses attached: the plastic nipples snap and aren't sold separately (Tenza Motorsports – Supplying the S54 wagon with an M3 rear end (2021), 06:40)

The separator sits in the right rear wheel well behind the trim, inside the arch graft: take it out before the arch work and refit it (BMW ST041 Part 3). All of it has to keep working for the leak test (Filler and EVAP)

A new holder is $92.19 at BMWPartsDeal (October 2026) (BMWPartsDeal). If you keep the well, keep your canister mount and covers 51718233265 and 51718233266
Fuel-pump relay K96 Keep BMW's drawings put its coil on X60004 pin 10 on both the MS43 and the MS45.1 (WDS). In documented swaps the US MSS54 drives it from that pin with no wiring change, leaving a stored pump fault that doesn't light the check-engine lamp (e46fanatics); prove it on your car (Fuel-pump control)
M3 fuel-pump module (EKP) 61357892976 Donor M3 Hold it even if you don't fit it: it's the fix if your state objects to the stored fault. ETK lists this number for the US coupe (ETK); a convertible's module sits behind the right rear side trim, so check its label. Don't clear the fault by flashing Euro software: the pin tables mark the EVAP leak-test circuits as US-only, so a Euro file may not run them (pinout sheet)

Front axle and steering

The fasteners that hold the front axle to the body, the subframe bolts, control-arm bracket bolts and strut-top nuts, are the same parts in the same numbers on both cars (ETK: M3, ETK: Touring, ETK: top mounts). So we expect the M3 front axle to bolt to your body as it does to a coupe's; the one open item is where the reinforcement plate's extra screws thread in (below). One 2004 US Touring took the M3's whole front subframe: "it looks like everything should be a direct bolt-on" (Tenza Motorsports – Front end with M3 parts (2021), 00:40).

Part Source Notes

Suction hose 32412229369, pressure hose 32412283893, return pipe 32412282354, cooling coil 17102282339 and its return line 32412282353 are all M3 parts. Fit new sealing rings: four A16×22 (32411093597) and two A14×20 (32411093596) (ETK)

Springs come from BMW's spring table by VIN: coupe 31332283130, convertible 31332282332 (FCP Euro: coupe, convertible, Suspension for Touring weight)
M3 front brakes: calipers, carriers, dust shields 34112282109/110, 325 × 28 mm rotors (345 × 28 mm on ZCP) Donor M3 Fit new pads and rotors. Hoses and pipes: Brakes and DSC

The end links (31356780847) and bar supports (31351094552) are the same parts on both cars; BMW says the M3's links were "adopted from the E46/2". New links needn't come from an M3 (ETK, BMW ST041)

Before it comes off the donor, note which part each hole threads into. At mock-up, run every screw in by hand on your car; if a thread is missing, fit your own plate on its 8. New screws either way (BMW SI B11 04 04)
Steering column, lower joint, flexible coupling and steering-angle sensor 32306793632 Keep The same parts on both cars. The lower joint was 32301094700 until 11/2003, then 32306764006 on both; keep whichever yours has. Fit new Torx bolts 32306778609 (ETK)

That likely explains why a 2004 Touring's plugs didn't mate with its 2002 donor's (Tenza Motorsports – 5 things they don't tell you, part 2 (2021), 03:20), while on a 2003 xi Touring, whose Bosch sensors use the same blue housings, the M3 sensors' plugs mated (e46fanatics). Ask a dealer for that one, or fit M3 coilovers with a rear spring about 10% stiffer than the kit's (our estimates); Ground Control's M3 kit takes any Eibach rate (Ground Control). No maker sells springs for an M3-axle Touring: H&R 29419, Eibach 2067.140 and Vogtland 951069 are for the non-M Touring (springrates). The pads (lower 33531094518, upper 5 mm 33531136385) and the lower control arm are common, so any E46 rear-drive barrel spring fits: choose by rate and height. Moved-over M3 coupe springs sat one Touring low enough to rub (Tenza Motorsports – ECS coilover install (2022), 00:40); late ZCP M3 springs (blue stripe front, green rear) sat another about 8 mm higher in front and 9 mm higher at the rear than early ones (yellow stripes), by its owner's measurement (NAM3 – Black & Tan 332iT #598 (2026))

Other kits are compared in Rear subframe mount reinforcement. Kit parts that brace against the sedan's rear-seat bulkhead won't fit a Touring (Calvin's Car Diary – What happened to my £200K E46 M3 Touring project (2025), 30:00)

This list follows the default route: keep your Touring's DSC unit, booster and master cylinder, the combination that cleared the DSC light in a documented S54 Touring (e46fanatics). On that route no brake pipe changes; only the front hoses do. Why, and the alternative: DSC, brakes and steering angle.

Electronics

Part Source Notes
M3 instrument cluster Donor M3 Needs a new M35080 EEPROM carrying your VIN and no mileage of its own, so that it takes your true mileage from the light module (e46fanatics, NAM3). PA-Soft alone can't rewrite a used cluster's VIN or mileage (e46fanatics). On one Touring built before 09/2001 the light module didn't pass the mileage across (e46fanatics). M3 clusters have no rear-door warning lights and over-read about 8.9% by design (e46fanatics). The new chip brings back the donor's vehicle order as well, and that's the order the cluster needs: BMW's coding data accepts an index-23 or -24 M3 cluster only with an M3 order, so leave the donor's there and keep your light module as the source of your car's order (BMW coding data, manual). Or use a cluster service (Shop briefs)
Your Touring's cluster Keep Hold it as the fallback, with its EEPROM backup
Light module (LCM), EWS, keys, lock cylinders, body module (GM5) Keep The light module holds your car's true mileage and VIN (e46fanatics); make the cluster match it, never the reverse
M3 clutch-switch module 61319122700 Donor M3, or buy new Required. The M3 module outputs +12 V with the pedal up, which the MSS54's clutch and gear-switch chain needs; your Touring's (61319231129) switches to ground and doesn't work with it (NAM3). Two S54 builds cured no cruise with it (e46fanatics, NAM3). Keep its wire to EWS pin 8, which stops the car cranking without the clutch

Buy these new. Part numbers come from ETK, BMW's SI B11 04 04 and the "Flow" compilation of ETK pages (Flow); confirm each by VIN. Torques for these fasteners are under Torque values in the Appendix.

Step-by-step build

The build runs in three stages, with bench work in parallel (Figure 3). Phases 0 to 2 come first: prove your tools on the unmodified Touring, record its baseline, and test the donor while it still runs.

  • Stage 1, strip and metalwork (Phases 4–6). All welding happens while the car is stripped and the fuel tank is out: subframe mounts, floor and rear arches (and the doors, if you reshape them). You fit-check the M3 rear axle and muffler before you close the floor, and mock up the axle with your final springs, dampers, wheels and tires before you cut the arches.
  • Stage 2, mechanical (Phases 7–12). Axles, fuel, engine, cooling, exhaust, wiring and coding, then the first start and shakedown with the M3 front end fitted in primer.
  • Stage 3, finish (Phase 13). Final bodywork, paint, trim and inspection.

If you would rather paint once with the car empty, you can move paint to the end of Stage 1. You give up the chance to fix gaps and clearances found during the shakedown without touching fresh paint.

Time puts the phases on a calendar, with the bench work running alongside.

How to use the phases. Each phase says what to do and in what order, and links to the deep dives and the Wiring and coding manual for how. Torques are in Torque values and fluids in Fluids and capacities. Each phase ends with a Done when table: the checks, what a pass looks like, and what to do if one fails. Don't cover a phase's work with the next one until every check passes.

Keep the fallbacks. Hold on to the parts on the hold list in Space, storage and logistics, among them your Touring's DSC unit, brake booster, master cylinder and cluster, until the car has passed inspection. In one S54 Touring the M3's DSC unit never cleared its fault, and refitting the Touring's own unit cured it (e46fanatics). Plan where two cars' worth of parts will live first: Space, storage and logistics.

Watch the whole order: two DIY series film a complete conversion: Tracks and Trails – building an E46 M3 Touring (2025), 06:00, on a North American 325i Touring, and M346 Projects – SMG Touring build Pt 1 (2023), 06:40, on a US Touring with a convertible donor. Treat their exhaust as a warning, not a model: both cars ended up with catless headers (Tracks and Trails – first drive (2026), 47:00, M346 Projects – Euro header install (2024), 10:20). Keep the M3's catalysts and every other emissions part (Registration and legal).

Phase 0: Paperwork and baseline

  1. Decode your VIN and note the build date and option codes. Then confirm what you have (Check your own Touring first explains each check):
    • A rear-drive 325i, not an xi. At bmwfans an xi's VIN decodes as "325xi" (NHTSA's decoder calls it a "325i"), and its vehicle order carries option $203, all-wheel drive. If it's an xi, choose a route in 325xi: rear drive or all-wheel drive before you buy a donor: it changes which donor you want.
    • An M54B25 engine with a plastic tank, not the M56 SULEV. BMW's bulletin introduced the M56 for 2003 with automatics, for California, New York and Massachusetts (Vermont from 2004). BMW's catalog can be read as listing a five-speed for the US 325i M56 Touring, but only in groups shared with other engines, and its M56 gearbox-module harness is for automatics only, so a manual M56 is probably a conversion. Either way a manual doesn't prove an M54: check the engine code and the tank. An M56 car has a pump controller, a metal tank and no return line, and the fuel plan doesn't apply (BMW B11 75 02, ETK: gearbox, ETK: pump controller).
    • The DME: an MS43 if built to 02/2003, an MS45.1 from 03/2003; confirm it on the label (ETK, manual). The re-pin list depends on it.
    • DSC, not ASC only. BMW lists ASC-only units for US Tourings, mostly up to 09/2001, and those cars have no steering-angle sensor (ETK).
    • Facelift or not. Tourings built from 09/2001 have the facelift front, which matters for fenders and bumper supports, and store their options as a vehicle order (FA) instead of the older key code (ZCS) (BMW ST406). That matters when an M3 module has to accept your car.
    • Climate control: automatic (IHKA) or manual (IHKR). A/C has only been confirmed working with the S54 on IHKA cars, so test it early on an IHKR car (e46fanatics).
    • The console switch panel. Some Tourings have only a DSC button; the M3 Sport button then needs the M3 switch unit and its power feeds as well as two DME wires (Tenza Motorsports – 5 things part 2 (2021), 08:45).
  2. Get the factory documentation (Factory documentation and coding kit). Pull wiring diagrams (WDS) with your Touring's VIN loaded for the body side and the donor's for the engine side. One Touring swapper found the diagrams changed once his car's VIN was loaded (e46fanatics).
  3. Ask your state what an engine change needs, and get the answer in writing: put the questions for your state program to it (Registration and legal). In Massachusetts, write to MassDEP and the RMV Title Division as set out in Massachusetts, and photograph your Touring's underhood emissions (VECI) label: its LEV, ULEV or SULEV category matters there. In California every engine change goes to a BAR Referee, and Smog Check fails modified DME software that doesn't match an OEM or CARB-approved configuration (BAR, BAR, 2021). Wherever software is checked, ask whether a VIN-matched EWS-delete flash passes before you choose your immobilizer route.
  4. Build and prove the coding kit on the unmodified Touring, before you change anything (Wiring and coding manual: before you start). The usual failures are a cable without pins 7 and 8 bridged (an E46's body modules talk on pin 8) and a COM port that doesn't match obd.ini (e46fanatics, NAM3). PA-Soft needs its own interface, and its driver is the step most likely to fail on Windows 10 and 11 (e46fanatics). The software circulates through forums and vendors, not BMW.
  5. Back up everything with the Touring's original modules fitted, as the manual's Session 1 and backup list describe: the FA or ZCS, read from both the light module (ALSZ) and the cluster (AKMB), with screenshots of the option list, production date and type code (e46fanatics); each module's coding files (FSW_PSW.TRC and NETTODAT.TRC) for the cluster, light module (LCM), GM5, DSC, EWS, climate control, and the airbag, steering-angle and park-distance modules if fitted (ECUWorx); the cluster and LCM EEPROMs, read with PA-Soft (e46fanatics); and every module's part number and fault list. Photograph the odometer, and note the mileage the cluster and the LCM each hold. With the DME still in, run its leak-test jobs and tag each X60004 wire with what it does: on an MS45.1 that settles which pin carries the leak-test pump (manual).
  6. Inspect your own shell. Check the rear axle carrier panel (RACP) at all four subframe mounts, top and bottom, against CMP's list of failure points (CMP, part 1, part 2). Check the rear arches (rust starts at the inner lip, Redish), sills, jacking points, battery box and the floor round the tank brackets. A badly cracked RACP changes the plan: BMW's 21 kg replacement panel (41117000246, ETK) is discontinued: BMWPartsDeal marks it "This part is discontinued" (last price $1,304.68, October 2026), so ask a dealer whether a successor exists (BMWPartsDeal, Turner).
  7. Record the baseline before anything changes:
    • Ride height (how): on level ground, loaded to BMW's normal position for your Touring: a full tank (or 3.2 kg (7 lb) in the cargo area for each US gallon short), 68 kg (150 lb) on each front seat, 68 kg in the middle of the rear seat and 21 kg (46 lb) in the middle of the cargo area. Set the tires to placard pressure, bounce each corner and roll the car a few feet. At each corner measure BMW's ride height (rim flange to arch edge), the heights of the hub center and the arch lip, and the jacking-point height; then the roof height at marked points front and rear. Compare the ride heights with BMW's figure for the label on each front strut: "6Z Serie" on 16-inch wheels, 589 mm front and 555 mm rear; "6Z Sport" on 17-inch wheels, 589 and 554 mm; ±10 mm (BMW's figures). The roof and jacking points are your reference for Massachusetts' ride-height rule, because the arch lips get replaced (Massachusetts); the corner heights are your reference for the arches.
    • Label and options: read the door-pillar label's GVWR and axle ratings (expect 2,045, 900 and 1,210 kg on a manual), and note S226A sport suspension or S338A M Sport II in the option codes.
    • Alignment and photos: an alignment printout, asking the shop to include BMW's ride-height figure for your car if its database has one; photos of the engine bay, the DME box (E-box), the harness routing and the underside.
    • A/C and fans: run BMW's A/C quick check: windows and doors shut, engine at 1,500–2,000 rpm, blower on medium, maximum cold, A/C on for more than 3 minutes. The centre vent should blow at least 11 °C (20 °F) below the outside air (BMW ST054, A/C service). Photograph the underhood A/C label, which gives the refrigerant charge and oil. Note the fan layout: a manual Touring should have an electric fan in its radiator shroud, with plug X82 on the shroud; look in front of the condenser for a second fan (Cooling and oil cooler). Book a shop to recover the refrigerant before teardown (Phase 4).
    • Rear doors: mark three points along each rear door's trailing edge and record the shut gap with feeler gauges and the flush with a straightedge across the gap: the arch work has to put them back (worksheet).

Watch: 50sKid – coding the vehicle order (2017), 08:52 reads the FA from an E46's cluster.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Coding kit INPA shows two solid black dots and reads the DME, cluster, LCM, EWS and DSC; NCS Expert reads the FA or ZCS Bridge pins 7 and 8, match the COM port, try another INPA build. Don't back up or code anything until this works
Backups FA or ZCS screenshots, a coding file per module, cluster and LCM EEPROM files and fault lists, stored in two places Repeat. Never change a module you haven't backed up
Your car Engine code, tank, DME, DSC, climate control and switch panel recorded M56, xi or ASC only: re-plan the fuel, axle or DSC parts before you buy a donor
Shell RACP, arches, sills and jacking points inspected and photographed Cracks: plan their repair for Phase 5. Torn or rotten floor: get a body-shop quote before you buy the donor
Baseline Corner, jacking-point and roof heights recorded at BMW's normal-position load; BMW's ride height within 10 mm of its figure for your strut label, left and right within 10 mm at each axle Outside that, or a bigger split: a sagging spring or a damaged part. Note it, so it isn't copied into your targets
Door gaps Rear door gaps and flush recorded at three marked points per door Record them before any welding; the arches have to put them back
Your state Written answer on what the engine change needs No answer yet: don't buy the donor

Phase 1: Buy and inspect the donor

  1. Shortlist manual M3s that meet the model-year rule (Choose the donor). Ask for the VIN, build date and a photo of the engine number. If you might use its DSC unit, prefer one built 09/2002 or later. From then the US M3 has an MK60 with the same 47-pin plug as a Touring built from 09/2001; earlier M3s have an MK20 with a 43-pin plug and a separate pre-charge pump (ETK, from 09/2002, ETK, to 09/2002).
  2. Inspect with the checklist in Choose the donor. Do a compression test and a leak-down and compare the cylinders. One compilation gives about 11–12 bar minimum for the S54, about the same on every cylinder (Flow torque compilation, p.47; confirm in TIS).
  3. Confirm the panels you need are straight and sound: hood, fenders, headlights, bumper, both rear arch areas including the inner lips, and the trunk floor. M3 inner arches rust from the inside (Redish); one builder's donor lost its inner arch as soon as it was stripped (Autoalex Cars – Part 1 (2023), 07:40).
  4. Collect the title or salvage paperwork and a bill of sale. Photograph the engine number and VIN plates; inspectors and insurers may ask for them.
  5. Before teardown, while it runs, record what you can't test later. How to run each test, and what to look for, is in the Test it while it still runs table:
    • Modules: every module's part number, software version and fault list, read with INPA. Note whether the DSC is an MK60 or an MK20.
    • DME: its identity, fault memory and AIF data (the record that holds the VIN), read with Tool32 and saved before it goes to a vendor (ECUWorx).
    • Cluster: its EEPROM, read with PA-Soft and kept untouched (e46fanatics).
    • VANOS: Tool32's timing and leak tests on a warm engine, coolant at 85 °C (185 °F) or more, to compare with after the refresh (MSS54 job reference). Owners and ISTA, not BMW, put a healthy adjustment time at about 180–300 ms (ISTA's limit 500 ms) and the leak test within about ±5 °KW; a status reading "weggedriftet" means the VANOS leaks (manual, Session 6).
    • Fuel pressure, at the threaded test fitting on the regulator beside the filter, with the pump on a bypass (pins 6 and 2 of the module's plug X10157): 5.0 ± 0.2 bar (72.5 ± 2.9 psi); 20 minutes later no more than 0.5 bar (7 psi) lost and still 4.5 bar (65 psi) or more. It decides whether the donor's regulator goes back in (Filter-regulator and vacuum reference) (BMW ST041, part 2, Bentley, quoted on e46fanatics). If you want the untested pump-control lead, also note Tool32's STAT_EKP_CFG_VERBAUT_WERT (manual).
    • Road test: every gear without a grind, no diff clunk, clutch, steering, brakes, ABS and DSC, and A/C that blows cold.
    • Labels: photos of the B-pillar tire placard and the underhood A/C and emissions labels.
    • Arch targets: on a level floor, on the donor's BMW 18- or 19-inch wheels, loaded to BMW's normal position for an M3 (a full tank, 68 kg (150 lb) on each front seat and 14 kg (31 lb) in the middle of the trunk), at all four corners: BMW's ride height, rim flange to arch edge (605 mm front and 587 mm rear on 18-inch wheels, 619 and 600 mm on 19-inch, each ±10 mm, left and right within 10 mm; outside that, use BMW's figure as your target, not the donor's stance; BMW's figures); then the heights of the hub center, the arch lip and a body point both cars share, such as the floor beside each rear subframe mount, and how far the lip sits outboard of the tire's sidewall. Subtract to get each corner's hub-to-body and hub-to-lip figures: they give you the M3's stance and where your new arches go in Phase 6 (Measure and mock up before you cut).
    • Exhaust at ride height: on the same level floor, the muffler's lowest point above the ground, each tip's center height and offset from the centerline, and the smallest gap from a tip to its bumper cut-out. No source publishes them, and they become your targets (Floor and exhaust positions).
    • Springs and struts: photograph the paint marks on each spring and the symbol on each front strut, and note the strut and damper part numbers. They identify the donor's spring-table parts (Suspension for Touring weight).
  6. Book refrigerant recovery for the donor while it can still be driven or towed to a shop.

Watch: Autoalex Cars – Part 1 (2023), 00:40 inspects a donor M3 on a ramp: split brake hoses, a bulging tire, and a trunk floor cracked by an old impact on the rear brace.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Engine Compression and leak-down even across cylinders; VANOS adjustment about 180–300 ms (ISTA's limit 500 ms), leak within about ±5 °KW, no "weggedriftet" (owner and ISTA figures, not BMW's); fuel pressure 5.0 ± 0.2 bar (72.5 ± 2.9 psi), and 4.5 bar or more after 20 minutes Low or uneven: budget a head or engine job, or walk away
Electronics record Module IDs and faults, DME identity and AIF, and cluster EEPROM saved Repeat before anything is unplugged
DSC Unit type noted: MK60 or MK20 MK20: plan to keep your Touring's DSC (option A)
Measurements Hub, lip and body-point heights and lip offsets at four corners, with hub-to-body and hub-to-lip worked out; BMW's ride height at the M3 load, rim flange to arch edge, 605 mm front and 587 mm rear ±10 mm on 18-inch wheels (619 and 600 mm on 19-inch), left and right within 10 mm; muffler and tip positions recorded; spring marks, placard and labels photographed Measure before the car is lifted or stripped. Outside BMW's ride-height range, use BMW's figure as your Phase 6 target
Paperwork Title or salvage paperwork and bill of sale in hand; engine number and VIN plates photographed Don't buy without them

Phase 2: Strip the donor

  1. Have a shop recover the A/C refrigerant before you open any line, and write down how much refrigerant and oil came out; venting it is prohibited (EPA). Drain the engine oil, coolant, gearbox, diff, power-steering and brake fluid, and the fuel tank, into approved containers, and dispose of them properly (Safety). The M3 radiator has no drain plug: drain the coolant at the lower radiator hose and at the block's drain plug (13 mm) (Blankowski).

  2. Label both halves of every connector with matching tags and photograph everything before it comes apart. Bag and tag fasteners by assembly. Support or strap the car before the engine or an axle comes out: its balance shifts on stands or a lift (Safety). Before the exhaust comes off, with the car on a lift, record the hanger stud positions, the exhaust's gaps and the M3 well's depth from the rear-mount datum, and mark and count the floor's perimeter spot welds (Floor and exhaust positions; method).

  3. Work down the Parts list and tag every Donor M3 line as it comes off. Easy to miss:

    • Cabin: cluster; the console switch unit with the Sport button (61316925520 on a coupe, 61316925521 on a convertible; ETK, ETK); the M3 clutch-switch module (61319122700, ETK); accelerator pedal; shift lever and carrier; mirrors; and the steering wheel if you want it (disarm the airbag per BMW's procedure first).
    • Engine bay: the complete engine harness with the DME, its gearbox-module harness and the whole E-box branch: the fuse carrier, the E-box plugs X6011, X6021, X6053 and X6054, and the battery feed X64101/X64102 (manual). Also the brackets for the expansion tank and secondary-air pump (41147894115 and 41147894116, on the front of the right strut tower), which a non-M body doesn't have: measure and photograph their positions before you cut them off (Tracks and Trails – first drive (2026), 23:20); radiator, shroud, both fans, oil cooler and lines; the heater hoses, and the heater valve if you'll use the M3's; power-steering reservoir, lines and cooler; the A/C pressure hose 64536902681, compressor to condenser (the other A/C lines match your Touring's); and the DSC unit with its lines and the master cylinder, plus the brake booster if you plan DSC option B. Keep the booster's check valve (34331161300) with the S54's booster hose: it goes into your booster (Brakes and bleeding).
    • Underside: label every fuel-line end (feed, return, purge) and photograph the clip positions first. Take the fuel filter-regulator with its vacuum-hose set and metal sleeve and the filter cover's sealing element (13327830949); the M3 fuel lines (16122229409, 16122229410, 16122229411) with their tubing supports (16122282049, 16131177494); the fuel pipes set (16112283288); and the front purge line (16132229652) (ETK). From the tank, take the in-tank set (delivery unit 16142229684, left sender 16142229683, jet pump 16142282208 and baffle 16112229656), or the whole tank with every hose off before you lower it (Fuel system). For an M3 trunk floor, also take the canister holder (16132229735) with its nuts, its cover (51717893604), the vent pipes (16132283286, 16132229415) and the rear purge line (16132229417); the complete exhaust with hangers and heat shields; the front heat shields, which differ on the M3 (Project BMW – S54 into a Touring (2021), 00:20); the driveshaft; the clutch hard line; and the M3 front brake hoses (34322229723), which are M3-only (ETK), though new ones are better (Brakes and DSC). The brake pipes can stay with the shell: an M3 built from 09/2002 uses the same pipes as your Touring (Brakes and bleeding).
    • Engine and gearbox: with a lift you can drop the front subframe with the engine still on it, as one UK builder did (PistonHeads); otherwise remove the gearbox and lift the engine out the top. Keep the gear-identification switch (23142229113) on the 420G; cruise control needs it (NAM3).
    • Front axle and steering: the rack with its tie rods and lines, control arms and brackets, struts, knuckles, hubs, brakes, sway bar and links, and the front reinforcement plate.
    • Rear axle as one unit (FCP Euro, part 1): subframe, diff, trailing arms with brakes and parking-brake shoes, half-shafts, sway bar, the tubular push rod (33312229295) and the V-brace (33312229899) (ETK). If you'll fit the V-brace, also cut out its body mounting boxes with their reinforcement panels (Phase 5). Take the rear dampers with their M3 top mounts (33526779670) and bump stops, and photograph each spring's paint marks before it comes out.
    • Wheel-speed sensors, from an MK60 donor (built from 09/2002): the same active type as your Touring's, so keep them as spares. An MK20 donor's are inductive sensors that don't fit your harness or suit your MK60 (manual). That's why a 2004 Touring with a 2002 donor found the plugs didn't mate (Tenza Motorsports – 5 things part 2 (2021), 03:15), while on a 2003 xi Touring, whose Bosch sensors use the same blue housings, the M3 sensors' plugs mated (e46fanatics, Driveline and rear axle).

  4. Remove the front panels: hood, fenders, headlights, bumper with its carrier and supports, kidney grilles and liners.

  5. Cut out the metal you'll graft (Rear arches and doors), drilling out spot welds where you can instead of cutting:

    • both rear arch areas with generous margins: the outer skin plus as much of the inner wheel tub as you can get, or "you're going to have a gap" (M346 Projects – Touring build Pt 14, body work (2024), 33:00);
    • the fuel filler flap with its surround;
    • if you'll graft the donor's floor rather than fit a new one (the guide recommends new: Exhaust and the spare-wheel well), the trunk floor around the muffler, cut with generous margins, with its front reinforcement (51717894229), which coupe and convertible floors both carry (ETK);
    • the M3 muffler brackets, unless you'll buy them new ($27.19 and $71.40 at BMWPartsDeal, October 2026): the rear-left (41122494844) and the right (41112493931). The right one sits on the right rear side member, not the floor, so cut it off the rail with 20–30 mm (about 1 in) of metal round it (our estimate).

    Before you cut the arches, take the rear bumper off and record each quarter: laser-to-skin offsets every 100 mm from 400 mm ahead of the rear axle to 500 mm behind it, at the lip and 30 mm under the shoulder crease, and section templates in 3 mm hardboard or stiff card at seven stations (400, 300 and 150 mm ahead of the axle, at the axle, and 150, 300 and 450 mm behind it) (Datum, stations and templates, worksheet). They show up accident damage now and give you the Phase 6 targets. Cut 40–50 mm outside the seam lines you plan for the Touring (Flare profile), and count the spot welds you drill along each lip.

  6. Sell what you won't use, such as SMG parts, the donor interior and glass, and a convertible's top. Keep the donor's DSC unit until your DSC plan has worked.

  7. Dispose of the shell and its title the way your state requires (Space, storage and logistics).

Watch: DBO – pulling an E46 M3 engine (2019), 27:01; M346 Projects – SMG Touring build Pt 1 (2023), 06:40 cuts the quarters and trunk floor from a convertible donor.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Parts Every Donor M3 line on the parts list removed, tagged, photographed and stored dry Missing or damaged: order it now, while you can still compare it with the donor
Fluids Refrigerant recovered (receipt kept); all fluids drained and disposed of Recover before any A/C line is opened
Floor and exhaust record Hanger studs, exhaust gaps and well depth recorded from the rear-mount datum before the exhaust came off; floor spot welds counted Record what you still can before the floor is cut (Floor and exhaust positions)
Body steel Arches with inner tubs, filler surround and, if you'll graft it, the floor section cut with margins; offsets recorded and templates made at seven stations per side, bumper off, left and right within 3 mm (our suggestion) Rotten or damaged donor steel: plan new BMW or aftermarket panels now (Rear arches and doors)
Shell Shell and title disposed of as your state requires Keep the donor's paperwork and engine-number photos either way

Phase 3: Bench work

This runs alongside Phases 4 to 8. The axles must be ready for Phases 7 and 8, the engine for Phase 9, the DME for Phase 11 and the fenders for Phase 12.

  1. Refresh the S54 on a stand (S54 refresh on the stand): rod bearings, VANOS, valve clearances, seals, rear main seal, water pump, thermostat and engine mounts.
    • Identify the rod bolts by their heads, not the build date. E-Torx (E12) heads are M10 bolts: always new, and tightened in three full cycles. Twelve-point (12 mm) heads are M11 bolts: reused, each in its own hole, and tightened once. BMW warns that not following the M10 procedure "will result in serious engine damage" (BMW SI B11 04 04).
    • Check the clearances with Plastigauge using the old bolts, and fit new M10 bolts only for final assembly: each check would use up one of a new bolt's tightening cycles. BMW's figure is 0.040–0.070 mm (BMW TIS 11 24 571). Some videos quote 0.03–0.07 mm; use BMW's.
  2. Clutch and flywheel: new flywheel bolts and pressure-plate screws (both single-use) and a new pilot bearing (Torque values, Consumables and single-use parts).
  3. Service the 420G while it's out: new input, selector-shaft and output seals (ETK printout in the Flow compilation, p.74), the gear-identification switch if it's worn, and new shifter bushings. Fill it in Phase 9, once it's in the car and level.
  4. Rebuild the axles: M3 subframe and diff mounts, rear trailing-arm bushings, worn arms, ball joints and end links, and the brakes. Fit the rear control arms to the subframe before the diff: one arm bolt can't go in with the diff in place (Tracks and Trails – perfecting the Touring's rear end (2025), 33:20). Keep powder coat out of the bushing bores. If a diff output flange comes out, mark its bolt first and refit it to the mark, which keeps the bearing preload (Flow compilation, pp.80–81). Fit the diff to the subframe here and torque its mounts on the bench, where you can reach them: front M14 bolt 200 Nm (148 ft-lb), rear M12 Torx bolts 20 Nm + 90° (Driveline and rear axle). Leave the rubber-bushed joints snug; you torque them at ride height in Phase 7.
  5. Send the DME away if you chose the delete route (Immobilizer (EWS), Shop briefs). Order the EWS delete and your Touring's full VIN. If the donor was an SMG car, add the manual (HS) software or a transmission-swap change: coding alone left one swapped car's SMG DME in limp mode (UNRIVALED – watch this before you S54 swap (2021), 02:02, NAM3). Decline every secondary-air, O2-sensor, catalyst and EVAP delete. Don't accept a Euro software flash either: it may drop US-only emissions functions such as the fuel-tank leak test, whose pins the DME tables mark "USA" (pinout sheet). The alternative, syncing the DME to your EWS, works only with a virgin DME: a used one has its rolling-code table burned in for good (BMW ST051).
  6. Prepare the M3 cluster now if you use a cluster service: your VIN, set to take your car's true mileage, and the rear-door warning LEDs that M3 clusters lack (e46fanatics, Instrument cluster and mileage). Otherwise do it in Phase 11.
  7. Graft the M3 front fenders off the car, if you're using genuine fenders (Front end on a 4-door body).
  8. Driveshaft: bolt a new flex disc to the shaft's front flange, with the M3's bolts and new self-locking nuts, at 115 Nm, turning the bolt and not the nut; its gearbox side waits for Phase 9. Fit a new center mount (Driveline and rear axle).
  9. Choose and buy the springs, dampers, wheels and tires you'll run (Suspension for Touring weight, Wheels, track and offsets); Phase 6 builds the arches around them. One S54 Touring on moved-over M3 coupe suspension sat so low that its rear tires rubbed (Tenza Motorsports – coilovers (2022), 00:40). Before you order springs, ask a dealer for an M3 coupe's and an M3 convertible's spring numbers by VIN: BMW picks springs from a spring table, and your rear wants about 7–9% more rate than a coupe's (our estimate).

Watch: FCP Euro – S54 rod bearings (2022), 20:51 shows the three M10 cycles; Paul Vo – rod bearing torque procedure (2017), 08:00; ECS Tuning – S54 VANOS rebuild (2025), 17:30, which fits E39 M5 (S62) diaphragm springs and plates; FCP Euro – S54 valve adjustment (2022), 17:19; FCP Euro – E46 M3 clutch (2022), 17:19; FCP Euro – E46 M3 control arms and bushings (2020), 12:23.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Rod bearings Plastigauge reads 0.040–0.070 mm on every rod (old bolts); final bolts fitted and tightened to the procedure for their type Out of range: measure the crank journals. BMW lists 0.25 mm undersize shells (ETK), which means a machine shop
VANOS New seals and oil-pump disc; exhaust-hub tabs intact or the hub replaced (Beisan); the cam bridge sits flat and the crank pin slides in after reassembly (ECS Tuning – S54 VANOS rebuild (2025), 55:11) Re-time before the covers go on
Valves Intake 0.18–0.23 mm, exhaust 0.28–0.33 mm, measured below 35 °C (BMW S54 module) Re-shim
Clutch and 420G Flywheel and pressure plate on new bolts, torqued and marked; three new gearbox seals; gear switch fitted Fix it now; later it's a gearbox-out job
Axles Bushings, mounts and arms renewed; the diff on the subframe with its mount bolts torqued; bolts torqued and marked, rubber-bushed joints left snug Re-press any bushing that went in crooked
DME Back from the vendor with a written list of changes: EWS delete, your VIN, manual software if needed, and nothing else Any emissions function removed: send it back
Running gear Springs, dampers, wheels and tires in hand for the Phase 6 mock-up Don't start Phase 6 without them

Phase 4: Strip your Touring

  1. Have a shop recover the Touring's A/C refrigerant before you open any line (EPA), and cap every opening. Ask the shop to write down how much refrigerant and how much oil came out: BMW puts the recovered oil back in at the charge (Air conditioning).
  2. Disconnect the battery. Drain the oil, coolant and power-steering fluid. Leave the brake fluid in: your brake pipes stay, so cap each pipe end as you open it (the front hoses at the strut brackets, the rear hoses at their brackets, the clutch line), keep the reservoir full, and leave a pedal depressor holding the pedal slightly down, BMW's way to stop the reservoir draining (TIS 34 32 971). Kept full, the DSC unit needs only BMW's bleed for caliper and hose work later, with the tester's routine on the rear circuit; if it runs dry, it needs the routine at every wheel (Brakes and bleeding).
  3. Drain the fuel. Run the tank as low as you can beforehand, then pump the rest into approved containers, outdoors or with good ventilation and an extinguisher at hand (Safety). The E46 tank is a saddle tank whose left half empties through a siphon jet driven by the return flow (BMW ST055), so check that half separately.
  4. Remove the exhaust, driveshaft, M54 engine and gearbox, front suspension and steering, and rear axle. Two Touring builders took the front end off and pulled the engine out of the front (Tracks and Trails – M54 removal (2025), 01:00, Project BMW – S54 swap in a driveway (2021), 00:20). Support or strap the car before each heavy part comes out, and again after: the balance shifts (Safety).
  5. Drop the fuel tank and remove the filler neck, which runs right past the right-rear arch you'll be welding, and cap every line. BimmerWorld calls tank removal "recommended, but not required" for the subframe welding alone (BimmerWorld); with the arches to weld as well, take it out. Then remove the EVAP parts near that arch and under the floor:
    • Vapour separator. A fuel expansion-tank bracket (41148196386) sits among the rear wheelhouse parts (ETK). It carries the liquid-vapour separator (16136752641), which sits in the right rear wheel well behind the trim, inside the arch graft (BMW ST041 Part 3). Take it out with its vent hoses, keep the bracket (or transfer it if you graft the donor's inner tub), and refit both before the tank goes back in.
    • Canister and leak-test pump. Under the right rear of the floor, between the battery box and the spare-wheel well, sit the charcoal canister and the DM-TL leak-test pump (Tenza Motorsports – No more SULEV (2021), 01:30). Photograph them and record their position from the rear-mount datum (Floor and exhaust positions), then remove them with their hoses and covers (51718233265, 51718233266), cap the hoses and label the pump's plug. The Phase 5 mock-up decides where they go back (Exhaust and the spare-wheel well).
  6. Remove the rear seats, cargo-floor trim and carpet, rear trim, rear door cards, wheel-arch liners and battery. Empty the spare-wheel well (spare, jack, tool kit, anti-drone liner and deadener), and take out the control modules under the load floor, labelled, plus the rear washer reservoir and the sound-system parts in the side areas (what's in the well). Strip sound-deadening back from every weld line, then record the well, the hanger plates and the battery vent and ground positions (Floor and exhaust positions).
  7. Remove the M54 harness and DME for resale. The body harness stays.
  8. Sell the M54, 5-speed, MS43 or MS45.1 DME and engine harness, the 325i axle parts and the Touring's front panels. Before the M54 goes, unbolt its A/C compressor, cap its ports and keep it until the A/C is charged: BMW sets the oil in a replacement compressor by what the old one held (Air conditioning). Keep the fallback parts in the hold list under Space, storage and logistics.
  9. Pressure-wash the underside and let it dry, then look again with everything off: the RACP from above and below, the rails, the inner arches, and the floor behind the tank and brake-pipe brackets, where builders have found trapped rust (Autoalex Cars – Part 3 (2023), 12:40).

Watch: Tracks and Trails – M54 removal (2025), 06:20 supports the rear once the engine is out.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
A/C Refrigerant recovered (receipt kept, with the refrigerant and oil amounts); every opening capped; the M54's compressor kept, ports capped Already empty: note it. The drier is replaced at the charge in Phase 12 anyway
Brakes Brake fluid left in: reservoir full, every opened pipe end capped, pedal depressor in place Reservoir ran dry or a pipe stood open: plan the DSC routine at every wheel in Phase 11 (Brakes and bleeding)
Fuel Both halves of the tank drained; tank, filler neck and EVAP parts, including the canister and leak-test pump, out and stored away from the work area Fuel left in the left half: drain it through its sender opening
Support Shell stable on stands or the lift with the engine and axles out Re-position the supports before anyone works under it
Fallback parts Every part on the hold list in Space, storage and logistics labelled and stored Don't sell them yet
Inspection Underside clean and dry; new findings photographed and added to Phase 5 Plan the extra repairs before you buy plates

Phase 5: Metalwork 1, subframe mounts and floor

This is the point of no return: once you cut into your Touring's floor, it can't easily go back to stock, so finish Phases 0–4 and be sure of the plan first. The reinforcement and the floor are one job. The tops of the rear mounts sit at the front corners of the spare-wheel well, so opening the well gives you access to them (CMP, part 2). Rear subframe mount reinforcement has the procedure, and Exhaust and the spare-wheel well has the floor options, the method and the pass values. This guide recommends a new BMW M3 trunk floor (41127895619) with its front reinforcement (51717894229): BMWPartsDeal lists them at $763.61 and $88.22 (October 2026), and new steel keeps donor body steel out of your car. Below is the order. The floor closes only after the axle and muffler have been tried in place.

If you're keeping the well and fitting a muffler in the Touring's own position, as some S54 Touring builders do (e46fanatics), reach the mount tops through trunk-floor windows in step 5 and close them with the kit's patch plates in step 9 (BimmerWorld). Skip step 8.

  1. Get the welding right first (Welding settings and safety). Measure your panel thicknesses, then weld test coupons in them with BMW's 8 mm (5/16 in) plug-weld holes, break them, and compare them with I-CAR's pass values. Set up fume extraction and a fire watch, and take every fuel and EVAP part away from the work, including the charcoal canister and leak-test pump under the right rear of the floor.
  2. Measure the body diagonals across the rear and the front subframe mounting points, and write them down (Welding settings and safety shows how). BMW's E46 body control dimensions cover the sedan, coupe, Touring and convertible on one set of sheets (TIS 41 00): ±1 mm up to 1 m, ±2 mm above. At the rear the damper mounts are 1,060 mm apart, the spring seats 1,013 mm, the trailing-arm mounts 1,296 and 1,536 mm and the rear axle carrier mounts 440 and 660 mm, and the front strut tower is 3,086 mm from the rear damper mount. BMW calls them a rough check; correct repairs need a straightening bench (TIS top view, rear). Before anything is cut, make sure the Touring's well, hanger plates and battery-box fittings are recorded from the same datum as the donor's, with the canister position you took before it came out in Phase 4 (worksheet).
  3. Clean to bare metal and repair what Phases 0 and 4 found: stop-drill and weld cracks, and re-weld failed spot welds.
  4. Weld the underside plates, with the kit's spacers as its instructions say.
  5. Open the spare-wheel well by the cut rules: drill its spot welds from the cargo side with an 8 mm spot-weld cutter, through the flanges only, and split it away from below, keeping the RACP, rail and rear-panel flanges whole. The drilled holes become your plug-weld holes. For a donor-floor graft, drill out the same welds on both floors (M346 Projects – Touring build Pt 14, body work (2024), 00:40). Then check every spot weld the well was hiding (method).
  6. Weld from above through the opening: the three rosette welds on top of each rear mount (BimmerWorld), any failed rail-to-floor spot welds, and topside rail plates if you fit them; CMP's list the Touring (CMP). Some kits' cabin-side pieces won't fit, because a Touring has no partition wall behind the rear seat (Calvin's Car Diary – PT15 (2025), 30:00). Then the front mounts: their top welds sit under the rear seat, and reaching them "requires cutting into the floor of the cabin" (CMP, part 2). Weld a patch over the opening afterwards.
  7. V-brace, if you'll fit it. A Touring has grommets where the M3 has threaded mounts for its V-brace, so builders weld in mounting boxes cut from the donor or bought (Autoalex Cars – Part 3 (2023), 05:00, Tracks and Trails – perfecting the Touring's rear end (2025), 06:00). Weld them in now, with the rest of the underside work. While the welder is out and the engine bay is empty, also weld the donor's secondary-air-pump brackets 41147894115 (front) and 41147894116 (rear), or new ones, to the front of the right strut tower at the positions you measured on the donor; the M3 expansion-tank holder most likely bolts to them in Phase 10 (our inference from BMW's catalog). Copies on rivnuts work too (Cooling and oil cooler).
  8. Fit-check before you close the floor. The M3 muffler hangs from two mounts on the left and one on the right (Redish Motorsport – Touring build Part 1 (2022), 06:00). Your front-left bracket (H1, 41112497585) is already the M3's part; replace the rear-left plate (H2; 41118204223 on your car) with the M3's 41122494844, and tack the right bracket (H3, 41112493931) to the right rear side member, all at the donor's recorded positions (hangers). Clamp or cleco the new floor in, bolt up the M3 rear subframe with its diff, and hang the M3 muffler on all three hangers. Check its gaps against the donor's figures and whether your canister clears the muffler's right end by 25 mm (1 in); if it doesn't, plan the M3 canister holder (canister). Weld the right bracket fully, then take the axle and muffler out again.
  9. Close the floor with a new BMW M3 floor (recommended), the donor's M3 floor, or a ribbed flat panel no thinner than the original (Exhaust and the spare-wheel well). Plug-weld it down through the drilled 8 mm holes into the floor beneath, at every factory spot-weld position and at least 25 mm (1 in) apart. Check that the battery tray and cargo-floor supports still fit.
  10. Measure the diagonals again and compare.
  11. Protect everything: weld-through or epoxy primer, seam sealer on both faces of every seam, a body plug in every hole, underbody coating outside and cavity wax in the box sections. Light-test the floor before the carpet goes back: Massachusetts fails any hole or crack that would let exhaust gas into the cargo area (540 CMR 4.04(12)(d)). No structural foam while there's welding still to come; it makes welding "more difficult and dangerous" (BimmerWorld).

Watch: Tracks and Trails – RACP plates on a Touring (2025), 07:20; M346 Projects – Touring build Pt 14, body work (2024), 00:40 swaps in the M3 floor; Tracks and Trails – perfecting the Touring's rear end (2025), 03:20 shows the muffler hangers.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Test coupons 8 mm plug welds 10–13 mm across and no more than 3 mm high; broken apart, each leaves a 5–10 mm hole in the bottom coupon; lap stitches tear the top coupon out along their length Change the settings and repeat before you weld the car
Repairs Every crack stop-drilled and welded; failed spot welds re-welded, including those the well was hiding Grind out and re-weld
Reinforcement Underside plates, rear-mount rosette welds, front-mount top welds and any rail plates and V-brace boxes done, with penetration visible from inside where you can see Grind out and re-weld before any sealer goes on
Fit check Hanger studs within ±3 mm and gaps within ±5 mm of the donor's; at least 25 mm (1 in) from any fuel, brake or EVAP part; no contact at full bump or rebound; canister clear or moved to the M3 holder Move the bracket, reshape the floor or move the canister before closing
Plug welds One at every factory spot-weld position, at least 25 mm apart; no porosity or cracks Grind out and re-weld
Diagonals Within about 2 mm of your before-welding figures Stop. Compare with BMW's control dimensions (TIS 41 00) and get a body shop with a straightening bench to check
Protection All seams sealed both sides; a plug in every hole; no light through the floor with a lamp underneath; primed, coated and cavity-waxed Finish it now; it won't be reachable later

Phase 6: Metalwork 2, rear arches

  1. Mock up the rear axle as Measure and mock up before you cut describes, with your final dampers, wheels and tires (Suspension for Touring weight) and the springs out. Jack each hub to its target height, within 2 mm:

    • the donor's hub-to-body height from Phase 1, if the donor passed BMW's ride-height check;
    • otherwise BMW's own M3 figure, measured on your Touring from the bottom middle of the rim flange to the lower edge of the arch: rear 587 mm (23.1 in) on 18-inch wheels or 600 mm (23.6 in) on 19-inch (TIS 33 00, M3);
    • or your own target, if your springs will set the car higher or lower.

  2. Find full bump: with the spring still out, jack each hub until the bump stop is fully compressed, turn the wheel, and check the tire's position there. The new arch has to clear it by at least 10 mm (our suggestion).

  3. Mark the targets: where each new lip must sit around its tire, at the donor's hub-to-lip height and its move-out at each station (Flare profile), checked from the car's center line so both sides match.

  4. Check the donor steel against your templates. BMW's drawings show the same arch on the M3 coupe and convertible, within 2–9 mm by our measurement, but compare before you cut. One builder's donor arches had accident damage and curled in at the bottom (M346 Projects – Touring build Pt 14, body work (2024), 58:40). If yours fail, or you want no donor steel in your body, new BMW M3 convertible steel was about $2,230 a side at BMWPartsDeal in October 2026 (A new-steel route).

  5. Choose the door treatment with the doors shut and aligned. We recommend standard doors with the flare blended in before the shut line, as BMW did; the alternative is to reshape the doors' trailing edges (Rear doors).
