  6. Mark the seams and cut (Arch graft step by step, steps 4–6). Put each seam where the donor and Touring templates agree within 1 mm. These starting positions are our inference from scaled drawings (Flare profile):

    • the top seam about 500–515 mm above the hub;
    • the rear seam about 550–600 mm behind the axle;
    • the front seam 25–40 mm behind the shut line.

  7. Weld in the arches (steps 7–13):

    • the inner arch first, extended or grafted, and checked against the templates;
    • then the outer skin: tacked, its lip plug-welded, then stitched;
    • the gaps at the rocker and door filled;
    • the front of the flare dressed in to meet a standard door, because the coupe's flare sits wider than a four-door body there (M346 Projects – Touring build Pt 14, body work (2024), 28:20), or the door's edge reshaped, as you chose in step 5.

    Graft the M3 filler surround with the right-side arch.

  8. Before you seal the right quarter, check the filler. Your filler pot (51718208646) is the same part on the Touring and both M3s (ETK), so it stays where it is (our inference). Check that it seats in the M3 skin's opening, that the M3 flap closes flush and latches, and that the filler pipe sits unstrained (Filler and EVAP). A filler that doesn't seal will fail the EVAP leak test (Inspection readiness).

  9. Seam-seal the lip channel and every joint, epoxy-prime and cavity-wax (step 14). Leave filler work for Stage 3.

  10. Remove the mock-up axle.

Watch: M346 Projects – Touring build Pt 14, body work (2024), 27:20 grafts the inner tub; Tracks and Trails – bodywork (2026), 12:40; M346 Projects – Pt 22 door flare (2025), 00:20.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Templates Every station's template fits within 1 mm Planish or rework before primer
Symmetry Station offsets and lip heights above the hub centers match within 3 mm side to side Re-check the mock-up corner heights before you rework metal
Bump clearance At least 10 mm from the tire to the lip and inner arch with the bump stop fully compressed (our suggestion) Rework the inner arch or lip now
Doors Doors open and close freely; gaps and flush within 0.5 mm of your readings from before welding (our suggestion), and inside BMW's E46 gaps: rear door to side wall 4 ± 0.75 mm, front door to rear door 4.5 ± 0.75 mm, doors to sill 5 ± 1 mm, each parallel within 1 mm (TIS 41 00) Rework the door edge or the flare's leading edge
Diagonals Within ±2 mm of your figures from before welding (our suggestion) Stop and have a body shop check the shell on a jig
Filler Your pot seats in the M3 opening; the flap closes flush and latches; the filler pipe sits unstrained Rework before the quarter is sealed
Inner lip A sealed, double-skin edge all round Weld and seal the gaps before primer

Phase 7: Fit the M3 rear axle and fuel system

Do the fuel system first, while the tank is out and easy to reach. Start with the tank empty and log every litre you put in: the log calibrates the fuel gauge later. Work outdoors or with the doors open, away from sparks and flame, with an extinguisher at hand (Test the fuel system).

  1. In-tank set and tank. Move the donor's in-tank set into your tank on the bench (route A, recommended); the donor's whole tank and your own pump are the other routes (Choose the pump route).
    • Remove your delivery unit and left sender. Fit the M3 baffle (16112229656) in the right half and push the M3 jet pump's transfer pipe (16142282208) into it, as Kalim did. Then fit the M3 delivery unit (16142229684) and left sender (16142229683) with new seals (16111184084) and O-ring (16141183543) under the lock rings (e46fanatics, ETK). Check that both plugs latch and both floats move freely.
    • Push the feed end of the M3 pipe set (16112283288) onto the pump and pull on it to check that it holds. Clamp its return hose to the tank's return nipple with a new L12-15 clamp (07129952104).
    • Refit the vapour separator (16136752641) and its hoses on its bracket in the right rear wheel well. Lift the tank on its straps without carrying it by its vent hoses, connect the vent pipe to the separator and the filler pipe's hose (16117176011) to the tank's filler stub with two new L42-48 clamps (07129952119), and keep every hose clear of the straps. Put in at least 10 L (2.6 US gal), our figure: BMW says never to run the pump unless it's "submersed in the fuel" (BMW ST041, part 2).
  2. Filter-regulator and lines.
    • On your bracket (13321435583): a new M3 filter (13327831089) with its arrow toward the engine, the donor's regulator housing (13537830368) with a new copper ring (07119963129), and the donor's 5-bar regulator (13531404089) with new O-rings and lock ring; a new regulator only if the donor's failed its Phase 1 test or couldn't be tested (Filter-regulator and vacuum reference).
    • The M3 rear feed (16122229409) from the pipe set's quick-connector to the filter inlet; the return (16122229411) from the housing to the pipe set's return hose; the front feed (16122229410) forward from the housing; and the M3 front purge line (16132229652). Clip them to your existing points and add the two M3 tubing supports (16122282049, 16131177494) (Lines and the pipe set).
    • Check that every quick-connector clicks and holds when you pull it, that feed and return are labelled (swapped, they gave one swap a no-start: NAM3), and that no line touches the exhaust path, the driveshaft or the brake lines. Cap the front feed's engine end with a quick-connect plug rated for at least 5 bar.
    • Route the regulator's vacuum hose forward in its metal sleeve along the feed line, away from the exhaust, and cap its engine end until the engine is in.
  3. Test the pump at 5 bar before anything covers it (Test the fuel system).
    • Put the gauge on the regulator's threaded test fitting under the left front floor, with the filter cover off; the rail has no port (BMW ST041, part 2).
    • Pull K96 behind the glovebox and fit a switch with a 15 A inline fuse across its socket's pins 6 (the F54 supply) and 2 (out to the pump), the way BMW's test bridges the relay socket. Check the pins on WDS for your VIN (WDS). Run on the battery alone, without the charger.
    • Run tests T1 to T5: static pressure, the 20-minute hold, delivery into a container from the return line at the regulator, the voltage at the pump connector, and leaks. Log them on the worksheet. Then reconnect the return with a new clamp, and refit K96 and the filter cover with the M3 sealing element (13327830949).
  4. Raise the rear axle on a table or jack, keeping the subframe level as it goes up over the studs (Tenza Motorsports – M3 rear end (2021), 04:40). The subframe hangs on four mounts: at each front mount an M12×1.5 stud screwed into the body (90 Nm) with a self-locking collar nut (77 Nm), and at each rear mount one M12×1.5×116 bolt (77 Nm). Torque the studs before the axle goes up, line up the front studs before the rear bolt holes, set the push rod with the kit's spacer plates over the front studs under their collar nuts, then torque the nuts and rear bolts and the push rod's bolts (Driveline and rear axle). Fit the V-brace if you fitted its mounts.
  5. Fit the M3 rear dampers on M3 top mounts (new M8 nuts at 28 Nm, new rod nuts at 14 Nm) with the M3 bump stops, and rear springs about 7–9% stiffer than an M3 coupe's, or M3 coilovers (Suspension for Touring weight); then the M3 sway bar and links, the half-shafts with new bolts, brake lines, your own wheel-speed sensors (or an MK60 donor's) (Driveline and rear axle), and your parking-brake cables. Torque the joints that don't need ride height as they go in: the trailing-arm brackets to the body and the two ball-joint bolts at each trailing arm, with new nuts.
  6. Adjust the parking-brake shoes (Brakes and bleeding). You bed them in during the shakedown.
  7. Fill the diff with BMW's limited-slip oil (Fluids and capacities).
  8. Torque the rubber-bushed joints at ride height, so the bushings aren't pre-twisted: the trailing-arm through-bolts, the control-arm bolts at the subframe and the damper lower bolts, which BMW's diagrams mark (Flow compilation, pp.16–17), and the anti-roll bar's brackets and links, which are rubber-mounted too (Driveline and rear axle). With the body on stands, jack each rear hub until hub-to-lip (hub center to the arch's lower edge) matches its target from the mock-up, within 5 mm, and torque there; or torque them once the car is complete on its wheels and loaded to BMW's normal position for an M3: a full tank, 68 kg (150 lb) on each front seat and 14 kg (31 lb) in the middle of the cargo floor (Targets for the mock-up and the bushed joints). Don't jack until the car lifts off its stands, as one builder did (Tracks and Trails – perfecting the Touring's rear end (2025), 40:20): without the engine and gearbox the car is lighter than when finished, so that leaves the suspension a little extended. Paint-mark every fastener.
  9. Refit the canister and leak-test pump now the axle is up, in the layout you chose at the Phase 5 mock-up: your Touring's mounting and covers (51718233265, 51718233266), or the M3 holder (16132229735, four nuts 07147153450) and cover (51717893604) (Filler and EVAP). Connect the vent pipes from the separator and the rear purge line to the front purge line, without kinks past the subframe, and plug in the leak-test pump. Every part has to keep working for the leak test.

Watch: Tracks and Trails – perfecting the Touring's rear end (2025), 35:00 raises the M3 axle into a Touring and torques the bushed joints at ride height.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Fuel pressure (T1, T2) 5.0 ± 0.2 bar (72.5 ± 2.9 psi) static at the regulator's test fitting; 20 minutes after switch-off, no more than 0.5 bar (7 psi) lost and still 4.5 bar (65 psi) or more (BMW ST041, part 2, Bentley, quoted on e46fanatics) Bleeds down: pinch the pipe set's feed hose, then its return hose, to find whether the pump's check valve or the regulator leaks, as BMW's test does. Low: regulator O-rings, filter, pump voltage, then the pump. High: a kinked return
Fuel delivery (T3) At least 1.12 L (1.2 US qt) in 30 s, the floor for every E46 engine (Bentley, quoted on e46fanatics), collected from the return line at the regulator so the pump works against 5 bar (our method). A kept non-M pump: 1.3 L (1.4 US qt) or more (our margin) Fit the M3 delivery unit and baffle. With the M3 unit in: the filter, a kinked hose, then the pump voltage
Pump voltage (T4) At the pump connector, within 0.5 V of the battery; 0.5 V or less on the ground side Clean and tighten the pump plug and its ground; check F54 and the K96 socket
Fuel leaks (T5) None at any joint with the system pressurised; feed and return confirmed Fix before the axle goes in
EVAP Separator, canister and leak-test pump in; filler hose on both clamps; every vent and purge hose connected without kinks; the pump plugged in Fix before the exhaust goes in: Phase 10 checks its clearance to them
Rear axle Studs, collar nuts and rear bolts torqued; every fastener paint-marked; the rubber-bushed joints done with hub-to-lip within 5 mm of target; push rod on its spacers Re-torque at the right height
Diff Filled to the fill plug Top up, check the plugs' seals
Parking brake Released: both rear wheels turn freely. 1st tooth: no braking. 2nd tooth: braking just begins. Lever fully up: the wheels lock (BMW TIS 34 10 014) Re-adjust the shoes, then the cables (Brakes and bleeding)

Phase 8: Fit the M3 front suspension and steering

  1. Keep air out of the DSC unit. Your brake pipes stay, so your MK60 can keep its fluid through the whole build. Keep every pipe end you opened capped and the reservoir full, and leave a pedal depressor (or a wedged length of wood) holding the pedal slightly down so the reservoir can't drain, as BMW does (TIS 34 32 971). Then BMW's bleed after caliper and hose work is all it needs, with its tester's routine on the rear circuit only (TIS 34 00 048). The routine at every wheel is needed only after work on the master cylinder, the DSC unit or the pipes between them, or if the unit ran dry (TIS 34 00 050).
  2. Front axle. Fit the M3 control arms and brackets, struts, knuckles, hubs and top mounts (left and right differ) to your front subframe, or the donor's: it's the same part. If you're installing the donor's subframe with the engine on it, combine this with Phase 9. Torque everything now, on stands, in the order in Front axle and steering, with new fasteners wherever Torque values says "new": subframe bolts 110 Nm (81 ft-lb), rear bolts first; control-arm bracket bolts 59 Nm (44 ft-lb); strut-top nuts 34 Nm (25 ft-lb), BMW's E46 figure, M3 included. Only the anti-roll-bar clamp nuts wait, snug, for the car on its wheels in normal position, at the M3 load, in Phase 12. They're the only front joints the M3 torque compilation marks "tighten in normal position" (Flow p.6). If you replace the front hubs (31222229501), each takes a new collar nut at 290 Nm (214 ft-lb) (Torque values).
  3. Reinforcement plate. Offer up the M3 plate and run all 12 main screws in by hand before you order new ones: TIS doesn't say which of its threads are in the body. New screws, rear row first, 59 Nm (44 ft-lb) + 90°, then the six small edge screws (Front axle and steering). If a thread is missing, fit your own plate (51717028433) on its 8 screws, and note it. Never drive without a plate.
  4. Wheel-speed sensors: your own, seated flush in the M3 knuckles, screw at 8 Nm (71 in-lb), leads clipped clear of the strut at full droop (manual).
  5. Center the steering: wheel straight ahead, and the notch in the steering shaft lined up with the coupler's bolt hole (FCP Euro – S54 rod bearings (2022), 39:54). Fit a new pinch bolt (BMW SI B11 04 04). The inner tie rods take 110 Nm (81 ft-lb), which meets the "100 + 10 Nm" TIS prints for every E46, the M3 included (TIS 32 21 2AZ). Before you fit a replacement rack, check that its hard lines clear the subframe; one aftermarket rack's didn't (50sKid – rack replacement (2018), 23:35).
  6. Power steering: connect the M3 lines at the rack with new sealing rings: the pressure hose's M16 hollow bolt at 40 Nm (30 ft-lb), the return banjo with its check valve at 35 Nm (26 ft-lb). The pump end and the cooler go on with the engine (Phase 10). You fill the system with ATF before the first start (Phase 12).
  7. Brakes: fit the parts for the DSC option you chose in DSC, brakes and steering angle. Option A, the default, puts the M3 front hoses (34322229723) between your own pipes and the M3 calipers; no pipe changes (ETK). Option B fits the M3 DSC unit with its master cylinder. With an MK20 donor, use option A. Either way, fit a new grommet (34336765316) and the M3's check valve (34331161300) in your booster now; the hose from the S54 goes on in Phase 10 (Brakes and bleeding).
  8. Fill, flush and prove the brakes (Brakes and bleeding): DOT 4 low-viscosity fluid at no more than 2 bar (29 psi). Flush each wheel, right rear, left rear, right front, left front, then bleed the front by pumping the pedal fully at least 12 times per side and closing the bleed screw with the pedal held down (TIS 34 00 048); then the static pedal test. The rear circuit's tester routine waits until INPA can talk to the DSC (Phase 11), and so does the routine at every wheel if the DSC unit ran dry or you opened the master cylinder or the pipes between it and the DSC unit. Don't blow air through the filled system to test it.

Watch: FCP Euro – E46 M3 control arms and bushings (2020), 15:58; 50sKid – rack replacement (2018), 12:35, on a non-M car with the same rack mounting.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Fasteners Torqued on stands and paint-marked, except the front anti-roll-bar clamp nuts, left snug for Phase 12 Re-torque
Reinforcement plate The M3 plate on all 12 new screws, or your own plate on its 8 Fit your own plate
Steering Wheel straight with the rack centered; full lock both ways without binding, or tire or line contact Re-index the coupler; re-route lines
Brake lines About 560 N (125 lb) on the pedal for 10 s: the pedal holds, with at least 20% of its travel left. Pedal wedged down overnight: no weeps at any union Re-make the union; replace crushed flares
Pedal High and firm after the flush and front bleed Bleed again before you go on. The rear-circuit routine follows in Phase 11, at every wheel if the DSC unit took air
Booster check valve Air passes only from the booster toward the engine Turn it round, or replace it

Phase 9: Install the S54 and 420G

  1. Bolt the engine and gearbox together with the clutch and flywheel you fitted in Phase 3. Fit the M3 engine arms, new mounts and the 420G's gearbox support. Fit the secondary-air valve before the engine goes in (M3projekts – Ep5 (2023), 14:00).
  2. Lower the engine in from above, or raise it in on the subframe. Unbolt the oil-cooler lines so the cooler clears the crossmember (Project BMW – S54 on jack stands (2021), 01:20). One Touring builder had to drop the front subframe to get the S54 in (Tracks and Trails – first drive (2026), 55:40).
  3. Before you tighten the engine mounts, check the gap between the oil pan and the steering rack and subframe. Route the power-steering lines clear of the pan and sway bar: one M3 owner's lines wore a mark into his pan (Paul Vo – rod bearing torque procedure (2017), video description).
  4. Fit the shift carrier and lever with new bushings, then the complete M3 driveshaft: bolt its flex disc to the gearbox's output flange at 115 Nm (the shaft side was done in Phase 3), and fit the center mount (Driveline and rear axle).
  5. Fit the M3 clutch hard line and bleed the clutch (Brakes and bleeding). Clamping the flexible hose while you change lines keeps most of the air out (Throttle House – E46 clutch delay valve removal (2016), 00:26).
  6. Fill the 420G to its fill plug with the car level (Fluids and capacities).

Watch: Project BMW – S54 into a Touring (2021), 05:20 installs the engine and gearbox together; FCP Euro – E46 M3 clutch (2022), 26:34 fits the 420G.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Oil pan Clear of the rack and subframe; power-steering lines clear of the pan and sway bar Check the engine sits on the M3 arms correctly; re-route the lines
Mounts Engine and gearbox mounts torqued and marked Re-torque
Clutch Pedal firm and returns; the slave's pushrod moves its full stroke (check from below with a helper) Bleed again; bench-bleed the slave (Brakes and bleeding)
Driveshaft Flex disc and center mount torqued; center bearing preloaded forward (the Flow compilation gives 4–6 mm, p.79) Loosen, preload and re-torque
Gearbox Filled to the fill plug, no leaks at the seals Fix a leaking seal now

Phase 10: Cooling, intake and exhaust

  1. Fit the cooling parts (Cooling and oil cooler):
    • the M3 radiator on your Touring's radiator supports, which take the same mounting parts; leave off the Touring's adjusting screw, drain plug and lower seal;
    • the oil cooler under it, with new O-rings: pipe unions 25 Nm (18 ft-lb), M8 flange screws 20 Nm (15 ft-lb), M6 bracket bolt 6 Nm (53 in-lb);
    • the shroud and its air ducts, then the viscous fan: fan to coupling 10 Nm (89 in-lb), coupling to water pump 40 Nm (30 ft-lb), with a left-hand thread;
    • the pusher fan and its compression shroud in front of the condenser, with plug X82 routed to it (manual);
    • a new M3 expansion tank on the donor's holder 17112229108, which also carries the air pump, bolted to the brackets 41147894115/116 you welded or riveted to the front of the right strut tower at the donor's positions, on the other side of the engine bay from the Touring's, with its level switch plugged in;
    • the S54's heater hoses and the heater valve you chose: your plain valve with the CSL's hose 64212282548 (recommended), or the M3 valve with its pump wired;
    • a new vent screw 17111712788 in hose 11537830716, left open for the fill in step 8.
  2. Fit the intake and airbox, and the power-steering reservoir, lines and cooler. Connect the S54's brake-booster hose to the M3 check valve you fitted in your booster in Phase 8. On the M3 the hose meets the booster from the other side, so shorten or re-route it to reach and clamp it with 11151726340, as Tenza and two other builds did (Tenza Motorsports – 5 things (2021), 07:40, Brakes and bleeding).
  3. Route every sensor lead now. The coolant-level sensor moves sides with the tank, the M3 washer tank sits low behind the bumper, and the radiator-outlet sensor lead has to reach the M3 radiator's sensor. Your 325i already reads that sensor; the one build that had to extend the lead was a Euro 318d diesel Touring (Tenza Motorsports – 5 things (2021), 00:40, M3projekts – Ep6 (2023), 07:31). The electric fan's plug X82 sits on a manual Touring's radiator shroud and has to reach the pusher fan in front of the condenser: compare the plugs, then extend it if it's short (manual). Extend leads with proper terminals or soldered, heat-shrunk joints, and list each one for the Phase 11 checks.
  4. A/C: fit the donor's pressure hose 64536902681 between the compressor and the condenser. Keep your Touring's other lines, condenser and drier bracket, which are the same parts on both cars (ETK, M3, ETK, Touring). Fit new O-rings at every joint you open, flange screws 20 Nm (15 ft-lb). Leave the old drier in place and keep the system capped for the shop: the new drier (64538377330) goes in on the day of the charge (Air conditioning).
  5. Exhaust: fit the M3 manifolds, catalysts and O2 sensors (label the sensor plugs so they can't be swapped) and the secondary-air parts. Then fit the front section 18107832909 and intermediate pipe 18107832313 on the center support 18211436309 with the M3 rubbers 18207832991, flanges at 22 ± 2 Nm (16 ± 1.5 ft-lb), and hang the muffler 18107831783 on the three Phase 5 brackets: hanger nuts 22 Nm (16 ft-lb), hanger bolts 20 Nm (15 ft-lb), and the clamp flange at 15 Nm (11 ft-lb) with new gasket rings (Exhaust and the spare-wheel well, Flow p.87). Fit every nut and bolt. If you kept the well, build or buy the rear section instead (Shop briefs). Keep every emissions part.
  6. Heat shields: the M3 rear-silencer shield 51482494848 over the muffler and the tunnel shield 51487893366 (one builder found your Touring's 51488193807 interchangeable), plus a shield wherever the pipes come close to the tank, the cargo floor or the battery.
  7. Clearance: with the suspension compressed and at full rebound, check the exhaust against the gaps you recorded on the donor (within ±5 mm) and keep it at least 25 mm (1 in) from any fuel, brake or EVAP part unless it's shielded (pass values). One Touring's aftermarket Remus system (engine not stated) touched the inside of its 255/35-18 rear tires until the owner switched to 245/40-18 (e46fanatics).
  8. Fill and pressure-test the cooling system, engine cold and ignition off: steps 1–8 of Fill and bleed the cooling system. It takes about 9.3 L (9.8 US qt) of BMW antifreeze 82141467704 and distilled water, 50/50 (Fluids and capacities). Fill slowly with the vent screw open, then pressure-test at 2.0 bar (29 psi), the cap's rating and never above it, for 15 minutes, and test the cap (Flow compilation, p.60, BMW SI B17 03 16). The rest of the bleed comes at the first start, in Phase 12.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Cooling Holds 2.0 bar (29 psi) on the tester for 15 minutes with no drop and no seepage; the cap holds and relieves at 2.0 bar; level at the cold mark Find and fix the leak before the first start
Exhaust Donor gaps within ±5 mm; 25 mm (1 in) from fuel, brake and EVAP parts; clear at full bump and rebound; heat shields fitted; new gaskets; every hanger nut and bolt fitted Re-hang it or move what it touches; don't modify the M3 muffler
Exhaust leaks Checked at the first start, in Phase 12, while the joints are cold: none at any joint; listen at each, or spray soapy water on them Re-seat the joint with a new gasket
A/C M3 pressure hose fitted; new O-rings at every opened joint; flange screws at 20 Nm; system closed and capped for the shop Replace any O-ring you reused
Sensor leads Every plug reaches its sensor without strain, and X82 reaches the pusher fan Extend or re-route it now

Phase 11: Wiring, immobilizer and coding

Work in this order. Pin lists, terminals and each coding session are in the Wiring and coding manual; the reasoning is in Electronics and coding. Steps 9 to 12 follow the manual's coding sessions 2 to 5, in order, and Phase 12 continues with sessions 6 to 9.

  1. Diagrams: BMW's WDS drawings for your build dates, on the public mirror the manual links, or ISTA by your VIN; the manual's tables name the drawing behind every wire (manual: engine harness and DME). Switch the ignition off whenever you plug or unplug a DME connector (BMW ST055).
  2. Engine harness and E-box: route the M3 engine harness, and fit its whole E-box branch with the fuse carrier, its gearbox-module harness and the DME. Compare each E-box plug (X6011, X6021, X6053 or X60531, X6054 or X60541, and X64101/X64102) with its mate, cavity by cavity, before you join them (E-box plugs): a mismatch at X6053 gave circuit-low codes on all six injectors in one swap (e46fanatics).
  3. Re-pin the body side from the move table for your DME: MS43 (to 02/2003) or MS45.1 (from 03/2003) (Harness and re-pinning). The moves cover the leak-test heater, the clutch signal, the cluster's three lamps and its start feedback, the brake-light switch's test contact and a recommended ground at X60004 pin 5, and on an MS45.1 the leftover wires in pins 5 and 15 (and 19, if fitted) come out. On an MS43, move the heater out of X6011 pin 7 before the clutch wire goes in. Re-pin; don't cut and splice. The four-wire move in older forum posts came from a different swap; on an MS43 Touring those wires move the other way (e46fanatics).
  4. Fuel-pump trigger: leave your Touring's pump wiring as it is. BMW's drawings put the K96 relay on X60004 pin 10 on both the MS43 and the MS45.1, and builders report the US MSS54 drives it from that pin; the M3's pump-module wire on X6021 pin 1 finds no mate in a 325i (Fuel-pump control, manual). Never connect the US DME's pulsed pump output to the relay. Expect a stored fault, location 1 (0x01), that shows in INPA but doesn't light the check-engine lamp (e46fanatics).
  5. Clutch, cruise and Sport button: fit the M3 clutch-switch module, 61319122700. The 325i's doesn't work with the MSS54's clutch chain, and two S54 builds cured no cruise with the M3 part (e46fanatics, NAM3). Its signal now crosses into the M3 harness at X6011 pin 7 and runs through the 420G's gear switch to X60002 pin 20; its wire to EWS pin 8, the start interlock fitted to US and Japanese cars, stays. The Sport button is optional (manual).
  6. Other body-side items: the rear-door LEDs in the M3 cluster; the heater valve, either your plain valve or the M3's with its auxiliary pump wired and coded, since an unwired pump made one builder's cooling hard to bleed (UNRIVALED – watch this before you S54 swap (2021), 02:32, manual); and the sensor leads from Phase 10.
  7. Check before first power-up: steps 1–19 of the manual's checks. With the battery off and the DME unplugged, prove every moved wire end to end and open to ground, and measure the coils, injectors, sensors and leak-test module. With the battery on, check the DME's feeds and grounds. Then, battery off again, the DME and every other module plugged in, measure the CAN bus: about 60 Ω between X60004 pins 36 and 37, back-probed at the DME, from BMW's two 120 Ω resistors (BMW ST040). Don't measure at the diagnosis socket: an E46's has no CAN pins, only the K-lines on pins 7 and 8 (WDS).
  8. First power-up: battery on a charger, ignition on, no cranking: steps 20–29. INPA should reach every module, the pump should prime once (STEUERN_EKP clicks K96), and the DME's status bits should follow the brake, the Sport button and, with a gear engaged, the clutch. The clutch module, brake switch and oil-level sensor are electronic, so these bits, not a meter, prove them.
  9. DME VIN (manual, Session 2): read the DME's VIN slots with Tool32 and check that the vendor wrote your Touring's full 17-character VIN. If not, write it into the next free AIF slot (ECUWorx). Inspection testers read the VIN from the DME (BMW SI B12 09 13).
  10. Immobilizer (Session 3): with an EWS-deleted DME, or one a vendor has matched to your EWS, there's nothing to sync; check that your EWS still reads the key and the clutch interlock (NAM3). A sync you do yourself works only with a virgin DME (Immobilizer (EWS)).
  11. Cluster (Session 4): fit the M3 cluster prepared to take your car's true mileage from the LCM (Instrument cluster and mileage). Never write a mileage into the LCM: it holds your car's record, and the replacement cluster must show the true mileage (49 U.S.C. §32704). On a pre-09/2001 (ZCS) car the LCM may not pass the mileage across, so check (e46fanatics). Then leave the donor M3's vehicle order in the cluster. BMW's coding data accepts an M3 cluster only with an M3 order (type key with S54B32, dated 09/2001 or later), so NCS refuses it with your Touring's order: don't write your order into it, and code it only from its own read-out. If a cluster service already wrote your order in, change the type key to BL93 for that coding session only, with no FA_WRITE. Your car's order stays in the light module (ALSZ): read it there for every other module, and never run Code Car (Session 4).
  12. DSC (Session 5): with your own MK60, initialise its VIN and steering angle in INPA, then run its other two compensation routines, pressure sensors and lateral acceleration (DSC, brakes and steering angle). An M3 unit first needs your VIN written in, and coding from a session vehicle order read from the light module (ALSZ), with the donor's M3 type key and a date of #0902 or later for that session only. This calibration is provisional; the final one comes after the alignment in Phase 12. If an M3 unit still won't clear "VIN not initialized", refit your Touring's unit (option A), as one S54 Touring owner had to; he had written a blank coding file to his and reset it in PA-Soft, not INPA (e46fanatics).
  13. Bleed with INPA's routine, now that INPA can talk to the DSC, BMW's way for the work you did (Brakes and bleeding, step 4). After caliper and hose work, BMW bleeds the rear circuit with its tester's routine and the front by pedal (TIS 34 00 048). If the DSC unit ran dry or was replaced, or you opened the master cylinder or the pipes between it and the DSC unit, run the routine at every wheel instead: right rear, left rear, right front, left front, restarting it for each wheel and pressing the pedal to the floor five times after each run (TIS 34 00 050). Pass: a firm pedal and the checks in Brakes and bleeding, step 6.
  14. Clear the faults in every module, cycle the ignition and read them again. Vehicle-order changes, body modules and headlight coding (Sessions 8 and 9) wait until the car runs, in Phase 12.

Watch: 50sKid – coding an E46 DSC unit (2016), 31:14, then the INPA VIN and steering-angle initialisation at 33:47; Tenza Motorsports – 5 things part 2 (2021), 08:45 wires the Sport button into a Touring.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Moved circuits Each reads continuity end to end, with no short to ground Re-seat the terminal; re-check the drawing for your car
CAN bus About 60 Ω between X60004 pins 36 and 37, with every module plugged in About 120 Ω: a terminating module unplugged or cut off (manual, step 19)
Modules INPA reaches the DME, cluster, LCM, EWS, DSC and the rest One module missing: its power, ground and bus wires. Several: the cable's pins 7 and 8
Warning lamps With the engine off, the red oil-pressure lamp and the charge lamp are lit Oil lamp out: the X60004 pin 11 wire to cluster pin 13, and the cluster's CAN_OELDRUCKSCHALTER coding (NAM3, manual)
Cluster Shows your car's true mileage (compare with your Phase 0 photo), with no tamper dot; NCS reads your Touring's order from ALSZ and the donor's from AKMB, as your coding sheet notes VIN mismatch between cluster and LCM (Troubleshooting)
DME VIN Tool32's AIF_LESEN and INPA show your Touring's full 17-character VIN; so does a generic OBD-II scanner, if the DME reports it (mode 09), which no rule required before the 2005 model year Write the AIF again
DSC DSC and brake lamps out; no 5EF1 or 5E1F; INPA reads about 0° with the wheel straight (provisional until the alignment) Session 5. An M3 unit: code it from a late session order read from ALSZ, then initialise it in INPA; still failing, refit your own
Clutch chain In Tool32, with a gear engaged, STAT_KRAFTSCHLUSS_EIN reads 1 with the pedal up and STAT_KUP_EIN 1 with it down; in neutral both stay fixed (MSS54 job reference) The M3 clutch module, the gear switch, the X6011 pin 7 crossing
Fuel pump One prime at key-on; STEUERN_EKP clicks K96 X60004 pin 10 to K96's coil wire (Fuel-pump control)
Fault memory Only location 1 (0x01), the pump fault, and, after a delete, possibly 130 (0x82) Fix every other fault before the first start (Troubleshooting)

Phase 12: Front end, first start and shakedown

Fit the front end in primer.

  1. Fit the grafted fenders, hood, headlights, kidney grilles and bumper with its carrier and supports; Tourings built from 09/2001 need the M3 bumper's fender supports added (Front end on a 4-door body). Keep the bumper's lower opening and ducting: the oil cooler breathes through it (MotoIQ).
  2. If the M3 headlights differ from your Touring's (xenon against halogen), check their wiring now: xenon lamps need BMW's xenon light module and two level sensors. The light module is the last coding session, at the end of this phase, and you aim the lamps then, at ride height; don't drive after dark before that.

Before the first start.

  1. Fill the engine with 6.5 L (6.9 US qt) of 10W-60, BMW's figure after a rod-bearing job (BMW SI B11 04 04), and the power-steering reservoir with ATF, to about 25 mm below its edge with the engine off; then bleed it after the start as Brakes and bleeding describes. One build's pump rattled dry at its first start until the ATF went in (M346 Projects – Pt 13 first start (2024), 08:00). Look under the car for drips.
  2. Charge the battery and keep it on a charger of at least 10 A for the whole session. One swap's first start failed on a flat battery (Tenza Motorsports – first start (2021), 03:55).
  3. Fit a mechanical oil-pressure gauge at the oil-pressure switch's port, which is threaded M12 × 1.5 (Flow compilation, p.58). On a tee, the switch stays connected and the red cluster lamp gives you a second reading.
  4. Fit the fuel-pressure gauge at the S54's test point, the threaded fitting on the regulator housing under the left front floor (filter cover off; BMW adapter 13 5 220), and tie it where you can read it. The rail has no port: BMW puts "the fuel pressure gage at the pressure test point at the fuel filter" (BMW ST055, MS S54, p.41, BMW ST041, part 2, Test the fuel system).
  5. Ignition on, engine off: in Tool32 load MSS54DS0.PRG, run IDENT and FS_LESEN, and save both results. This is step 1 of the manual's Session 6, which the rest of this phase follows (MSS54 job reference).
  6. Coolant, with the ignition on (steps 9 and 10 of Fill and bleed the cooling system). Engine off. With IHKA: heat at maximum, blower low, A/C off. With IHKR: blower at 1 and the temperature dial fully right, since at 0 the valve is energized shut. That holds the heater valve open and runs the M3 valve's pump, if you fitted it. After a few minutes, top up to the cold mark and crack the vent screw until coolant runs without bubbles; refit it at 2.5 Nm (22 in-lb) (BMW ST054, engine cooling, BMW ST054, IHKR).

Prime the oil.

  1. Stop fuel and sparks: pull the fuel-pump relay (K96) and the injector relay (K6327, ETK), and unplug the six ignition coils. On the S54 the injector relay is what powers the injectors (BMW ST055).
  2. Test the start interlock: with the clutch up, the starter must not turn; with it down, it cranks. That's the clutch switch's wire to EWS pin 8, fitted to US and Japanese cars (BMW ST051).
  3. Crank in short bursts, with pauses to let the starter cool, until the gauge shows oil pressure and holds it while cranking and the red oil lamp goes out. The tachometer should move while you crank: the DME sees engine speed (the manual's steps 30–32).
  4. Refit the relays and the coil plugs.

Reset the adaptations and let the throttles learn. Do steps 2 to 5 of Session 6: clear the adaptations and the faults from cranking with the relays out, let the throttles run their key-on self-test, and check that STAT_WDK_ADAPT_WERT reads 0 and the clutch, brake and Sport inputs respond (BMW ST041, part 1). Then, with the key on, the pump primes: check 5.0 ± 0.2 bar (72.5 ± 2.9 psi), and look along the lines, the filter-regulator and the rail for leaks.

Start it.

  1. Start without touching the accelerator. Watch the oil gauge first: pressure must show at once. If it doesn't, switch off.
  2. Let it idle. Top up the power steering and bleed it: full lock each way twice, never held there (Brakes and bleeding). Look for fuel, oil, coolant and power-steering leaks, and for exhaust leaks at each joint while they're still cold (listen, or spray soapy water on them), and listen for knocking or VANOS rattle.
  3. Bleed the cooling system as it warms (Fill and bleed the cooling system, steps 11–14; steps 9 and 10 came before the start). Idle about one minute with the cap off, top up and fit the cap. Then watch the coolant in Tool32, not the gauge, which shows oil temperature: STATUS_MOTORTEMPERATUR for the engine and STATUS_KUEHLW_AUSL_TEMPERATUR for the radiator outlet. The outlet should climb steadily once the engine passes about 80 °C (176 °F). Run STEUERN_E_LUEFTER to check that the electric fan runs.
  4. At hot idle, check:
    • oil pressure at least 0.7 bar (10 psi), a figure from the Flow compilation, p.49 to confirm in TIS;
    • fuel pressure below 5 bar with the vacuum hose connected; BMW's diagram shows 3.8 bar with part-throttle vacuum (BMW ST041, part 2). Pull the hose: the pressure returns to 5.0 ± 0.2 bar, and the hose is dry inside; fuel in it means a leaking regulator diaphragm (our check);
    • a steady idle, and fuel trims (STATUS_LAMBDA_ADD_1 and _2) near zero. A positive value means the DME is adding fuel to make up for a lean mixture (BMW ST041, part 3).
  5. Still warm, with the coolant at 85 °C (185 °F) or more, run the VANOS timing and leak jobs (Session 6, step 7) and compare them with the donor's readings from Phase 1. BMW publishes no limits; owners and ISTA give about 180–300 ms adjustment time (ISTA's limit 500 ms) and a leak test within about ±5 °KW, with no "weggedriftet" status (manual).
  6. Read the faults in every module. Expect only location 1 (0x01), the pump fault, and, after a delete, possibly the immobilizer's 130 (0x82), which doesn't stop the engine starting (NAM3). Fix anything else before you drive. If it runs for a few seconds and then dies, that isn't the immobilizer: see the manual's Won't start. A brief fire while cranking that never catches is: see Immobilizer (EWS).
  7. Switch off and let the coolant cool to 30 °C (86 °F) or below. Crack the vent screw: a hiss of air means another heat cycle, and two are usual (step 13 of Fill and bleed the cooling system). Top up to the cold mark and check the oil.
  8. Refit the oil-pressure switch. Take off the mechanical gauge and its tee and screw the switch back into its port at 27 Nm (20 ft-lb) (Torque values). At the next key-on the red lamp lights, and it goes out once the engine runs, with no oil at the switch.

Shake it down, align it, then finish the coding.

  1. Brakes: with a firm pedal, make progressive stops on a quiet road, then a careful hard stop from moderate speed. ABS should pulse and the car stop straight. Bleed again after the first few drives (NAM3). Bed in the parking-brake shoes on an empty road (Brakes and bleeding).
  2. Wheel speeds: in INPA's DSC status, all four should agree while rolling. An M3 built before 09/2002 has sensors that don't suit your harness. If a speed is missing or the ABS lamp stays on, read the DSC fault memory before you go further: 5D90–5DC5 are the wheel-speed faults, and the last digit points to wiring, seating, the pulse wheel or tire size (manual).
  3. Short drives near home, then check the paint marks, wheel-bolt torque, fluid levels and fault memory.
  4. Fuel gauge: starting near empty, add a measured amount and check that the gauge, the range and Tool32's KOMBI46R.PRG → STATUS_AIF_TANKDATEN_LESEN follow it (STATUS_TANKINHALT_LESEN belongs to the older cluster's KOMBI46.PRG). With the M3 delivery unit and left sender in your tank, the cluster reads BMW's own M3 sender pair in a tank of the same 63 L (16.6 US gal); with your Touring's senders, nobody has reported the reading. The reserve lamp should come on with about 8 L (2.1 US gal) left, and the leak test relies on the reading (manual).
  5. Speedometer: compare with GPS. The M3 cluster over-reads by about 8.9% by design (e46fanatics).
  6. Ride height and alignment: after 5–10 miles, load the car to BMW's normal position for an M3: a full tank, 68 kg (150 lb) on each front seat and 14 kg (31 lb) in the middle of the cargo floor. Check the ride height, rim flange to arch edge: BMW's 605 mm front and 587 mm rear on 18-inch wheels (619 and 600 mm on 19s), ±10 mm, left and right within 10 mm (After the build). Then load it as in Phase 0 and check the roof and jacking points against your Phase 0 readings for Massachusetts. Torque the front anti-roll-bar clamp nuts, 21 Nm (15 ft-lb), with the car on its wheels at the M3 load; everything else at the front was torqued on stands in Phase 8. Then have the car aligned to BMW's E46 M3 figures in BMW's design position: the M3 load, plus weights near the struts until each corner is within 2 mm of BMW's ride height. Tell the shop not to use the rig's ride-height-input mode, which BMW bars for M cars (Wheel alignment, Shop briefs).
  7. Then calibrate the steering-angle sensor (Session 7) and run the other two DSC compensation routines, pressure sensors and lateral acceleration, with the wheel straight, no pressure on the brake and the car level (DSC, brakes and steering angle). It comes after the alignment, not before, because the calibration takes the wheel's position at that moment as straight ahead (Evan Goyuk – E46 steering-angle calibration in INPA (2020), 02:48).
  8. Vehicle-order changes and body modules (Session 8): none need swap coding if you kept your Touring's vehicle order. M Track doesn't need a stored change either: keep $7MA out of the stored order. If you do change the order, change it in the light module (ALSZ) only, since the cluster keeps the donor's; code only the modules it touches, one at a time and never with Code Car, and reset the DME adaptations again only after an engine-side change.
  9. Headlights (Session 9): halogen M3 lamps in a halogen Touring need no coding; check the bulbs and that the light module stores no lamp faults. Xenon lamps need BMW's xenon light module, fitted new or virginized, and two level sensors. Then aim them, at ride height.
  10. A/C: have a shop fit the new drier, set the oil, evacuate the system for at least 30 minutes, with no more than 7 kPa (2 inHg) of change in a 5-minute hold, and charge it by weight to the underhood label; then run the compressor in (Shop briefs). Then run BMW's checks: the compressor engages (STAT_AC_EIN and STAT_KO_EIN read 1); in BMW's efficiency test the evaporator reaches 15 °C (59 °F) or less within 3–4 minutes; the low side reads 1–2 bar (15–30 psi) and the high side 10–15 bar (150–225 psi); the centre vent blows 4–20 °C (40–68 °F), at least 11 °C (20 °F) below the outside air (A/C checks and pass values, worksheet). If the compressor never engages, start with the climate control's coded compressor lock (manual).

Break in the engine and set the readiness monitors.

  1. Drive 1,200 miles (1,930 km) below 5,500 rpm and 105 mph (169 km/h), BMW's figures after new rod bearings (BMW SI B11 04 04). Include closed-throttle coast-downs in gear, so the fuel cuts off: that's when the DME learns the crankshaft wheel, and its misfire detection is less sensitive until it has (BMW ST041, part 3).
  2. Checks during the break-in. BMW's bulletin gives none, and it says no oil service is needed at the end of the break-in (same SI). Our suggestion, logged on the break-in worksheet: at every fuel stop, the oil level and a look for leaks; after the first few drives, the paint marks, wheel-bolt torque, fluid levels and fault memory, and a second brake bleed; after the first few heat cycles, the coolant level; at about the halfway mark, every module's faults again; at 1,200 miles, the oil and filter.
  3. Change the oil and filter at the end of the break-in (our recommendation, not BMW's), and look for metal in the drained oil and the filter.
  4. Don't clear codes or disconnect the battery in the weeks before an inspection: both reset the readiness monitors (NYVIP3). Drive the MSS54 readiness plan in Inspection readiness and the manual. The fuel-tank leak test is the slow one: it runs with the engine off after at least 20 minutes of driving that followed at least 5 hours parked, with the tank 15–85% full, and only every second time those conditions are met (BMW ST041, part 3). The DME reads the fuel level from the cluster, so check the gauge first.

Watch: M346 Projects – Pt 13 first start (2024), 03:27 primes the oil before refitting the pump fuse; Tenza Motorsports – first start (2021), 05:38; Evan Goyuk – E46 steering-angle calibration in INPA (2020), 02:48.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails
Oil before firing The gauge shows pressure while cranking with fuel and sparks disabled Stop. Check the oil level, the pickup tube's O-ring and the pump before cranking again
Start interlock The starter turns only with the clutch down The clutch-switch wire to EWS pin 8
Throttles STAT_WDK_ADAPT_WERT = 0 after the reset; steady idle Repeat the reset with the battery on charge; check the throttle wiring
Shifts Revs drop cleanly between gears Rev hang: check the clutch-switch chain first, then that the DME runs manual software. In one non-M automatic-to-manual swap the cause was a tune written for an automatic (e46fanatics)
Hot oil pressure At least 0.7 bar at hot idle (compilation figure; confirm in TIS) Switch off and find the cause before you drive
Oil-pressure switch Refitted at 27 Nm with the gauge off; no oil at the port; the red lamp lights at key-on and goes out running Re-tighten; check the switch and its port for damage
Fuel 5.0 ± 0.2 bar at key-on; lower at idle with vacuum, and back to 5.0 ± 0.2 bar with the hose pulled; no leaks Vacuum hose, regulator, then the Phase 7 checks
Cooling In Tool32 (the M3 gauge shows oil), the radiator-outlet temperature rises once the engine passes about 80 °C; no fault 96 (0x60); no hiss at the vent screw when cold, usually after two heat cycles; the electric fan runs on STEUERN_E_LUEFTER and with the A/C on at idle Bleed again; with the M3 heater valve, check its pump's wiring and coding. Fault 96 (0x60): the radiator-outlet sensor's plug and hose, then the thermostat (Cooling checks and pass values)
Brakes and ABS Firm pedal; ABS pulses in a hard stop; the car stops straight Bleed again with INPA's routine. ABS lamp or a missing wheel speed: read the DSC fault memory (manual)
Ride height and alignment At the M3 load: BMW's ride height ±10 mm, left and right within 10 mm. At your Phase 0 load: roof and jacking points within 50.8 mm (2 in) of Phase 0. Printouts before and after, with every value inside BMW's E46 M3 tolerances, set in BMW's design position (Wheel alignment) Ride height off: springs wrong for the axle load (After the build). A value the shop can't reach: a bent part, a top mount on the wrong side, the wrong ride height, or a bushed joint torqued at the wrong height
Steering angle Calibrated after the alignment; INPA reads 0° with the wheel straight (Evan Goyuk – E46 steering-angle calibration in INPA (2020), 03:19); DSC lamp out Recalibrate; a sensor that won't hold 0° may be faulty (DSC, brakes and steering angle)
A/C The compressor engages; the evaporator reaches 15 °C (59 °F) or less within 3–4 minutes in BMW's test; low side 1–2 bar, high side 10–15 bar; centre vent 4–20 °C (40–68 °F), at least 11 °C (20 °F) below the outside air Never engages: the coded compressor lock, then the cluster's gateway and relay K19 (manual). Cools poorly: have the shop recover and weigh the charge
Break-in 1,200 miles below 5,500 rpm and 105 mph done; the checks along the way logged; oil changed; no metal in the oil or filter Metal: stop driving and find its source
Readiness A generic scanner shows every monitor ready. New York, for example, fails a 2001-or-later car with more than one not ready (NYVIP3) Fuel-tank leak test stuck: check its conditions, the leak-test wiring and the filler-neck seal (Inspection readiness)
Fault memory Only location 1 (0x01), the pump fault, and possibly 130 (0x82) after an EWS delete Troubleshooting

Phase 13: Paint, trim and paperwork

  1. Final bodywork: filler, guide coat, block sanding and panel gaps. Over the arch seams use only a skim of filler, so the arch keeps its crisp edge (Arch graft step by step, step 16).
  2. Paint. Most builders paint the whole car so the new arches and front panels match. Brief the paint shop on what you've prepared, the colour, and whether the jambs and engine bay are included (Shop briefs).
  3. Fit trim and badges, the side skirts (with M3 rocker clips), the mirrors (on adapter bases if they're M3 mirrors) and the rear bumper with its quad-tip cut-outs (Rear bumper, skirts and trim).
    • The Touring's tailgate opening drops lower than the M3 bumper allows, so builders graft the Touring bumper's center section into the M3 bumper (Tracks and Trails – bodywork (2026), 28:00).
    • Facelift Touring doors use ribbon-cable mirror wiring; M3 mirrors need the older door harness (M346 Projects – Pt 21 (2024), 00:20).
    • If you flared the doors, their rubbing strips need reshaping to follow the flare (Calvin's Car Diary – PT9 (2020), 04:20).
  4. Pre-inspection check:
    • all lights, side markers and rear reflectors (keep the reflectors on the modified bumper), and headlight aim;
    • horn, wipers and washers;
    • brakes, parking brake and tires;
    • ABS, DSC, airbag and check-engine lamps light at key-on and then go out;
    • no exhaust leaks;
    • readiness monitors set, and your Touring's VIN in the DME: Tool32 shows it, and a generic scanner does if the DME reports it (no rule required that before the 2005 model year; Inspection readiness).
  5. Inspection, registration and insurance (Registration and legal). In California the car goes to a BAR Referee first (BAR).
  6. Once it has passed, sell the fallback parts.

Watch: M346 Projects – making an E46 M3 Touring rear bumper (2024), 00:20.

Done when

Check Pass If it fails

Inspection Passed; in California, the Referee label fitted Fix what the inspector lists; for an emissions fail, see Inspection readiness
Paperwork Registration and title updated as your state requires; agreed-value insurance in place Keep receipts, photos and the donor's paperwork together for the insurer

Deep dive: chassis and drivetrain

This chapter explains how and why for each mechanical job. Torques appear at the step that needs them; the full table is in Torque values, oils and capacities are in Fluids and capacities, and single-use fasteners are in Consumables and single-use parts. Values marked "Flow" come from a forum compilation of RealOEM and BMW TIS printouts, not from BMW itself (Flow PDF, via NAM3). Where TIS gives a figure, use TIS. Group numbers such as "TIS 11 24" point you to BMW's own procedure.

Rear subframe mount reinforcement

What cracks. The floor panel the rear subframe bolts to (the rear axle carrier panel, RACP), not the subframe itself. Torque reversals from the diff flex the mounts; the spot welds fail first, then cracks spread through the floor (CMP, part 1). BimmerWorld describes the floor as two sheets with a gap between them, with the mount gussets tack-welded to the bottom sheet only, and says most cracks begin at three rosette welds on top of the rear-most mounts (BimmerWorld). Worn subframe bushings add movement and fatigue.

Why do it on a Touring. CMP says every E46 built after about February 2000 shares the same RACP, with cracks common on coupes, sedans, Tourings and convertibles (CMP, part 1, part 2). BMW's catalog agrees: the US 325i Touring, the sedan and the M3 coupe list the same RACP repair panel (41117000246), and the Touring and sedan share the trunk floor (41127062570), rails and battery tray. Only the rear-seat backrest differs, where a Touring cross member (41148253150) takes the place of the sedan's partition (ETK: floor, trunk floor, partition). So a 2007 forum claim that the wagon floor is "slightly different… for more cargo space" doesn't hold at the mounts, and its "the subframe mounting points are not reinforced" only means no stronger than the sedan's. Tourings do crack, among them an Alpina B3 3.3 Touring "with extensive subframe cracks" (e46fanatics). Your conversion feeds M3 torque into a body without the M3's extra gussets, weld points and C-pillar reinforcement (BMW ST041), and CMP says failures are worst on M3s. No source calls reinforcement mandatory, but by Phase 5 the exhaust, driveshaft, subframe and tank are already out, which is most of the labor.

Check your own floor. Look for cracks close to each mount, at the ends of the panel's V-shaped beam, along the spot welds joining the chassis rails to the boot floor, and along the RACP's front edge (CMP, part 2). A 2001–05 Touring has the later mount insert, which CMP identifies by two rectangular indents on the vertical face in front of the rear mounts; on these cars cracks spread through the RACP rather than tearing the insert out (CMP, part 1). If the floor is badly torn, BMW's repair is the whole 21.3 kg RACP (41117000246), a body-shop job, and it's discontinued: BMWPartsDeal marks it "This part is discontinued" (last price $1,304.68, October 2026), so ask a dealer whether a successor exists (ETK, BMWPartsDeal, Turner).

Kits and the Touring. No kit maker publishes Touring-specific cargo-side plates or instructions. The steel is the sedan's, so sedan-pattern plates should land in the same places, but dry-fit and trace before you cut. On one Touring, parts of a kit wouldn't fit because the Touring has no partition wall behind the rear seat (Calvin's Car Diary – PT15 (2025), 30:00).

Kit Touring fitment Cargo-side (topside) parts
CMP Stage 1 underside plates "All E46 non-M, E46 M3 (Excluding Hatch)" (CMP) None
CMP Stage 1.5 Chassis Rail Plates Same wording (CMP) Tie the RACP to the rails under the boot trim; 2.5 mm zinc-coated steel
CMP Stage 2 rear weld-in RACP beam Same wording; fit Stage 1.5 first (CMP) A beam welded in from above
CMP front weld-in beam No: coupes and sedans with split folding seats only (CMP) —
Redish/PS Designs V3 Not named; used on two Touring conversions (Autoalex – build part 3 (2023), 14:20, Tracks and Trails – Touring RACP (2025), 01:20) Four pieces fitted from above (Hack Engineering) and plates tying the RACP to the chassis legs; £180 for the plates plus £125 for six replica tank and brake-pipe brackets, July 2023 (Autoalex, 16:20)
Turner TDR4675412 Rogue lists the wagon (Rogue) New sheet metal for the mount tops (Turner, unverified)
Properparts 99–06 "Convertible, Coupe, Sedan and Wagon"; 16-gauge (1.5 mm) (Properparts) Not stated
DriftShop Competition Every E46 except the Compact; a buyer says there are no instructions (DriftShop) Not stated
BimmerWorld, Garagistic, Revshift All E46; Touring not named (BimmerWorld, Garagistic, Revshift) Plates to close trunk-floor windows
Condor plate kit "E46 coupe & sedan"; Touring not listed (Condor – plate install, coupe (2019), description) Two square trunk block-off plates; 14-gauge plates

Vorshlag trunk frame-to-floor kit Non-M and M3; Touring not named (Vorshlag) Fitted after the mounts are reinforced, through a section cut from the upper trunk floor

Sources disagree on whether the cargo-side work is needed on cars built after early 2000. PS Designs makes its trunk-floor plates optional on them (PS Designs/Redish); BimmerWorld says "Partial reinforcement (skipping the trunk portion) is not advised" (BimmerWorld). With M3 torque going in and the floor already open, do it.

Where the mounts sit. On the Touring, as on the sedan, the rear mounts sit under the front edge of the steel spare-wheel well, beside each chassis rail, and the front mounts sit under the rear-seat base. CMP reaches the tops of the rear mounts by cutting away the front of the well within 120 mm (5 in) of each rail. In front of the well the RACP is spot-welded to the rails along a flange, and behind the mounts it joins the crumple structure on each side of the well (CMP, part 2). In the cargo area only trim covers this: Touring base panels, cover lids, a right-hand tray and side trims (ETK: cargo trim). If you take the well out (options 1–3 in Exhaust and the spare-wheel well), you reach the tops of the rear mounts through that opening instead of cutting separate windows.

Procedure (assembled from the Garagistic, Morehead, BimmerWorld and CMP instructions and two Touring builds). It is one sequence with the floor work in Exhaust and the spare-wheel well: the floor closes only after the axle and muffler have been tried in place.

  1. Prepare as in Welding settings and safety: fuel system and battery out, fire watch, fume extraction, test coupons. Strip the cargo trim, carpet, sound deadening and rear seat to bare steel.
  2. Measure the body diagonals before the first weld (same section).
  3. Strip the underside: exhaust, driveshaft, rear subframe and suspension, fuel tank, underbody panels and liners near the welds (Morehead). The plates can't be worked past the tank (Tracks and Trails – Touring RACP (2025), 02:00).
  4. Inspect all four mounts from below, as above.
  5. Clean to bare metal around each mount: paint, seam sealer and factory coating all come off. Clean mill scale off the plates and grind zinc coating off where you'll weld.
  6. Repair before reinforcing. Drill a small hole at the tip of any crack to stop it, weld the crack, and repair failed spot welds (Morehead).
  7. Underside plates. Each large plate fits one mount; test-fit and mark them. Tack the kit's spacers first, then the plates, with weld-through primer on their backs (Tracks and Trails – Touring RACP (2025), 07:20). Plug-weld through the plate's holes; over a double-skinned area, "drill through the first layer of sheet metal only" so the plate fuses to the structure behind (Garagistic K0536). Weld the perimeter in short stitches, moving between mounts to spread the heat.
  8. Open the floor by the cut rules in Exhaust and the spare-wheel well: drill the well's spot welds from the cargo side and lift it out downward, keeping the rail, RACP and rear-panel flanges whole. CMP's 120 mm (5 in) is the strip of the well it cuts away beside each rail to reach the mount tops, not a zone to avoid; what you must never cut or grind through is a flange. If you keep the well, cut BimmerWorld's windows instead: butt the trunk plate against the seam across the floor, trace it, and cut about ¼ in (6 mm) inside the line (BimmerWorld).
  9. Topside welds. First check every spot weld the well was hiding: those nearest the rails and the front "commonly let go first and are not visibly failed from beneath the car" (CMP, part 2). On each rear mount, weld the three rosette welds on top, then weld the upper and lower layers together at each existing spot weld (BimmerWorld). Stitch failed spot welds along the rail-to-RACP flange (CMP, part 2), then fit the rail plates: CMP's, or Redish's, which Tracks and Trails welded from inside the trunk (Tracks and Trails – Touring RACP (2025), 11:20). CMP's Stage 2 beam follows the rail plates.
  10. Front mounts. Their top welds sit under the rear-seat cushion, and CMP calls them "often neglected" (CMP, part 2). Tracks and Trails drilled out the rear-seat tabs to reach them and welded over the factory welds (Tracks and Trails – Touring RACP (2025), 05:40), and Redish reinforces "underneath the rear seat panel" on Tourings (Autoalex – build part 3 (2023), 04:00). Patch any opening you cut.
  11. V-brace mounting boxes, if you'll fit the M3 V-brace (below).
  12. Mock up before you close the floor. Hang the M3 rear axle and muffler in place, or leave the floor open until the Phase 6 mock-up, so the floor height and hangers suit the exhaust. Check them, and your canister, against the figures you took off the donor (pass values).
  13. Close the floor: plug-weld it down through the drilled 8 mm (5/16 in) holes at the factory spot-weld positions (see Exhaust and the spare-wheel well).
  14. Measure the diagonals again and compare them with your first readings.
  15. Protect it: epoxy primer, seam sealer on every joint (both sides), a body plug in every hole, underbody coating outside and cavity wax inside (Tracks and Trails – Touring rear end (2025), 09:40). If you want BMW's structural foam in the mount cavities, inject it last: foam makes later welding "more difficult and dangerous" (BimmerWorld). Trim the cargo carpet if it no longer lies flat.

Weld, don't glue. Morehead: "Do not attempt to epoxy reinforcements… It does not work." BimmerWorld calls glue pointless because the mount tops must be welded anyway. One Touring builder bonded his plates with panel adhesive (M346 Projects – pt 14 (2024), 23:00); nobody has compared the two, and the kit instructions say weld.

Push rod, V-brace and spacers. The M3 subframe comes with a tubular steel push rod (front crossmember, 33312229295) in place of the non-M cast-aluminium part, bolted to the body with four M8 bolts (ETK: M3 carrier, Morehead). Fit it with your kit's spacer plates, which make up for the plate thickness; PS Designs calls them "ESSENTIAL" and gives 25 Nm for the four bolts; BMW's figure for its M8 8.8 screws is 21 Nm (TIS 33 32 17AZ), which we use (PS Designs/Redish). The M3 also has a V-shaped brace (33312229899) that "connects the rear axle carrier to the body" (BMW ST041), held by three M10×35 10.9 bolts at 59 Nm + 90° (ETK, PS Designs/Redish). Your body has nowhere to bolt it: "on the non-M models, there's nothing there" (Tracks and Trails – Touring rear end (2025), 06:00), and Redish says the Touring has grommets where the M3 has M10 threaded receivers (Autoalex – build part 3 (2023), 05:20). Builders added the mounting boxes in four ways: cut the donor's boxes off and plug-weld them at the factory weld points, a full day's work (Tracks and Trails, 06:20); bought an aftermarket lower box, "like a hundred bucks" (07:40); had new boxes fabricated (Autoalex v2 – update (2024), 04:20); or used the brackets in M3Projekts' kit (M3projekts – trunk floor (2023), 10:00). The boxes carry axle loads, so weld them as carefully as the plates, with the floor still open.

Stiffer subframe mounts. BimmerWorld recommends urethane or solid subframe mounts "even on street cars", noting that BMW's bracing of the front mounts only moved the stress elsewhere (BimmerWorld). Stiffer mounts pass the subframe's load into the floor more directly, so fit them only with the full underside and topside reinforcement.

Warning

Garagistic and Morehead recommend professional installation, and BimmerWorld recommends an experienced, professional shop. You will be welding thick plate to thin sheet, partly overhead. Practise on coupons first (see Welding settings and safety). Tracks and Trails spent about CAD 2,300 doing it himself, including a new welder, against a CAD 2,500 shop quote (November 2025), and concluded "for this, take it to a shop" (Tracks and Trails – Touring RACP (2025), 13:00). If you use a shop, give it the brief in Shop briefs.

Watch: Tracks and Trails – Touring RACP (2025), 07:20, Tedward – subframe cracks (2020), 10:57 (E46 M3 trunk-floor step; chapters only checked), O'Leary's – reinforcement done right (2024), 08:07, Condor – plate install, coupe (2019), description (Condor's kit lists the coupe and sedan only, not the Touring). Read: StanceWorks DIY and the photo instructions from Garagistic and BimmerWorld.

Exhaust and the spare-wheel well

On a non-M E46 the M3's transverse rear muffler sits where the spare-wheel well is. BMW had to make room on the M3 too: the coupe's boot floor was modified for the larger silencer, whose mounts sit "on the outer ends of the under body" (BMW ST041), and an M Mobility tire kit replaced the spare wheel to free space for a "40 liter half-shell muffler with four outlets" (BMW S54 module). Petroyle cuts the Touring's well out and inserts a carbon-fiber panel (Autocar).

The two floors. Your Touring's trunk floor (41127062570) is the deep-well floor BMW fits to every non-M E46, sedan and coupe included (ETK). The M3's floor (41127895619) keeps a shallow well at the front, where a foam moulding holds the M Mobility kit (BMW ST041): "a little bit of a hump" that then "tails off" (Redish – Touring build part 1 (2022), 05:49). Its rear part is flat, "so there is enough space for the large exhaust under it" (M3projekts – trunk floor (2023), 17:14). Everything around the floor is shared: the rails, side floors, battery tray, wheelhouse extension, canister brackets, jack bracket and ground pin carry the same part numbers on both cars. What differs is the floor pressing, the M3's front reinforcement (51717894229), two of the three muffler brackets, and the Touring's spare-wheel bracket (ETK: Touring, M3). So the M3 floor replaces yours part for part, on the same flanges. We infer that from the catalog; M346 found that "they all match up" (M346 Projects – pt 14 (2024), 00:40).

What's in the well now, and where it goes. BMW USA lists a space-saver spare as standard on the 2003 Sport Wagon, with about 57 L (2 cu ft) of extra room under the cargo floor (BMW USA). The load floor lifts out to reach the spare and the "control module mounting area located beneath" it (BMW ST034). Photograph it all before anything comes out.

Item, US 325i Touring BMW number When the M3 floor goes in
