A new-steel route. The convertible quarter plus its inner lateral trim panel makes a full set of new BMW arch steel.

  • Cost: about €2,120 per side, or about €4,280 for both sides plus an M3 filler flap (51172695524, €45.06), at eStore-Central's October 2026 prices before shipping (eStore-Central). It shows no stock levels, so ask before you order. In the US, BMWPartsDeal listed the same panels at $2,105.60 a side panel and $127.54 (left) or $118.80 (right) an inner trim panel on 22 October 2026: about $2,230 a side before freight and tax, or about $5,309 for both arches plus the new M3 trunk floor and its reinforcement (our arithmetic). Each page said "Ships in 1-3 Business Days", but stock isn't confirmed until you order. The coupe route, quarter plus interior side frame, comes to about €7,724 or $8,240 per side.
  • Title: no donor steel goes into your body, which by our reading of the statute removes the Massachusetts "reconstructed" question for the arches (Massachusetts).
  • Rust: a new skin has no hidden rust in its lip.

Check the steel before you cut.

  • Shape. Take the donor's rear bumper off, then make the section templates and record the station offsets as Datum, stations and templates describes. Left and right should agree within 3 mm (our suggestion). A test fit of an M3 rear bumper end and the filler flap is a quick first look.
  • Damage. M346's donor quarters had been in an accident and curled in at the bottom; they needed a fender roller, and the rear bumper had to move in and forward to meet the new flares (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 58:40).
  • Margin. Cut 40–50 mm (1.6–2.0 in) outside the seam lines you'll use on the Touring (Flare profile): from the donor's door shut line back past 600 mm behind the axle, and from the sill to just above the shoulder crease, keeping the factory spot-welded lip intact. If you'll graft the donor's inner tub, "make sure to cut as much of the wheel tub as possible… if you don't have that you're going to have a gap" (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 33:00). On the right side, take the filler surround and flap.

Measure and mock up before you cut

The arches are welded around this mock-up for good, so have the final springs, dampers, wheels and tires in hand first; the choices are in Suspension for Touring weight. It matters: on the M3's springs and dampers, Tenza's Touring, which kept its standard arches, sat so low that its wider rear tires rubbed (Tenza Motorsports – Coilover install (2022), 00:40).

BMW's ride height for the M3. TIS measures it from the bottom middle of the rim flange straight up to the lower edge of the wheel arch, in BMW's normal position (TIS 33 00, TIS 31 00). For an M3, BMW's normal position is a full tank, 68 kg (150 lb) on each front seat and 14 kg (31 lb) in the middle of the trunk (TIS 32 00, Suspension for Touring weight).

Axle 18-inch wheels 19-inch wheels Tolerance
Rear 587 mm (23.1 in) 600 mm (23.6 in) ±10 mm; left and right within 10 mm of each other
Front 605 mm (23.8 in) 619 mm (24.4 in) ±10 mm; left and right within 10 mm of each other

Use it two ways: to vet the donor before you copy its stance, and to set the mock-up height if the donor fails. The arch opening is the same height on both cars (Rear arches and doors), so the same reading taken on your Touring, with the M3 wheels fitted, puts its rear hubs where an M3's sit. BMW's figures for the Touring itself, at its own load, are your Phase 0 baseline, not a mock-up target (BMW's figures). As one forum member warns, "You will never be able to accurately place the tape in the exact center of the rim" (NAM3), so take each reading twice.

Flare profile

This is how far the M3 skin stands out from the Touring's at each station, measured along the car from the rear axle line. The figures are our measurements from BMW's dimension drawing of the M3 coupe and a drawing of the Touring scaled to BMW's published dimensions (M3 coupe drawing, Touring drawing). They're good to about ±5–10 mm.

Your own offsets and templates, taken on both cars, set the targets you work to. The table tells you what to expect. If one of your readings is more than 10 mm away from it, measure again before you trust it (our suggestion).

Station M3 skin proud of the Touring's What's there
400 mm ahead of the axle 0–9 mm The flare starts 380–420 mm ahead. Any difference here is the coupe's slightly wider body, which you don't graft
350 mm ahead About 16 mm The flare's ramp. The Touring's door edge meets the arch near here
300 mm ahead to 100 mm behind About 21–23 mm The full flare. Over the axle the lip itself moves out about 21 mm
150 mm behind About 25 mm From about 150–220 mm behind, the arch edge below the bumper line is the bumper cover
200–350 mm behind About 29–32 mm Mostly the M3 bumper corner, not steel (our inference)
400 mm behind About 22 mm Bumper corner
450 mm behind About 13 mm Bumper corner
500 mm behind About 10 mm Fading out
600 mm behind About 7 mm The coupe's and Touring's bodies differ slightly here

Going up, the flare fades out. At the axle station:

Height above the hub M3 skin proud of the Touring's
345 mm (the arch crown and lip) About 21 mm
385 mm About 16 mm
435 mm About 12 mm
465 mm About 6 mm
500 mm (the top seam) About 2 mm
525 mm About 0
540 mm (the shoulder crease) 0

The M3 bulge ends at a styling line that peaks about 475 mm above the hub, over the axle, and curves down at both ends. At the front it ends about 315 mm ahead of the axle and 375 mm above the hub. Behind the axle it runs down into the bumper's top line, about 300 mm behind the axle and 305 mm above the hub. Between the top of that line and the shoulder crease is a flat band only about 50–65 mm tall, and that's where the top seam goes.

Under the bumper (our inference). From about 150–220 mm behind the axle rearward, the bumper's top line meets the arch edge, and below it the surface on both cars is the bumper cover. Above the bumper, the steel flare tapers out between about 200 and 300 mm behind the axle. So the big figures from 200 to 450 mm behind are mostly how far the Touring's bumper corner must come out (Rear bumper, skirts and trim). The steel and lip hidden behind the bumper may need less. Measure the donor with its bumper off to find out.

Seam lines. We infer these from the same drawings; confirm them with templates.

  • Top seam: about 500–515 mm (19.7–20.3 in) above the hub, in the flat band, at least 25 mm under the shoulder crease.
  • Rear seam: about 550–600 mm (21.7–23.6 in) behind the axle. It runs straight down from the top seam to about 250 mm above the hub, where the bumper hides it. The Touring's tail-lamp starts about 700 mm behind the axle, so the seam stays at least 100 mm clear of the lamp pocket.
  • Front seam: 25–40 mm (1.0–1.6 in) behind the door shut line, parallel to it, down to the sill flange. If you'll carry the flare onto the door, the front joint goes on the door instead (Rear doors).
  • Donor cut: the same lines, 40–50 mm further out.

Datum, stations and templates

Measure both cars the same way, so their numbers compare.

  1. Level the shell. Support it on its four jacking pads. Level the sill pinch welds side to side and front to back with a digital level, and write the readings down.
  2. Snap a center line. Drop plumb bobs from matching left and right points: the centers of the four rear subframe mounting bolts on the rear axle carrier panel (41117000246, the same part on both cars, ETK) and the front subframe bolts. Mark the midpoint of each pair on the floor and snap a chalk line through them.
  3. Set a reference line. Set a cross-line laser parallel to the center line at a fixed distance, such as 950 mm, beside each rear wheel. Use the same distance on both cars.
  4. Mark the stations. Mark the rear axle line (the hub center) on the body, then every 100 mm from 400 mm ahead of it to 500 mm behind it.
  5. Take the offsets. At each station, measure from the laser line to the skin at two heights: at the lip, and 30 mm below the shoulder crease. Record them in the worksheet (donor, Touring). The Touring's reading minus the donor's, at the lip, is the move-out you need at that station.
  6. Make the templates. At seven stations (400, 300 and 150 mm ahead of the axle; at the axle; 150, 300 and 450 mm behind it), copy the section with a profile gauge onto 3 mm hardboard or stiff card. Make one set off the donor, with its bumper off, and one off the Touring, both before you cut. Label each with car, side and station.
  7. Template the lines. Tape on a side-view template of your cut lines and trace it. If you'll touch the door, make a tape-and-card template of its edge too. On Tracks and Trails' door template, "the tape outline's doing most of the work" (Tracks and Trails – What it really takes (2026), 16:20).
  8. Tram the body. Besides the body diagonals below, measure two cross-car distances with a tram gauge: lip crown to lip crown, and crease to crease at the axle station.

Pass: left and right agree within 3 mm at every station. That is our suggestion, not a BMW body figure: BMW's side-to-side ride-height tolerance in its design position is 2 mm, and body-measuring practice is about ±2–3 mm.

Measure both cars, then mock up

1. Measure the donor before you strip it (Phase 1). Put the M3 on level ground, loaded to its normal position (a full tank, 68 kg on each front seat and 14 kg in the middle of the trunk), its tires at placard pressure. At each rear corner (and the front corners too, for reference), measure:

  • BMW's ride height, rim flange to arch edge. Pass: the table above. Outside it, the donor's springs are tired or not stock, or its body is damaged: use BMW's figure as your target, not the donor's stance;
  • the height of the hub center above the floor;
  • the height of the arch lip straight above the hub center;
  • the height of a body point the Touring shares, such as the floor beside a rear subframe mount; the rear axle carrier panel there is the same part on both cars, 41117000246 (ETK);
  • how far the lip sits outboard of the tire's outer face, using a plumb line from the lip;
  • the gap from each rear bump stop to the damper body, and later, with the dampers out, each bump stop's free length. BMW publishes no wheel-travel or bump-stop figures for the E46 M3, so these tell you how much bump travel the mock-up has to clear.

Subtract to get hub-to-lip and hub-to-body for each side. Note the fuel level and photograph the tire placard. Later, with the bumper off and before you cut any steel (Phase 2), take the station offsets and make the templates.

2. Record the Touring before any welding. Note the ride height at all four corners (Phase 0), then:

  • Door gaps and flush. Mark three points along each rear door's trailing edge. At each, record the shut gap with feeler gauges, and the flush: lay a straightedge across the gap and measure under it with feeler gauges, noting whether the door sits in or out (worksheet). Your own readings are the target. They should fall inside BMW's E46 gaps: rear door to side wall 4 ± 0.75 mm, front door to rear door 4.5 ± 0.75 mm, doors to sill 5 ± 1 mm, each parallel within 1 mm (TIS 41 00).
  • Door-to-arch junction. Measure where the door's trailing edge meets the arch: how far ahead of the axle, and how high above the hub. Our estimate is 300–350 mm ahead and 150–250 mm up, ±50 mm.
  • Station offsets and templates, as on the donor.
  • Body diagonals. Pick fixed points you can find again, such as the four rear subframe mounts and the front subframe mounting points, and tape the two diagonals across each set. Measure again after every welding session, in Phase 5 as well as here; a change means the floor or body has pulled. BMW's control dimensions are in TIS 41 00 (Phase 5).

3. Mock up (Phase 6).

  1. Bolt the M3 rear axle in with the dampers you'll run, the brakes, and the final wheels and tires at road pressure. Leave the springs out.

  2. Jack each rear hub to its target height. With the springs out, the shell's missing weight doesn't matter: you set the suspension position directly instead of trying to load a stripped shell to ride height. Make sure the light shell can't lift off its stands as you jack.

    • If the donor passed BMW's check, match its hub-to-body figure. Check: the Touring's own arch then reads rim flange to arch edge within 10 mm of the donor's reading, because the openings match.
    • If it failed, set rim flange to arch edge on the Touring to BMW's figure: 587 mm on 18-inch wheels, 600 mm on 19-inch.
    • If your springs will set the car higher or lower, use your own target instead.
    • Pass: each side within 2 mm of its target, and left and right within 2 mm of each other, BMW's side-to-side tolerance in its design position. Jacks make that easy.

  3. Mark the new lip at each station: the donor's hub-to-lip height above the hub center, and the donor's move-out from your offsets, each within 3 mm.

  4. Check symmetry. Measure from each side's lip mark to the same center point on the floor, such as the middle of the rear axle carrier panel, and to the center line. Pass: within 3 mm side to side.

  5. Full bump. Jack the hub until the bump stop (M3 33532229777, ETK) is fully compressed. Turn the wheel by hand and check:

    • the tread to the planned lip;
    • the outer sidewall to the outer wheelhouse half and the lip flange;
    • the inner sidewall to the inner wheelhouse and the brake lines.

    Repeat at your planned static camber, and mark the tire's outer face and top on the body. Pass: at least 10 mm (0.4 in) to sheet metal everywhere. That's our suggestion; BMW publishes no rear wheel-travel figure for the M3. Also note how far each hub rose from its target height to full bump: subtracted from the new lip's hub-to-lip, it gives the full-bump figure for the loaded check in Phase 12 (After the build).

  6. Filler (right side). Hold the donor's filler surround at its marks. Check that your own filler pot sits in the M3 surround's opening. The pot, 51718208646, is the same part on the Touring and both M3s, so it stays where it is (our inference): only the surround and flap change (ETK: Touring, ETK: M3).

  7. Remove the mock-up axle before you weld.

Arch graft step by step

Weld as described in Welding settings and safety, with fume extraction, a fire watch, and the fuel tank, filler pipe and every fuel and EVAP part near the right-rear arch removed first. ETK lists a fuel expansion-tank bracket (41148196386) among the rear wheelhouse parts, so look inside the quarter for tanks and vent lines before you cut; keep the bracket, or move it to a new inner tub (ETK, Fuel system). The bracket carries the liquid-vapour separator (16136752641), which sits "in the right rear wheel well behind the trim" (BMW ST041 Part 3). Take it out with its vent hoses before you cut, refit both before the tank goes back in, and let the leak test prove them (Filler and EVAP).

BMW allows a panel to be sectioned only where its repair information supports it (I-CAR – Structural sectioning: BMW/Mini (2017)). BMW's own E46 procedure replaces a Touring's rear side wall whole, cut 200 mm below the roof edge on the C-pillar, at the D-pillar and at the sill, never around the arch (TIS 41 35 101, Touring, p.1, p.2). So an arch graft is not a BMW repair, and these sixteen steps come from the documented builds, I-CAR, BMW's own joint practice and our measurements. Each ends with the check that proves it. Figures marked as estimates come from scaled drawings (Flare profile): your own templates and offsets overrule them.

Before you cut.

  1. Record both cars before anything moves (Measure and mock up before you cut): the donor's ride height, offsets and templates, with its bumper off for the last two; the Touring's door gaps and flush, offsets, templates and body diagonals. Check: the donor reads 587 ± 10 mm rim flange to arch edge on 18-inch wheels (600 on 19-inch), left and right within 10 mm, or you've switched to BMW's figure; both cars have templates at all seven stations.

  2. Mock up with the M3 axle, final dampers and wheels, springs out and hubs at the target height. Check: each lip mark at the target height and move-out within 3 mm at every station, and at least 10 mm from tire to sheet metal at full bump (our suggestion).

  3. Choose the door treatment now (Rear doors). With a standard door, BMW's way, the M3 nose has to come in about 11–20 mm over its last 60–100 mm before the shut line (our estimate). With a flared door, the door's trailing edge comes out by the same amount. Check: the choice is made; it sets where the front seam goes.

  4. Mark the cut lines on the Touring from your side-view template (Flare profile). These positions are our inference from the drawings.

    • Top seam: about 500–515 mm (19.7–20.3 in) above the hub, at least 25 mm under the crease.
    • Rear seam: about 550–600 mm (21.7–23.6 in) behind the axle, at least 100 mm ahead of the tail-lamp, down to about 250 mm above the hub, where the bumper hides it. You don't need the donor's tail-light area.
    • Front seam: 25–40 mm behind the shut line and parallel to it, down to the door–arch junction. Below that only a narrow band of panel is left between the opening and the shut line, so run the seam along the shut line to the sill flange. SOS Customz ran its cut to the door at the shut line and lined it up with the filler-door area (SOS Customz (2023), 02:00).
    • Right side: if the top seam would cross the filler surround, step the line up and around it, so the whole M3 surround comes in with the section. M346 made "a big square cutout" around the filler on that side, and didn't need one on the other (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 55:40).

    Check: along every line, the donor and Touring templates agree within 1 mm, so the seam sits on matching panel. Where they don't, move the line.

Cut.

  1. Prepare the donor section. Cut it 40–50 mm outside your lines.

    • Drill, don't cut. Drill out the spot welds where you can instead of cutting, and count those along the lip: that's your plug-weld count in step 10.
    • Separate the skin from the inner arch panel it's welded to: the coupe's interior side frame (41217890677/678); on a convertible, the inner lateral trim panel (41217894553/554) or the interior side frame. Keep as much of the inner arch flange as you can (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 27:20). M3projekts cut its donor's fenders "together with part of the inner edge… drilled down at the point welds, leaving only the outer plate" (M3projekts – Ep8 (2023), 14:00).
    • Clean it. Grind the factory seam sealer off the donor's rolled lip, because it burns and spoils the weld ground (13:40), and grind off the zinc coating where you'll weld (11:00).

    Check: no rust in the lip's U-channel (Redish), and the section still fits its templates within 1 mm.

  2. Open the Touring. With the fuel system out, drill the arch-lip spot welds and remove the skin inside your lines, leaving the outer wheelhouse half (41218242355/356) in place. Tracks and Trails drilled the spot welds and removed only the outer skin, keeping as much healthy Touring wheelhouse as possible (Tracks and Trails – What it really takes (2026), 12:40). Grind the sound-deadening mat back about 25 mm (1 in) from the weld line so its glue doesn't contaminate the weld (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 41:20). Check: the outer half's flange is whole and straight, and the door still opens and shuts cleanly.

Inner arch and skin.

  1. Rebuild the inner arch first, before the skin goes on. This is the hardest joint: on a 325Ci coupe, one forum member called joining the inner fender to the wider M3 arch "the biggest issue" (e46fanatics). Two methods have been shown on Tourings:

    • Graft the donor's arch flange or inner tub. M346 bent the Touring's inner-tub lip, which "was originally pointed straight down", up with a hammer, and welded the M3 tub to the shell in one piece before the skin (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 30:20).
    • Extend the Touring's outer half outward with a fill strip, by the move-out at each station. Expect about 21 mm at the crown, 16–22 mm around 300–350 mm ahead of the axle, and up to 25–32 mm from 150 to 350 mm behind it (our estimates). From about 200 mm behind the axle rearward, under the bumper line, take the figure from the donor with its bumper off instead. The Touring's inner well "comes down a little bit lower" than the donor flare. Tracks and Trails bonded lip to lip with panel bond, hammered one section out into a new lip, bonded that to the flare and welded the rest, with weld-through primer on the back first (Tracks and Trails (2026), 17:40).

    Tack it, dry-fit the skin to check, then plug-weld or stitch in short runs and let each cool. Put weld-through primer on the faces that touch. Check: with the skin dry-fitted, the templates at the axle and 300 mm behind it still fit within 1 mm, and the quarter's corner by the bumper hasn't pulled in. A year on, M346 found that corner bent in, which he put down to the heat of welding the inner tub, and pulled it back out with a ratchet strap and heat (M346 Projects – Pt 23 (2025), 14:00, 14:40).

  2. Fit the skin. Trim the section to a butt gap of 0.8–1.0 mm, about one skin thickness; Tracks and Trails used a 1 mm gap (Tracks and Trails (2026), 15:40). Hold it with clecos or butt-weld clamps every 75–100 mm (3–4 in).

    • Joint: we recommend a butt joint over a backing strip of skin-thickness steel, which makes alignment and penetration easier. It's BMW's own practice on these bodies: its sectioned joints are butt joints over a backing strip about 60 mm wide on the Touring (40 mm at the coupe's pillars), pushed about 30 mm into each side and plug-welded through holes drilled in the body's side of the joint (TIS 41 35 101, Touring, p.8). I-CAR describes the same idea, with adhesive, on a 2017 X5 (I-CAR).
    • The alternative is a joggle: a step pressed into the old panel, plug-welded through punched holes, as SOS Customz did (SOS Customz (2023), 14:00). It's easier to align and forgives gaps. But it leaves a double layer that traps moisture unless it's sealed from inside, and a stepped seam takes more filler.
    • Right side: the filler. Graft the M3 filler surround with the section, and check that your own pot (51718208646) seats in the M3 opening. The pot and filler pipe are the same parts on both cars, so the pot stays where it is (our inference; Filler and EVAP). The M3 flap's bracket holes sit in different places because its door is a different shape. Some builders slot the holes, but M346 grafted the M3 surround in, matching its radius (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 37:00). The flap hinge differs: 51172695527 on the coupe, while the convertible's 51178151955 is also your Touring's (ETK).

    Checks: flush across every seam within 0.5 mm (0.02 in) before welding (our suggestion); the lip at its target within 3 mm; the door opens and closes; the bumper corner trial-fitted (Rear bumper, skirts and trim).

Weld.

  1. Tack. Tack the top seam first: the center, then the ends, then halve the gaps down to a 25–30 mm (1.0–1.2 in) pitch, about 30 tacks. Then tack the rear seam (the ends, then the middle) and the front seam (top, bottom, middle, then halves). Check: gap, flush, door and templates again. Adjust now, before any stitching.

  2. Weld the lip joint. Join the skin's lip flange to the inner flange with plug welds through 6 mm (1/4 in) holes at the factory spot positions, the count from step 5. Or bond it with panel adhesive and plug every second position.

    • Hole size. BMW's general rule is 8 mm holes at least 25 mm apart (I-CAR: BMW). On this narrow lip use I-CAR's 6 mm thin-to-thin size, which it gives for "plug welds on a pinchweld flange joining two exterior panels, such as along a wheelhouse opening" (I-CAR).
    • Order. Weld every second position first, from the crown outward, alternately forward and back. Then fill in the rest.
    • Crimp the edge, as BMW does. On a new side wall BMW crimps the outer skin's arch edge over the inner flange along most of the arch, then seals it (TIS 41 35 101, p.15). After the plug welds, close any part of the lip that opened up the same way, before it's sealed in step 14. On the coupe, the donor's body, BMW also bonds the outer arch section to the side reinforcement with adhesive 51 0 032, after a contact-pattern check with no gap over 1 mm (TIS, coupe, p.9, p.12).

    Pass, on a coupon of donor offcuts before you touch the car: each plug's face 8–10 mm across and no more than 3 mm high; broken apart, it tears a 3–8 mm hole in the bottom piece (I-CAR practice welding guide, test coupons).

  3. Stitch 10–15 mm (0.4–0.6 in) welds between the tacks, in a skip pattern, until the seam is continuous, letting each area cool between passes.

    • First pass: top seam gaps 1, 5, 9…, then the rear seam's odd gaps, then the front seam's gaps 1, 5, 9…, then the other side of the car.
    • Later passes: come back for gaps 3, 7, 11… only when the first area is hand-warm, then 2, 6, 10…, then 4, 8, 12….
    • Limit: lay no more than about 150 mm of weld per seam per pass (our suggestion). GM's published rhythm for overlap seams is the same idea: 25 mm welds with 25 mm gaps, then fill (I-CAR).
    • Why: "you can't continuously weld this thickness gauge metal because you'll get heat distortion… so you have to stitch it" (Calvin's Car Diary – PT9 (2020), 12:40). BMW does the same on its butt seams: spots stitched "so close together … that a continuous seam is created", each area left to cool (TIS 41 35 101, p.11).
    • Settings: overhead, turn them down 10–15% (Miller). Use an argon/CO2 mix, BMW's 82/18 or the common 75/25 (Welding settings and safety): M346 started on 100% argon and "could not get a good solid bead" (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 14:40).

    Check: penetration visible on the back along every seam, the test Calvin's body man uses. Grind and planish each seam as you finish it, not at the end.

  4. Close the gaps at the sill and door. Where the new quarter met the sill by the door shut, M346 found "a moon-shaped hole" and filled it with a fabricated plate and many small welds (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 46:00). Tracks and Trails templated the gaps with tape, cut gussets from scrap and tacked them in (Tracks and Trails (2026), 23:20). Check: no open hole into the sill or the cabin.

  5. Dress the welds. Grind with 80-grit flap discs without thinning the panel, then planish (hammer the seam on a dolly) to relieve the shrinkage. Check:

    • every template fits within 1 mm;
    • the station offsets match left to right within 3 mm;
    • the body diagonals are within ±2 mm of your figures from before welding (our suggestion);
    • the door gaps and flush are back to your before readings.

Finish.

  1. Seal and protect. Brush seam sealer into the lip's U-channel until it's full. Redish sprays a thin coat into the welded lines first, then a thicker one, curing 24 hours between (Redish – M3 rear arches replaced (2016), 09:20). Seam-seal the inside of every joint, epoxy-prime, and cavity-wax the quarter. Tracks and Trails scuffed with 100 grit, then used 2K epoxy primer, filler, more epoxy and high-build primer, with seam sealer and Wool Wax inside (Tracks and Trails (2026), 24:20, 27:40). M346 put weldable zinc primer on all exposed metal before the skin went on (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 41:40). Check: the lip is a sealed double skin all round.
  2. Rebuild the door edge, if you flared it. Build the gap back with panel bond against a 4 mm card wall, cure it 24 hours, and sand it to feeler gauges (Rear doors). Check: the gaps and flush are back to your before readings.
  3. Use filler as a skim only. Heavy filler loses the arch's crisp edge. M346's painter: "a lot of times when people do conversions, they get so much bondo and glaze that… the arch just kind of gets lost". He skim-coated the weld ripple, which "you can't really see, but you can feel" (M346 Projects – Pt 24 (2025), 00:20, 01:20). BMW allows filler only where the surface is out by less than 2 mm (0.08 in), and tins anything deeper (TIS 41 00, p.2). Final filler and paint come in Phase 13. Check: before any filler goes on, no low spot is 2 mm deep or more under a straightedge or a section template; planish until none is.

Wheel-arch liners. The widened arches need liners that fit them, so take the donor's. M3projekts lists rear liners among the parts the conversion needs (M3projekts – Ep3 (2023), 09:30). BMW lists M3-only "coverings", 51712695667 left and 51717895936 right, on both M3s; they may be the rear liners, but we couldn't confirm it (ETK).

Check before you seal and prime. Pass values not credited to a source are our suggestions.

Check Pass
Templates Every station within 1 mm of its template
Symmetry Station offsets and lip heights above the hub center within 3 mm side to side
Body diagonals Within ±2 mm of your figures from before welding
Full bump At least 10 mm from tire to sheet metal
Doors Open and close freely; gaps and flush back to your before readings
Lip A sealed double skin all round
Filler, right side Your pot seats in the M3 opening, the flap closes flush and latches, and the filler pipe sits unstrained (Filler and EVAP). A poor seal fails the EVAP leak test, which finds leaks as small as 1.0 mm (BMW ST041 Part 3, Inspection readiness)

Rear doors

Decide with the door shut and aligned, before you mark the cut lines (step 3 of the graft). The Touring's rear door forms the front of the arch opening, and its trailing edge meets the arch roughly 300–350 mm ahead of the axle. At the shut line the M3 surface would stand about 11–20 mm (0.4–0.8 in) proud of the stock door. Both figures are our estimates from drawings; measure your car (Rear arches and doors). Three ways of dealing with that step have been shown:

  1. Leave the door standard and blend the flare in before the shut line. Beat the M3 nose in over its last 60–100 mm (2.4–3.9 in) so it lands flush with the door.
    • BMW and Petroyle. This is how BMW built the prototype: BMW "decided against melding the rear wheel-arch sculpting into the door" (Autocar). Petroyle says the arches "don't go into the doors… we would finish the arch before the door exactly the same as the concept car" (Hagerty – Petroyle's E46 M3 Touring (2026), 07:40, 08:40).
    • Other builds. One e46fanatics builder kept flat doors "to follow the BMW prototype" (e46fanatics). The builder of the Renner car warns that "some people… continue the quarter panel to here and that's not correct so you got to be very careful how do you contour the door… this is the stock touring door" (Larry Chen (2025), 05:20).
    • The nose. M346 describes it: on a sedan or Touring "this part is actually pushed in more and then starts to flare out" (M346 Projects – Pt 14 (2024), 28:40). Expect to dress the door's trailing edge so it meets the new arch line cleanly.
  2. Flare the door's trailing edge out by the same amount.
    • Without welding. SOS Customz pounded the edge out (SOS Customz (2023), 02:00). M346 marked start and stop points on the quarter, opened the door and massaged the edge out with a 2x4 (M346 Projects – Pt 22 (2025), 00:40). His friend Lauren "flares the door first and then he puts on the quarter panel" (01:00).
    • With a welded section. Calvin's body man welded a section into the door so it "flicks out" to meet the flare (Calvin's Car Diary – PT9 (2020), 02:20).
    • Rivet-on kits take the same approach: HARD's flare kit has separate rear-door pieces.
  3. Carry the flare across the shut line, then re-cut the gap.
    • Tracks and Trails made a cardboard-and-tape template of the door edge, overlaid the front of the flare onto the door, then re-cut the gap from the template (Tracks and Trails (2026), 15:40, 21:40).
    • A German forum poster planned the same in 2006: weld the M3 side panel "bis über die hinteren Türen" (right across the rear doors), then "den Türspalt wieder aufsägen" (saw the door gap open again) (bmw-syndikat).
    • Other builders have "added a bit of metal" to the door's trailing edge (e46fanatics).

Our recommendation: option 1, the standard door, for a first build. It's BMW's own answer. The door skin, its gaps and its trim stay untouched, and the extra shaping is confined to the last 60–100 mm of the new quarter. Choose option 2 if you want the flare to carry onto the door, and budget for rebuilding the gap.

Restoring the gap. The target is your own car's baseline: the gaps and flush you recorded at three marked points on each door before any welding. They should sit inside BMW's E46 gaps: rear door to side wall 4 ± 0.75 mm, front door to rear door 4.5 ± 0.75 mm, doors to sill 5 ± 1 mm, each parallel within 1 mm (TIS 41 00).

  • Flaring opens the gap. Flaring the door after the quarter is on opens the shut gap by about 3–4 mm (M346 Projects – Pt 22 (2025), 01:00).
  • Panel bond builds it back. M346 built it back with 3M panel bond (38315) against a taped card wall about 4 mm thick, let it cure for 24 hours, sanded it with a hard block and checked it against the stock gap with feeler gauges (04:00, 22:20). His reasoning: it's a small area that doesn't flex, where panel bond is stronger than filler (07:20).

Pass: at each marked point, the gap and the flush are back within 0.5 mm of your before readings (our suggestion), and the gap inside BMW's band.

Trim that follows. On a flared door, the straight side rubbing strip has to be reshaped to follow the flare, and one plastic side skirt was heated and bent out to meet it (Calvin's Car Diary – PT9 (2020), 04:20, 11:20).

Tip

A faster route is rivet-on flares. HARD Motorsport's M3-style rear set for the E46 sedan and Touring is ABS plastic, molded from M3 fenders, with separate rear-door pieces, $294 list ($264.60 on sale in October 2026) (HARD Motorsport). The rivets show, as on one 2018 car (BMWBlog), and you still have to cut and seal the old lip behind them.

Wheels, track and offsets

Wheel Front Rear
Style 67, 18-inch (standard) 8J ET47, 225/45R18 9J ET26, 255/40R18
Style 67, 19-inch option 8J ET47, 225/40R19 9.5J ET27, 255/35R19
Style 163M (Competition) 19 × 8 ET47, 225/40R19 19 × 9.5 ET27, 255/35R19
CSL 19 × 8.5 ET44, 235/35R19 19 × 9.5 ET27, 265/30R19

Sources: BMW wheel and tire list, BimmerTips.

Offset math. The outer rim edge sits (rim width in mm ÷ 2) − ET outboard of the hub face. One inch is 25.4 mm.

  • 325i Sport Package wheel, 8J × 17 ET47, the wheel BMW's MY2003 wheel and tire list gives the 325i Touring's 225/45R17 tires (BMW wheel and tire list: Touring, BMW USA): 8 × 25.4 ÷ 2 − 47 = 54.6 mm. The same list puts the 7J × 16 standard wheels at ET46 or ET47, depending on the style
  • Style 67 rear, 9J ET26: 9 × 25.4 ÷ 2 − 26 = 88.3 mm
  • ZCP rear, 9.5J ET27: 9.5 × 25.4 ÷ 2 − 27 = 93.7 mm, so 5.4 mm further out than Style 67

At the rear, the hub faces match to within a millimetre or two, so the M3 wheel alone puts the outer rim edge about 33.7 mm further out than that 8J ET47 wheel. At the front, the M3's axle parts move each hub face about 18.5 mm out (1,508 mm against 1,471 mm of track; the M3's front wheels are ET47, like the Touring's 17-inch wheels), which the M3 front fenders cover. Tire sidewalls bulge past the rim, so leave margin. The wheel fitment calculator works these positions out for any wheel and tire.

What builders ran. Autoalex runs the M3's 18-inch rear wheels on all four corners and reports no rubbing (Autoalex Cars – Finale (2025), 08:20); M346 also kept the M3 rears for a square set (M346 Projects – Pt 1 (2023), 07:40). Tenza's donor came on aftermarket wheels too wide and too aggressive in offset for the wagon, so Tenza bought a fourth M3 wheel (Tenza Motorsports – Total build cost (2022), 03:40).

BMW's staggered sizes for the Touring. The same BMW list gives the 325i Touring two staggered sets: 17-inch, 225/45ZR17 on 7½J × 17 ET41 front and 245/40ZR17 on 8½J × 17 ET50 rear; and 18-inch, 225/40ZR18 on 8J × 18 ET47 front and 255/35ZR18 on 8½J × 18 ET50 rear (BMW wheel and tire list: Touring). BMW's 2004 US Sports Wagon manual also gives pressures for the staggered 17-inch set (p.27). The M3's own sizes, 225/45R18 and 255/40R18, aren't on the Touring's list: that's the question for a Massachusetts inspection station (Massachusetts).

Tires for Touring weight. Compared like for like in US curb weights, your finished car carries about what an M3 coupe does on its front axle, but about 824–842 kg on its rear axle against the coupe's 770 kg (our estimate; see Weights and axle loads). Two checks before you buy tires:

  • Load index. Read the axle ratings on your Touring's door-pillar label (BMW's 2004 US manual gives 900 kg front and 1,210 kg rear for a manual 325i Touring), and check that the load index of the M3-size tires you'll fit covers them, axle by axle (BMW manual, p.162). A tire shop can check it against the maker's load table, or use the tire load check.
  • Pressures. BMW's 2003 US M3 manuals give the same cold pressures for the 18- and 19-inch sizes: 230 kPa (33 psi) front and 240 kPa (35 psi) rear with up to four people, and 280 kPa (41 psi) front and 330 kPa (48 psi) rear with four people and luggage (M3 coupe manual, p.27, M3 convertible manual, p.27). BMW gives the 325i Touring itself 220/260 kPa (32/38 psi), and 260/310 kPa (38/45 psi) loaded, on its 16- and 17-inch tires: its heavier rear wants more pressure (2004 Sports Wagon manual, p.27). Start from BMW's M3 figures, use the loaded ones whenever the car carries luggage, and have the tire shop check the rear pressure against the tire maker's load table for your rear axle load.

Rear bumper, skirts and trim

  • The bumper corner is part of the arch. We infer from BMW's drawings that from about 150–220 mm behind the axle rearward, below the bumper's top line, the arch edge is the bumper cover. There the M3's outline stands about 29–32 mm (1.1–1.3 in) proud of the Touring's from 200 to 350 mm behind the axle, falling to about 13 mm at 450 mm behind (our estimate, ±5–10 mm; Flare profile). That is roughly how far the Touring bumper's corner has to come out to follow the M3 arch, so trial-fit the bumper before the final welding (step 8 of the graft). M346 made relief cuts in the Touring bumper's corners "so that it'll follow the contour of the M3 flare because originally… the stock touring bumper doesn't come out this wide" (M346 Projects – How to make an E46 M3 Touring rear bumper (2024), 62:40). Ultimate Klasse's Touring bumper "was given the proper widening treatment with plastic weld to line up with the newly fattened arches" (Ultimate Klasse), and M3projekts pairs the wide M3 rear fenders with "the M3 bumper corner" (M3projekts – Ep3 (2023), 03:00).
  • Rear bumper. Either keep and modify your Touring bumper, as on the Sloan car's customized OEM bumper (BMWBlog), or fit the M3 bumper, whose corners meet the M3 quarters (M3projekts – Ep3 (2023), 02:00). The Touring's tailgate opening drops lower than the M3 bumper allows, so builders cut the center section from the Touring bumper and plastic-weld it into the M3 bumper (Tracks and Trails (2026), 28:00, Calvin's Car Diary – PT9 (2020), 09:20, SOS Customz (2023), 21:00). M346's 82-minute video shows one method: move the two center parking sensors down to the lower middle section, keep the Touring bumper's inner pieces to stiffen the M3 bumper, and graft in the Touring's wider corners with relief cuts, hot staples, ABS rod and two-part epoxy (M346 Projects – How to make an E46 M3 Touring rear bumper (2024), 06:00). His painter then spent about two weeks finishing it (M346 Projects – Pt 24 (2025), 04:20). The M3 bumper carrier's Kevlar tabs often break (M346 rear bumper, 44:20), and it can't take a tow hitch (Autoalex v2 – Massive update (2024), 11:20). Mark the tip cut-outs with the exhaust hanging in its final position; see Exhaust and the spare-wheel well.
  • Side skirts. M3 skirts fit with OEM M3 rocker clips, which are black and a little taller than the white non-M clips (e46fanatics, M3projekts – Ep3 (2023), 05:30). The coupe skirts are a few mm shorter than the Touring's; M346 split the difference front and rear (M346 Projects – Pt 18 (2024), 08:40), and M3projekts found the mounting points pull the rear corner down slightly (M3projekts – Ep3 (2023), 06:00).
  • Mirrors. M3 mirrors don't bolt to 4-door doors: sedan and Touring doors have three mounting points, the coupe's two (M3projekts – M3 mirrors on a Touring (2024), 00:30). M3Projekts sells an "E46 M3 Touring/Sedan mirror base" for €239–459 before VAT (M3Projekts); it's the same part for left- and right-hand drive and needs the M3 mirror modules and switch (06:30). On M346's left-hand-drive car the driver's glass sat too far out, so he ground off the housing's locating tabs and elongated the holes (M346 Projects – Pt 21 (2024), 26:20). Facelift Touring doors have "ribbon cable" mirror harnesses; the M3 mirrors use the older connection, so M346 fitted non-ribbon door harnesses from a sedan (02:00).
  • Paint. The BMW prototype wears Chrome Shadow metallic. Most builders repaint the whole car once the metalwork is done, with only a skim of filler over the arch seams (step 16 of the graft); M346's car spent about four months at the paint shop (M346 Projects – Pt 25 (2025)). What to tell the painter is in Shop briefs.

Registration and legal (US)

Note

Practical notes, not legal advice. Rules vary by state and county. The car this guide follows is registered in Massachusetts: read the federal picture, then Massachusetts. For another state, read California's rules as an example and put the questions at the end of this chapter to your own state program before you buy the donor.

Federal. EPA's 2020 tampering enforcement policy replaced its 1991 Engine Switching Fact Sheet (EPA). It treats an engine switch as acceptable when the result matches a certified configuration of the same or a newer model year. For anything else it expects a documented "reasonable basis", such as emissions testing showing the vehicle complies for its full useful life, prepared before the work. BMW never certified an S54 Touring, so read the policy and talk to your state program early. In practice, keep everything that made the donor M3 compliant:

  1. An S54 the same model year as your Touring or newer.
  2. The complete M3 emissions system: catalysts, all four O2 sensors, secondary air injection, evaporative system connections (including the DM-TL leak-test pump) and crankcase ventilation.
  3. The M3 DME with its emissions calibration, and working OBD-II: check-engine lamp, diagnostic port and readiness monitors. Getting the monitors to set is covered in Inspection readiness.

Engine-computer software. Every immobilizer route touches the DME (see Immobilizer (EWS)), and some inspections now check the software itself.

  • VIN. Have your Touring's full 17-character VIN written into the DME. Plug-in tests read the VIN from the OBD port (e46fanatics), and BMW issued a bulletin about E46s failing state tests because the DME reported an incomplete VIN (BMW SI B12 09 13).
  • EWS delete. Order the delete only, with every emissions function kept. Vendors carry their own warnings: Severn's delete page says "Recommended for off-road use only!" (Severn).
  • No Euro or CSL software. Euro-market M3s have no DM-TL leak-test pump (M3projekts – Ep6 (2023), 02:48), so a Euro or CSL flash may drop US emissions functions such as the EVAP leak test, and a plug-in test may then show monitors that never set.

State inspections. Nevada's Engine Swap Fact Sheet (form EC-054, revised 02/2026) is a good model of what inspectors ask for (Nevada DMV):

  • an engine the same model year or newer;
  • all emission devices fitted and working;
  • a federally certified highway engine, with verifiable proof of its year and configuration;
  • OBD-II compliance, including monitors that can be "commanded to incomplete" and then set to completion;
  • contact with the emissions lab before the swap.

New York's OBD test fails model-year 2001-and-later vehicles with more than one monitor not ready (NYVIP3). Some programs only test cars of certain ages: Ohio's E-Check now covers vehicles 6 through 26 years old (Ohio EPA), so check how your state treats a 2001–05 car.

If your car is an M56 SULEV. From the 2003 model year BMW sold some US 325is with the low-emission M56 engine in California, New York and Massachusetts (Vermont from 2004), with a stainless-steel tank, filler neck and canister (BMW B11 75 02) and a fuel-pump controller (ETK). BMW's bulletin introduced it with automatics, and the only gearbox-module harness BMW's catalog lists for the M56 is for automatics (ETK). Yet the catalog's pages for the US 325i M56 Touring also list a five-speed gearbox and clutch, in groups shared with other engines (ETK: gearbox, ETK: clutch). A manual M56 is probably a conversion, but check the engine code in Phase 0 even on a manual car. Tenza Motorsports replaced a 2004 SULEV Touring's tank and evaporative parts with an M54/S54-type tank and the M3 charcoal canister (Tenza Motorsports – No more SULEV (2021), 00:20). That changes a certified evaporative system, so ask your state program how it treats it before you change anything, especially in California.

Massachusetts

Key point

This build's Touring, a 2003, is registered in Massachusetts. A 2001–05 car gets no emissions test there in 2026, but the state's anti-tampering rules still apply, its engine-switch rule can't be met to the letter by any S54 Touring, and grafting steel from the donor may bring a "reconstructed" title. Get written answers from MassDEP and the RMV before you buy the donor. The rules below were checked in October 2026; several mass.gov pages blocked automated reading, so confirm anything marked "(unverified)".

Inspection: safety only. Massachusetts exempts gasoline cars "15 or more model years old" from the emissions test, so in 2026 only model year 2012 and newer get the OBD plug-in test. The station's computer decides from your Touring's VIN, not from the engine (310 CMR 60.02(3)(b)4, c. 111 §142M, Vehicles Tested, Vehicle Check Module 1 (2026)). The program's site is now mavehiclecheck.com. The car still needs the annual safety inspection: $35, 14 items, filmed by bay cameras (Basic Inspection Information, 540 CMR 4.04, amended 3 January 2025). No public inspector's manual exists: the program posts 540 CMR 4.00 as the procedure, and its inspector training modules cover emissions only. The items this build can fail:

Item The rule What to do
Ride height No more than 2 inches above or below "the original manufacturer's specified height", which means your Touring's, not the M3's (c. 90 §7P, 540 CMR 4.04(13)). The state publishes no way to measure it; BMW's TIS ride height for your Touring is the clearest published figure (our inference) In Phase 0, load the Touring to BMW's normal position (full tank; 68 kg in each front seat, 68 kg in the middle of the rear seat, 21 kg in the trunk), tires at placard pressure, and measure it BMW's way, rim flange to arch edge. Compare with BMW's figure for the suspension named on the front-strut label: "6Z Serie" on 16-inch wheels, front 589 mm (23.2 in) and rear 555 mm (21.9 in); "6Z Sport" on 17-inch wheels, 589 and 554 mm; ±10 mm (TIS front, TIS rear, strut label; other sizes in Key numbers). The arches will change, so at the same load also record the sill height at each jacking point and the roof height at marked points (BMW publishes 1,409 mm (55.5 in), or 1,444 mm (56.8 in) with roof rails; a 325xi stands 20 mm higher: 325xi). Finish within 50.8 mm (2 in) of those, ideally within 25 mm (1 in, our target); the M3's 18-inch tires alone add about 14 mm (0.6 in) (Massachusetts ride-height baseline)
Tires The same size on each side of an axle; front and rear may differ only "as determined by vehicle manufacturer"; tires that stick out past the body need flaps (540 CMR 4.04(11), (12)(c)). On M3 wheels, an unflared Touring's rear tires would stand about 22 mm (0.9 in) proud of the body; the M3 flares bring the body out to them (our estimate; Rear arches and doors) BMW's MY2003 wheel and tire list gives the 325i Touring staggered 17-inch (225/45ZR17 front, 245/40ZR17 rear) and 18-inch (225/40ZR18 front, 255/35ZR18 rear) sizes, but not the M3's 225/45R18 and 255/40R18, so ask your station about the M3's sizes before the appointment (BMW wheel and tire list: Touring, Wheels, track and offsets)
Exhaust Tight, leak-free, "securely fastened with fasteners in place and undamaged", discharging "beyond operator, passenger, and/or trunk compartment", and no louder than "the vehicle when equipped with the original manufacturer's equipment"; the inspector revs the engine to check (540 CMR 4.04(5)). No muffler "cut-out or by-pass", no muffler whose "baffle plates, screens or other original internal parts have been removed and not replaced", and no exhaust "modified in a manner which will amplify or increase the noise" (c. 90 §16) Fit the stock M3 system with the muffler intact, no valved, gutted or "delete" section, and every hanger nut and bolt in place. Keep the receipts and part numbers that show an unaltered BMW M3 system, and ask the station how it judges an M3 system on a 325i (Exhaust and the spare-wheel well). Three S54 swaps on the non-M floor, two of them Tourings, ran a US E36 M3 muffler (NAM3, NAM3, NAM3); whatever you fit must be no louder than the car's original equipment
Lights US-spec (FMVSS 108) lamps only, all working and aimed (540 CMR 4.04(10); 540 CMR 22.07) Keep BMW US-spec lamps and every reflector and side marker
Brakes The inspector tests the service brake at 4–8 mph for pull, the parking brake against the engine in the lowest gear at 1,200–1,300 rpm, and a stop from 20 mph within 30 ft on the foot brake or 80 ft on the parking brake. With the car stopped, about 125 lb on the pedal for 10 s must hold, with at least 20% of the travel left and the brake failure warning lamp off; the booster must assist when the engine starts; and the lines and hoses must be secure and free of leaks and chafing (540 CMR 4.04(4)) Run the same tests first (Brakes and bleeding). BMW's red BRAKE lamp means low fluid or the parking brake on; DSC and ABS faults light the yellow BRAKE lamp, the ABS lamp and the DSC lamp (BMW ST056). Get all four dark before the appointment
Suspension and steering The front end is jacked and inspected; ball joints are checked "in accordance with the applicable manufacturer's specifications"; the steering must reach full lock both ways without "binding or interference"; excessive play, or broken, bent or missing shocks or springs, fail; and the suspension must not upset headlamp aim (540 CMR 4.04(1), (6)) Check the ball joints, dampers and full lock before the appointment, and aim the headlights at the final ride height
Structure No "modified" structure that causes "a hazard or structural weakness" (540 CMR 4.04(12)(f)) Sound, sealed and corrosion-protected welds, with photos of the work
Floor pans No "holes or cracks, due to rust or otherwise, in the floor pans or other body panels which would permit the passage of exhaust gases into the passenger or trunk compartments" (540 CMR 4.04(12)(d)) Seal every seam of the trunk floor on both faces, fit a plug in every hole, and check the floor with a light or smoke before the carpet goes back (Phase 5)
Fuel cap and bumpers The cap must fit and the fuel system be tight; bumpers fitted (540 CMR 4.04) Check after the filler-flap work in Phase 6

The airbag-lamp check applies only to cars ten or fewer model years old (540 CMR 4.04).

Untested still means regulated. None of the state's anti-tampering rules has an age limit (c. 90 §7O; c. 111 §142M(f), with fines up to $25,000 a day; 310 CMR 60.02(23); 310 CMR 7.40(2)(h)), and the federal ban applies for a car's whole life (EPA tampering policy). Keep every M3 emissions part fitted and working, keep the US emissions calibration and every OBD monitor, and order the DME work as an immobilizer-only change.

The engine-switch rule. 310 CMR 60.02(12)(d) expects a car with a switched engine to be a "certified configuration" in "the same emissions certification category", with no switching between California- and federally-certified cars or between vehicle classes; the program's 2026 inspector training repeats the rule (Module 1). BMW never certified an S54 Touring, so no build matches it to the letter. How far off yours is depends on the category on your Touring's underhood emissions (VECI) label (EPA certification data):

Your Touring Category Against the S54 (LEV; federal Bin 9 from 2004)
2001–02, and 2003 cars in test group "LER" LEV Same category
A 325xi, any year 2001–05 (test group "LER", or "M54" for some 2001 cars) LEV; for 2004–05, California LEV and federal Bin 9 Same category in every year (325xi)
Other 2003–05 325i cars (test groups "UL2" and "SMG") ULEV The S54 is less stringent
M56 cars (sold in Massachusetts) SULEV The S54 is much less stringent

Every S54 test group was certified for both California and federal sale, so choose a donor whose VECI label shows a US 50-state certification. Massachusetts adopted California's new-vehicle standards but not California's engine-change referee, so there's no approval route like California's. The nearest formal step is a MassDEP "finding" that the altered car meets the standards for its model year (310 CMR 7.40(9)(b)2). Nobody has documented whether MassDEP gives one to a private owner, so ask. EPA expects any "reasonable basis" for an engine switch to be documented before the work. Note that the "same model year or newer" rule comes from EPA's policy; the Massachusetts rule has no model-year test for cars.

This build's 2003. Both 2003 test groups for an M54 325i Sport Wagon, LER (LEV) and UL2 (LEV-II ULEV), were certified for California and for all 50 states, so where the car was first sold doesn't tell you which one yours is; its VECI label does (EPA certification data). Read two labels before anything else: the build month on the driver's door pillar and the test group under the hood. UL2 is the M54 Touring's first LEV-II certification, and the MS45.1 with its secondary-air air-mass sensor arrived in 03/2003, so a car built before 03/2003 is probably an MS43 in LER and a later one an MS45.1 in UL2. That pairing is our inference, so go by the labels. A 2003 in LER matches the S54's LEV category, the best case this rule allows; one in UL2 would drop from ULEV to LEV, so put that question to MassDEP before you buy a donor. To meet EPA's "same or newer model year" test, choose a 2003–06 M3 as the donor.

Title: the "reconstructed" question. Massachusetts titles record cylinders, transmission type, fuel, colour and odometer, not the engine number, and no rule was found that requires reporting an engine change. But anyone who "reassembles a motor vehicle by means of welding together ... the frames or unit bodies of two or more motor vehicles" needs a new title application, an RMV-appointed inspection and a "reconstructed" title (c. 90D §20F). Ask the RMV Title Division whether grafting the donor's arch steel or trunk floor counts: the statute's affidavit asks for "the location of the point of connection or weld joint of the two or more vehicle frames" (c. 90D §20F). New BMW panels avoid the question. For the arches, the M3 convertible quarter 41357894541/542 plus its inner lateral trim panel 41217894553/554 make a complete new set, about $2,230 per side at BMWPartsDeal (about €2,120 at eStore-Central) in October 2026 (Rear arches and doors). For the floor, the new M3 trunk floor 41127895619 and its front reinforcement 51717894229 are listed in the US at $763.61 and $88.22 (BMWPartsDeal, October 2026; Exhaust and the spare-wheel well). A "reconstructed" brand would cut the finished car's value.

The donor's title. Whoever takes a car to be junked or scrapped must surrender its title within 10 days, and the record is branded JUNK for good (c. 90D §20E); a salvage-titled donor has its own 10-day rule (§20C). Run the donor's VIN through an NMVTIS provider before you buy, buy only with the title (or salvage title) and a bill of sale listing the VIN, and leave every VIN plate and stamping with the donor's shell (c. 266 §139). Scrap the shell through a licensed recycler and keep the junking paperwork.

While the car is off the road. Either keep the Touring registered and insured and file the Off-the-Road Verification form before its sticker expires (renewed after 12 months), or cancel the plates (540 CMR 4.03, form VSC123). When it returns to the road, get it inspected straight away; after a new registration you have 7 days. A failed car gets a free re-test at the same station within 60 days (Test Results).

Insurance and plates. Tell your insurer about the swap in writing: a misrepresentation that "increased the risk of loss" can void a policy (c. 175 §186). Agreed-value collector cover exists in Massachusetts but rules out daily use. From 1 July 2025 the compulsory minimums are $25,000/$50,000 bodily injury, $30,000 property damage and $8,000 PIP (Insurance Journal). Antique plates need a car "over twenty-five years old" and limit use to shows and club events, and Year of Manufacture plates must not look like current plates, so neither suits this car (c. 90 §1, 540 CMR 2.07).

A/C and odometer. Massachusetts adds nothing to the federal A/C rules in the next section. Its odometer law matches the federal one (c. 266 §141): program the M3 cluster to your Touring's true mileage.

Ask in writing before you buy the donor (enclose photos of both cars' VECI labels):

Ask Questions Contact
MassDEP, Bureau of Air and Waste Does 310 CMR 60.02(12)(d), c. 90 §7O or c. 111 §142M(f) treat this swap as a violation in an emissions-exempt car, if every M3 emissions part, the US calibration and OBD are kept? Do you make findings under 310 CMR 7.40(9)(b)2 for one vehicle, and on what evidence? Does the answer change for a ULEV or SULEV Touring, or for a 325xi converted from all-wheel to rear-wheel drive? Is an immobilizer-only DME change treated as tampering? 100 Cambridge Street, Suite 900, Boston MA 02114; 617-292-5500 (MassDEP letter, October 2026)
RMV Title Division Does welding M3 arch or trunk-floor sections cut from a donor into my Touring count under c. 90D §20F? Would new BMW panels avoid it? Must I surrender the donor's title under §20E, or apply for a salvage title under §20C? Must I amend the registration after the engine change? 857-368-8050 (unverified)
Vehicle Check or your inspection station Is my VIN decoded as emissions-exempt whatever engine is fitted? How do you judge staggered M3 tire sizes on a Touring, ride height against the original (I'll bring roof and jacking-point heights measured before the build), and a stock M3 exhaust on a 325i? 1-844-358-0135 (Test Results); station locator
Your insurer Agreed-value cover for the modified car, with what use limits? Cover while it's off the road? What records do you need? Your agent

Keep the replies in the car's file with the donor's title or junking receipt, the bills of sale, the VECI label photos and the odometer records.

California

California's Bureau of Automotive Repair (BAR) runs the strictest program, and its rules show what a careful state will ask (BAR):

  • Referee first. Every vehicle with an engine change must pass an initial inspection at a BAR Referee center and carry a BAR Referee label inside the engine compartment. After that, regular Smog Check stations do the inspections, based on the label. Appointments: (800) 622-7733.
  • Donor rules apply. The initial Referee inspection follows the Smog Check requirements of the engine's donor vehicle, and bringing the donor's VIN to the appointment simplifies the process.
  • Tampering law. State and federal anti-tampering laws prohibit changes to the emission control system as the manufacturer certified it (California Vehicle Code section 27156; 16 CCR 3362.1). BAR's Engine Change Guidelines are in its Smog Check Reference Guide.
  • Modified software. Since 19 July 2021, Smog Check has failed vehicles whose OBD data doesn't match an OEM or CARB-approved software configuration, reported as "Modified Software". BAR counts a vehicle's software as part of its emissions control system, and a failed car's software must be restored to an OEM or CARB-approved version (BAR).

So before you choose between an EWS-delete flash, syncing a virgin DME and fitting the donor's EWS and keys (see Immobilizer (EWS)), ask the Referee whether a VIN-matched EWS-delete flash will pass. California has reportedly failed cars for detected DME tunes (e46fanatics). One San Diego E46 M3 wagon passed as "a totally legal California swap" after "like five trips to the BAR referee" (Driving Cody – The E46 M3 wagon BMW should have made (2020), 02:20).

A/C, odometer, title and insurance

A/C refrigerant. Under the Clean Air Act, nobody may vent refrigerant. Anyone who services a car's A/C for pay must be certified under Section 609 and use approved equipment; certified equipment must remove the refrigerant before the system is opened; and recovered refrigerant must be recycled or reclaimed before it goes back into a car (EPA). Refrigerant in containers over 0.9 kg (2 lb) is sold only to technicians certified under Section 608 or 609. Small cans of R-134a, 0.9 kg (2 lb) or less with a self-sealing valve, can still be sold for DIY use (EPA, EPA), but they don't change the order of work: recovery by a certified shop comes first. EPA's approved Section 609 programs include ASE, ESCO Institute and MACS (EPA). In practice, have a certified shop recover the refrigerant from both cars before you open any A/C line, cap every open fitting, and after the first start have a shop evacuate the system and charge it by weight to the underhood label. The shop brief is in Shop briefs, and the job in Air conditioning.

Odometer. Program the M3 cluster to your car's true mileage. The light module (LCM) holds the car's mileage record, and a cluster with the matching VIN takes its mileage from it (e46fanatics), so make the cluster match the LCM, never the reverse (see Instrument cluster and mileage). Federal law lets you fit a replacement odometer if it shows the same mileage (49 U.S.C. §32704), so the cluster keeps your Touring's true mileage. The federal written mileage disclosure on sale no longer applies to model-year 2010 and older vehicles (49 CFR 580.17), but your state may still require it. Keep screenshots and photos of the cluster and LCM mileage before and after.

Title and paperwork. Keep the donor's title or salvage bill of sale, its VIN, photos of the engine number, receipts, and your state's written guidance. Nevada, for example, wants "verifiable proof" of the engine's year and configuration (Nevada DMV). Some states record engine changes on the title or registration; ask your DMV. Plan how you'll dispose of the donor shell and its title; see Space, storage and logistics.

Insurance. Use an agreed-value policy, backed by receipts, photos and an appraisal, which costs about $250–$500 (June 2026). Insurers have paid out modified cars as stock when the owner couldn't document the work (Automotive Addicts). Recent prices make useful comparables: one finished conversion was bid to $59,250 on Bring a Trailer in August 2024 without meeting its reserve (BaT), and an all-wheel-drive S54 Touring was listed at $65,000 (Built for Backroads).

Questions for your state program

Ask before you buy the donor, and get the answers in writing if you can:

  1. Does an engine change need a referee or special inspection, and what must I bring (donor VIN and title, engine-number photos, receipts)?
  2. Must the engine be the same model year as the car or newer? Must it come from a vehicle certified for this state?
  3. Which emissions parts must be fitted and working: catalysts, all O2 sensors, secondary air, the evaporative system with its DM-TL leak-test pump, crankcase ventilation?
  4. Does the test check DME software (calibration ID and CVN)? Will a VIN-matched EWS-delete flash pass, or must the software be OEM or state-approved?
  5. How many readiness monitors may be "not ready" for my model year?
  6. If my car is an M56 SULEV, which fuel tank and evaporative system must it keep?
  7. Is the engine change recorded on the title or registration, and is there a form to file?
  8. Does the state require any mileage disclosure when the instrument cluster is replaced with one set to the car's true mileage?

  6. Tracks and Trails: "What it really takes to build an E46 M3 Touring" (2026). The closest match to your car, a 2004 325i Touring built at home; front end, quarters, doors and rear bumper on camera.
  7. M346 Projects: Pt 14 "M3 Body Work" (2024). An hour of trunk floor, inner tubs, quarters and filler surround on a Touring, with convertible donor steel. Both of these builds fitted catless headers; see the cautions under Videos.
  8. Autoalex Cars on YouTube and the finale. More than two years, £70k, a rusty donor.
  9. BMW SI B11 04 04. BMW's rod-bearing bulletin: both rod-bolt procedures, oil, break-in.
  10. FCP Euro: E46 M3 rear subframe overhaul. The rear axle, step by step.

  12. BimmerWorld: rear subframe floor reinforcement. Why the floor cracks and how to weld it.

Factory documentation

How to set up the documentation and coding kit is in Factory documentation and coding kit.

  • TIS (newTIS): BMW's repair instructions, torque tables, body dimensions and wiring diagrams, by VIN (newTIS). Load the Touring's VIN for the body side and the donor's for the engine side: one swapper found the diagrams changed once his wagon's VIN was loaded (e46fanatics). Our automated checks couldn't open newTIS itself. The TIS values in this guide come from BMW's E46 TIS, issue 12/2007, which workshop-manuals.com publishes page by page for each E46 variant (325i Touring, M3 coupe), and from printouts and screenshots posted elsewhere.
  • WDS: BMW's Wiring Diagram System. A public mirror at wds.psjr.org has the E46 drawings, DME pin tables, connector views and component locations behind the manual's pin tables. It has no VIN filter, so pick each drawing by the models and build dates in its title. ISTA shows the diagrams for your exact VIN; BMW's official portal sold a one-day subscription for $32 in October 2026 (BMW AOS).
  • SGBD job documentation: a community transcription of BMW's job files, with every Tool32 job, status bit and fault number the manual uses: MSS54DS0 for the S54's DME, DSC_MK60, EWS3, KOMBI46R for the M3 cluster, LSZ_2 for the light module and IHKR46 for manual climate control.
  • Coding data and NCS Expert: BMW's E46 coding data (SP-Daten V32) on archive.org, the ncsx project's notes on its format, Revtor's NCS Dummy manual, the FSW/PSW parameter list, owners' E46 coding traces and a comparison of MK60 coding values read from real cars. BMW's retrofit instructions for xenon headlights with levelling and headlight washers show the wiring and coding.
  • ETK: BMW's parts catalog, mirrored by bmwfans.info and RealOEM. Check every number against your VIN.
  • Bentley: the E46 3 Series service manual from Bentley Publishers (site blocked our check; coverage of the M3 per a seller listing, unverified). One swapper found its wiring page didn't match his car (e46fanatics).
  • BMW training: ST041 E46 M3 complete vehicle, driveline (text), engine electronics part 2 and part 3, and running gear; the S54 engine module; ST055 MS S54, fuel management and emissions overview; ST034 E46 driver information and engine management; ST052 E46 driver information systems; ST054 climate control: engine cooling, A/C service, IHKA, IHKR and outputs; ST056 chassis dynamics: suspension and alignment, E46 DSC and level control; ST503 wheel alignment; ST040 bus troubleshooting, E46 IHKR and DSC, plus the E46 all-wheel-drive system and Bosch DSC III 5.7 (text); ST043 E46 update; ST051 EWS; ST034 E46 models (text); ST045 E85 driveline; ST601 E85 M Roadster (text); ST406 vehicle coding information.
  • BMW service bulletins: SI B11 04 04 (S54 rod bearings), SI B12 09 13 (DME VIN and state tests), SI B17 03 16 (cooling-system pressure test, written for a later model).
  • BMW owner's manuals and wheel lists: the 2004 US 325i Sports Wagon manual (manualsnet, archive.org), the 2003 US sedan manual, for the M54's capacities (archive.org), the US M3 manuals for 2002 (archive.org) and 2003 (coupe; convertible on manualsnet and archive.org), and BMW's wheel and tire lists for the MY2003 Touring (BMW) and the MY2005 M3 (BMW).
  • BMW USA spec sheets: weights, tracks, steering and final-drive ratios for the 2002 M3, 2003 M3, 2006 M3, 2002 325 models and 2003 325 models.

  • Subframe reinforcement: Garagistic K0536 instructions, CMP part 1 and part 2, CMP chassis rail plates, Turner PDF
  • Wiring and coding: Kassel Performance S54 swap wiring chart (X60004 moves for MS42, MS43 and MS45 cars; see Sources to treat with care), swap harnesses from Redline Motorsport and Race German (both need an EWS-deleted DME), Tulay's Wire Werks connector kits, Bali: installing BMW Standard Tools, ECUWorx: VIN and AIF with Tool32, ECUWorx M Track guide, NAM3 MSS54/MSS54HP DME information
  • DME services: Kassel Performance (EWS delete, VIN recode and swap-coding options), RPM Motorsport (EWS delete)
  • Body: Redish: E46 M3 rear arches and rust, M3Projekts shop, HARD Motorsport rear flares, EU prices for new M3 arch steel at eStore-Central, BMW's M3 dimension drawings via getoutlines (coupe, convertible), the E46 M3's bodywork widths in Motorsport Australia's recognition document, and I-CAR on BMW sectioning and steel GMA welding
  • Fluids: BimmerWorld pages for MTF-LT-2, SAF-XJ+FM and CHF 11S, DOT 4 low-viscosity brake fluid; MAHLE's refrigerant and oil fill quantities (a vendor handbook)
  • Welding and safety: Miller: MIG basics for automotive repair, OSHA fact sheet on welding fume, I-CAR on BMW's plug-weld rules and weld-through primer, I-CAR plug-weld sizes (2022), I-CAR practice welding guide (2023)
  • Parts catalog: bmwfans.info ETK, 325i Touring, M3 coupe, M3 convertible
  • Prices and fitment: BMWPartsDeal, a US BMW dealer's parts site, for the October 2026 US prices in this guide (trunk floor, convertible quarter); FCP Euro's fitment notes for BMW's springs by car (Touring front spring)
  • Law: EPA 2020 tampering policy, EPA A/C servicing rules, Nevada Engine Swap Fact Sheet, California BAR engine changes, BAR modified-software rule, 49 U.S.C. §32704, 49 CFR 580.17, EPA refrigerant sales restriction, 13 CCR 1968.2 (California's OBD rule, VIN from MY2005); Massachusetts: 540 CMR 4.04, the inspection program's site mavehiclecheck.com with its 540 CMR 4.00 copy and inspector Module 1 (2026)

Forum threads by topic

  • Wiring: S54 swap wiring information (its four-wire X60004-to-X6011 move describes an earlier M54 swap), battery and oil lamps, Kalim's S54 sedan swap, oil lamp with an MS45.1 ZHP, clutch-switch path, leak-test pinout on an MS43 wagon, switch-center plugs
  • Fuel: S54 swap California BAR certification (fuel-pump wiring and smog), fuel pressure info (Bentley's figures)
  • EWS: EWS sync for S54 swap into E46 Touring, can't sync EWS on an S54 wagon, MSS54 EWS delete, EWS sync solved (one hardware-converted CSL-clone MSS54 whose ISN had been written in by BDM; not a virgin or used US DME)
  • Engine tests: VANOS test with Tool32, DIS VANOS results, failed VANOS test
  • Cluster and DSC: DIY: M3 cluster into non-M, E46 M3 cluster coding, MK20 to MK60 swap, MK60 VIN issue on an M3 (the session production date), a non-M MK60's coding options (a 2002 318i, coding index C05, archived)
  • Body: M3 rear quarter replacements (on a 325Ci coupe), how the rear quarter attaches to the wheel well, coupe and convertible quarter differences, are coupe and convertible panels interchangeable?, 2M Touring fenders, Touring front-end conversion
  • Chassis: E46 M3 stock ride height, with TIS screenshots, NAM3 comprehensive steering thread, M3 rear swap completed, Touring subframe failure
  • Legal: S54 swaps and smog in California, chassis, DME and EWS VINs mismatched

Sources to treat with care

You'll meet these in forum threads. They come from another car or engine, or contain errors, so the guide doesn't rely on them:

  • Dr. VANOS Stage I sheet (PDF): the procedure for single-VANOS M50/M52/S52 engines, not the S54's double VANOS. Its tools and chain advice don't apply.
  • BMW "DSC III" training PDF (ge39.com): an E38/E39 Bosch DSC module. The E46 appears only in an overview table, which lists the M3 as MK20 only.
  • Z4 M (E85) material: the S54 valve train is the same, but disassembly differs (z4-forum valve DIY), and Pelican's S54 throttle-actuator article is written on a Z4 M (the actuator is the same S54 part).
  • Treats On The Streets subframe playlist (YouTube): all four videos are E36 M3.
  • Condor Speed Shop's plate kit (video description): fitment is "E46 coupe & sedan", with modification for the convertible; the Touring isn't listed.
  • FCP Euro's non-M clutch video (5S7-gNEgJoM): a Spec E46 race car with an aluminium flywheel and an E36 M3 clutch. Use FCP's M3 video, NmEOFBqreX8.
  • M5x Mechanix valve video (mTcIK8Ryc04): shows only a few valves and misstates the intake range once (11:08). Use FCP Euro's.
  • e46fanatics "330i to 325i rear subframe swap" (thread): non-M to non-M.
  • BimmerForums oil-pan clearance thread (thread): an E36 engine in an E46, unverified.
  • Kassel's S54 swap wiring chart (image): its MS45 removals match BMW's drawings, but it puts the oil-pressure lamp on cluster pin 14 (the K-bus; use 13), prints the brake wire BR/GN (it's BR/GR), and leaves out the clutch, the leak-test heater and some lamp moves. Use the manual.
  • The DME pinout workbook (pinout sheet): a forum member's transcription of BMW's tables. Its "MS45.1 X3ZHP" tab is a 3.0-litre table and its "MS45 903" tab the M56 layout, so neither describes a US 325i Touring's MS45.1.
  • bimmer-service "DME MSS54 (S54) pinout" (page): the Z3 M's table, not the E46's. It has a leak pump on pins 28 and 30, among other differences.
  • vTuned garage – M3 wagon quarter swap (2025) (YouTube): an F80 M3's quarters on an F31 328i wagon, not an E46. Its tail-light advice doesn't apply; on the E46 the rear seam stays well ahead of the tail-lamp.
  • candyshowroom – The M3 BMW never built (2026) (YouTube): calls Petroyle's arches carbon. BMWBlog says "The quarter panels stay in steel"; Petroyle's carbon panels are the front wings, sills, rear bumper and boot floor.

Appendix

Torque values

Use these with BMW's repair instructions (TIS). Where we could read a BMW document, the source says so: SI B11 04 04, BMW's E46 TIS (issue 12/2007, as workshop-manuals.com publishes it), a TIS screenshot and printouts. Most other values come from compilations of BMW data: the "Flow" E46 M3 torque PDF, a forum compilation built on RealOEM printouts and updated in February 2024 (Google Drive, via the NAM3 torque thread; page numbers are the PDF's), and Department 69, which cites TIS. Confirm compilation and video values in TIS for your parts. US units are in brackets. Each fastener has its own row, and these marks show what to watch:

  • New (Notes column): fit a new fastener, or the new seal it names, with BMW's part number where we have it. Reuse marks the one fastener BMW wants refitted in its own hole.
  • Conflict (Value column): the sources disagree. Both values are given, and the question is in Open questions to verify.
  • At ride height (Notes column): tighten that rubber-bushed joint with the suspension where it sits in BMW's "normal position", so the bushings aren't pre-twisted (Flow p.16). That's the height of the finished car on its wheels with the M3's normal-position load (a full tank, 68 kg in each front seat and 14 kg in the trunk; see Wheel alignment), or each hub jacked to that height (Targets for the mock-up and the bushed joints). At the front that's only the anti-roll-bar clamp nuts; the control-arm bushing brackets carry no ride-height condition in Flow or Department 69. Ball joints and plain brackets can be torqued in any position.
